News.title: Mystery stowaway found frozen to death in landing gear at Gatwick Airport
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

FLIGHT TRAGEDY Mystery stowaway found frozen to death in landing gear at Gatwick Airport

A MYSTERY stowaway was found frozen to death in the landing gear of a plane at Gatwick, an inquest heard.

The unnamed man was discovered in the wheel compartment of the Air Arabia plane from Morocco in June.

Horsham Coroner’s Court was told he suffered a fatal cardiac arrest, followed by hypoxia and hypothermia.

West Sussex Brighton and Hove Area Coroner Joseph Turner said inside the wheel compartment would have been extremely cold and there would have been a lack of oxygen.





He formally opened the inquest on the basis he had “reason to believe this death was unnatural”.

The hearing was told the man is yet to be identified as inquiries continue to establish his name.

He was found by a ground engineer at Gatwick, who spotted a packing strap hanging out of the wheel compartment.

The Air Arabia Airbus A320 has flown from Tangier on June 16.

Mr Turner adjourned the full inquest until February 4, 2027.

At the time of the horror, a Gatwick spokesperson said: “London Gatwick’s emergency services attended an Air Arabia aircraft just after 11.30am on Tuesday June 16 2026 when an incident was identified upon arrival.

“As Sussex Police have confirmed, a body was found. Our teams subsequently supported Sussex Police and the coroner.

“Our thoughts are with everyone affected.”

News.title: ‘Much-loved’ NHS worker, 28, dies in early morning house fire just months before qualifying as paramedic
News.content:
TRAGIC LOSS ‘Much-loved’ NHS worker, 28, dies in early morning house fire just months before qualifying as paramedic

AN NHS worker tragically died in a house fire just months before she was due to qualify as a paramedic.

Jess McKee, 28, was in a house that went up in flames on Saturday morning.

Four others managed to escape without injury after the blaze in Thetford, Norfolk.

Jess was an Emergency Medical Technician based in Suffolk who was due to qualify as a paramedic in January.





Tributes have flooded in for the “much-loved” worker with a “bright future”.

The East of England Ambulance Service said on Facebook: “It is with great sadness that we confirm the death of Jess McKee on Saturday.

“Jess was an Emergency Medical Technician based in Suffolk, and was set to graduate as a qualified paramedic in January.”

Chief Executive Neill Moloney added: “On behalf of everyone at EEAST, I would like to extend our heartfelt condolences to Jess’s family, friends and loved ones. Our thoughts are with them at this incredibly difficult time.

“Jess was a much-loved colleague, known for her kindness, professionalism and dedication to patient care.

“She had a bright future ahead of her and was just a few months away from achieving her ambition of becoming a paramedic, which makes this loss all the more tragic.

“Jess’s death has deeply affected colleagues across our organisation, and we are continuing to support those impacted.

“We would ask that the privacy of Jess’s family, friends and colleagues is respected at this difficult time.”



A spokeswoman for Norfolk Constabulary said: “Officers were called to Sycamore Covert by Norfolk Fire and Rescue Service who were dealing with a house fire.

“Sadly the body of a woman was found inside the address and she was pronounced dead at the scene.

“A cordon that was in place while officers and fire investigators worked to determine the full circumstances of the fire has since been lifted.

“The death is currently being treated as unexplained but is not believed to be suspicious.”

News.title: ‘Beloved’ woman, 23, found dead in luxury London flat is pictured as family pay tribute – after 4 women & 2 men arrested
News.content:
MURDER PROBE ‘Beloved’ woman, 23, found dead in luxury London flat is pictured as family pay tribute – after 4 women & 2 men arrested

A “BELOVED” 23-year-old woman who was found dead in a luxury London flat has been identified, as her heartbroken family pay tribute.

A murder probe was launched after police were called to an address in Islington, London, on Thursday, August 6, amid reports of a concern for welfare.

Tragically, 23-year-old Clara Bale was pronounced dead at the scene despite the best efforts of medics.

Officers arrested four women, aged 20, 21, 23 and 26, and two men, aged 21 and 24 at the scene on suspicion of murder.





They have all since been released on bail while the probe into the alleged murder continues.

In a tribute, Clara’s family said: “Clara was a brilliant young woman filled with dreams, a bright light whose loss has left an immeasurable void in our lives.

“She embodied hope, resilience and love. Her inspiring aura was felt in every room she entered and in every space she had yet to step into. A beloved friend, daughter and sister who cherished life above all else.

“Our hearts bleed with grief following her loss.



“We will forever miss her smile, her presence and her humanity.”

A security guard confirmed the incident happened inside Valencia Tower in Islington, North London.

He said: “There were lots of ambulances and police here, but it all happened inside here. That’s all I know.”

Two bedroom two bathroom flats in the luxury block cost almost £5,000 per month to rent.



Forensics vans could be seen on City Road next to the development for days after the tragedy and detectives could be seen coming in and out of the building.

Detective Chief Inspector Paul Waller, who is leading the investigation, said: “Our thoughts remain with Clara’s family and loved ones following her tragic death.

“The police investigation is ongoing and we are making good progress in establishing the events leading up to Clara’s death, including speaking to a number of witnesses.

“I would continue to urge anyone with information, no matter how minor it may seem, to come forward and speak with officers.

“Every piece of information helps with our investigation.”

News.title: Horror moment ‘wolf’ attacks mum & daughter, 12, in Italy as man desperately hurls chair at beast to fend it off
News.content:
THIS is the horror moment a suspected wolf charged at a man as it attacked a mum and daughter at a holiday resort.

Shocking footage shows a man desperately hurling a chair at the predator to fend it off.



He first attempts to punch the animal, sending it running.

The beast attacked a holidaymaker mum, 52, and her daughter, 12, in the coastal town of Gallipoli, southern Italy on Thursday.



It also launched itself at the 47-year-old man staying in the same hotel.

Another clip shows the suspected wolf prowling the streets of the holiday town moments before it attacks.

Two German tourists can be seen fleeing the animal as it charges at them.

They try to warn others of its danger.



Eventually the man chucks a chair at the predator, sending it scurrying away.

Authorities are investigating whether the aggressive animal was a wolf or a wild dog.

Domenico Capriello told France Info that he was bitten in the attack.



He said at first he didn’t think it was a wolf and started punching the beast.

Domenico witnessed the beast biting the child and chucked a chair to scare it off.

All three victims of the animal attack were treated in hospital for their injuries but have now been discharged.

The area is being closely watched for the beast, with the Forestry Carabinieri on high alert.

Italy is thought to be home to around 3,300 wolves after conservation efforts brought the beasts back from the brink of extinction in the 70s.



Further north in Bari, Puglia, a hunt is underway for an animal that attacked three children earlier this month, then went on to seriously maim two people in Noicattaro.

Parks were shut as authorities scoured the area for the beast, deploying drones, thermal imaging cameras and snares.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Veterinary Professor Antonio Camarda said the animal was showing “abnormal behaviour” “compared to the normal behaviour of a wolf”.

He said a wolf normally “does not attack humans, because humans are not prey” but that “from the information we have, morphologically it is a wolf”.

News.title: Man dies and woman fighting for life after horror multi-car crash during pursuit involving police vehicle and Audi
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

SMASH TRAGEDY Man dies and woman fighting for life after horror multi-car crash during pursuit involving police vehicle and Audi

A MAN has died and a woman is in a critical condition after a horror multi-car crash involving a police vehicle and Audi.

Tragedy struck following a pursuit on the A439 near Stratford, Warwickshire, yesterday afternoon.

Officers had initially attempted to halt the black Audi on the Birmingham Road at around 5.20pm.

But the driver refused to stop and drove off towards the A46, before travelling back towards Stratford on the A439.





Warwickshire Police said: “A man has died and a woman is critically injured after a pursuit involving a police vehicle and a car near Stratford.

“At around 5.23pm on Monday (24 August) officers attempted to stop a vehicle on Birmingham Road.

“The driver of the car – a black Audi – failed to stop and made off in the direction of the A46 before travelling back towards Stratford on the A439 Warwick Road.

“At approximately 5.44pm, the car driver is understood to have been in collision with another vehicle – a white Ford Puma.

“The male driver of the Audi was sadly pronounced deceased at the scene by paramedics.

“The Ford driver was taken to hospital where she remains at this time in a critical condition.

“Their families have been informed and are being offered specialist support. A number of other vehicles were damaged during the pursuit.”

News.title: Man charged with murder after woman, 31, plunged to her death from building in London
News.content:
FALL HORROR Man charged with murder after woman, 31, plunged to her death from building in London

A MAN has been charged with murder after a woman fell to her death from a building in London.

Emergency crews were scrambled to the horror in Old Kent Road, South East London, at around 2.50pm on Friday.

Tragically, Kerry Ann Goodbrand, 31, could not be saved and was declared dead at the scene.

Mohammed Sherif, 54, has now been charged with murder and is due to appear at Croydon Magistrates’ Court today.





The Met Police said officers were called to reports that a woman had fallen from a height.

The force confirmed Kerry’s next-of-kin have been informed and are being supported by specialist officers.

Detective Chief Superintendent Emma Bond, who leads policing in the area, said: “Our thoughts are with the woman’s family and loved ones at this incredibly difficult time.

“Officers are working diligently to establish the full circumstances surrounding her death and members of the community will see an increased police presence in the area while enquiries are conducted locally.



“If you have any concerns, or any information which may be able to assist, please speak to an officer or contact us.”

Anyone with information can call police on 101, quoting CAD 4316/21AUG26, or contact Crimestoppers anonymously on 0800 555 111.

News.title: Andrew & Tristan Tate admit their glam lifestyle is FAKE in humiliating court confession revealing supercars are rented
News.content:
ANDREW and Tristan Tate have been forced to admit their glam lifestyle which attracted millions of impressionable young fans is actually fake.

The brothers gave a humiliating court confession revealing their luxury trove of supercars is all rented as they remain behind bars over sex charges.



Andrew, 39, and Tristan, 38, gained a cult following, promoting a life of cash, swanky cars and attractive women online.

Disgraced Andrew would even refer to himself as the “Top G” as he proudly flaunted his “king of toxic masculinity” moniker across social media.



But new court filings have revealed the siblings are trying to escape extradition to the UK over a slew of sex crime allegations by claiming their life of luxury is all just for show.

The pair’s lawyers say federal authorities have been fooled by deliberately “outrageous” social media claims made by the brothers, according to the Daily Mail.

Both brothers would regularly film themselves inspecting their fleet of Bugatti and Aston Martin cars in their Romania bunker’s driveway.

But court documents claim all the cars seen on social media videos were actually rented to create the impression the pair are “uber-wealthy”.



Their lawyers said: “The more hyperbolic and outlandish the post, the more likely it will generate views and likes.

“Which in turn generates income. In short, they are playing a role.”

The docs claim that Tristan’s car collection – made up of a £1.5million Aston Martin and £3.6million and £5.1million Bugattis – has never been owned by him.



And a £36million superyacht the siblings would often film videos on board was simply owned by someone who paid them to promote the vessel due to their large following.

Their representatives declined to comment when contacted by The Sun.

The outlandish new claims come as the Tates remain locked up in a Miami jail, where they have been since their July 18 arrest.



Despite denying all charges against them, judges fear they could flee the US if allowed to be released on bond.

Authorities have cited their vast wealth as a key concern should the pair be allowed to walk before a trial or extradition.

The US government has even suggested the superyacht could be used to take the brothers into international waters and help them disappear.

This theory was fuelled last month, when several passports under different aliases were seized by cops searching the pair’s homes.

One passport for Tristan was under the name “Vladimir Scorpius” – the eponymous villain of the James Bond spy novel “Scorpius”, court documents showed.



Tristan’s lawyers claim the passport isn’t real and was only made of cardboard as part of a Halloween costume.

Their lawyers reportedly presented various social media posts in the latest obtained court filings to prove they were boasts rather than facts.

One included a public message from Andrew where he claimed to generate nine figures from his X posts.



Other posts from the pair in the past have suggested the Tates have unlimited crypto, Bitcoin and cash.

“All of these posts are hyperbole,” the filing says.

It is in their best interest to portray themselves as wealthy due to their careers, the docs add.

Andrew and Tristan have been locked up since their arrest at a bare-knuckle boxing event in Miami in mid-July.

They have been charged with rape, sex trafficking and a host of other offences related to indecent images of a child and extreme pornography.



They are being held in Florida’s Miami Federal Detention Center, where their lawyers claim they are suffering in the harsh conditions.

Self-described misogynist Andrew called his Special Housing Unit (SHU) “punitive housing for people who murder their cellmates”.

The dual US-UK citizen claimed he had been forced to drink unclean water that made him sick.

His only water source is a shower and a “brown and filthy faucet” which has left him suffering “persistent stomach problems”, he claims.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The jail has faced cooling and water problems and a clash between inmates and staff in recent months, according to the US Bureau of Prisons.



Andrew also claimed to have been woken up in the middle of the night by other prisoners yelling death threats as well as hearing a “demonic roar” from a neighbouring cell.

News.title: Reckless teens kill couple in horror crash after stealing SUV & speeding down wrong side of road during police chase
News.content:
A CREW of four teens have allegedly killed a couple as they smashed into a stolen car while driving the wrong way down the road in a dramatic police chase.

The teens are accused of slamming a £160k SUV into another car after trying to escape cops in an hours-long chase.



The New Jersey youths allegedly swiped the Mercedes-Benz G Wagon on Saturday morning.

They went on to crash head-on into a sedan containing Robert Barr Jr., 54, and Alice Stilwell, 67, sending their car flying and killing them both, according to prosecutors.



The alleged joyriders were first spotted by police in Longport at 3.42am, who tried to pull the vehicle over.

But the teens sped off over the JFK Memorial Bridge, cops said, pulling them into a high-stakes chase.

Police then tracked down the car’s owner – who was yet to even realise the luxury SUV had been taken – and told officers across the county to be on the lookout for it.

Cops said they found the Mercedes four hours later at 7.46am in Hamilton Township with a Land Rover.

Both cars allegedly fled the area.



Police gave chase to the Mercedes, but eventually lost sight of it.

Just six minutes later, the teens were allegedly speeding on the wrong side of the road when they slammed into the couple’s car.

Robert and Alice were sent careening into a petrol station by the impact.

Prosecutors said they were both killed in the crash.



Officers found the wreck seconds later and arrested four people who had allegedly tried to flee the Mercedes on foot.

The four, three juveniles and one adult, were largely unscathed after the crash, authorities said.

Nayshaun Brown, 18, and three other teens who were not named because of their ages, were charged with joyriding, conspiracy to commit aggravated assault and eluding police.

Prosecutors did not reveal who was driving at the time of the accident.

Alice was a “beloved mother and grandmother”, and Robert her long term partner, a GoFundMe revealed.



Friend of the family Nicole Wright called their deaths a “devastating loss” on the fundraising appeal.

She wrote: “This unimaginable tragedy has left their family in deep grief, and the shock of how suddenly it happened has made this painful time even harder to bear.

“Her daughters and their families are now doing their best to honor their mother (grandmother) while carrying the emotional and practical burdens that come with such a devastating loss.”

She added: “Every contribution, no matter the size, will help ease some of the weight this family is carrying and show them they are not alone as they honor their mother’s memory.”

News.title: More than 70,000 social and affordable homes to be built across England over 10 years
News.content:
Ministers have announced where more than 70,000 social and affordable homes will be built in England over the next 10 years as part of an initial allocation of almost Â£10bn, in a bid to address the housing crisis.

Funding has been granted to Greater Manchester, the West Midlands, West Yorkshire, South Yorkshire, North East England, and Liverpool. An additional Â£6bn was previously announced for London.

It is the first part of a wider plan to build 300,000 social and affordable homes across the nation, under the government's Â£39bn social housebuilding programme.

Earlier this year, before he became prime minister, Andy Burnham had called for the entire 10-year Â£39bn affordable housing budget for England to be spent on homes for social rent - which means the cost of the unit is about half that of market rents, and there are strict criteria for who can apply for it.

"I would actually devote all of it to social housing," Burnham told The Social Housing Podcast in May.

But of the new homes announced on Monday, 60% would be for social rent.

Housing minister Matthew Pennycook told BBC Breakfast he did not accept Burnham had failed to meet his previous commitment, saying the government had taken a "pragmatic approach" and wants to "get money out the door".

He said the next tranche of funding would be more focused on council houses - which are usually also classed as homes for social rent.

It is understood ministers decided against giving councils more of the funding announced in the first tranche because they did not believe councils would be in a position to build the required number of social homes.

News.title: Beyond China's humanoid robots, a quieter machine revolution is unfolding
News.content:
"I take a nap and the world changes," says Chen Tianyu.

His world certainly does. The 28-year-old keeps up with the latest technology by spending his spare time in factories that are switching to automation. That way he knows what to prioritise when teaching his class about artificial intelligence (AI) and robotics.

In front of him, around 30 college students are studying code. One of them is typing furiously as his eyes dart from the screen to the robot: "The idea is it will grab that cylindrical piece and move it over there."

A line of industrial robots are waiting to be programmed, and in another part of the classroom, students are trying to develop robotic medical instruments. As he guides them, Chen declares: "If you are not needed by the world of AI and robotics, then you'll definitely be among those eliminated".

For the people in this room, this is a step - or rather a leap - towards a future that China is meticulously building: Xi Jinping's $20bn (Â£14.7bn) plan to put his country at the forefront of innovation and in direct competition with the US.

The evidence is all around them. They are in the Hangzhou Technician Institute, one of several huge, purpose-built vocational schools that want to churn out the next generation of tech-savvy engineers. The campus sits on the outskirts of Hangzhou, a former imperial capital whose futuristic skyline is just the first hint of its role as a global tech hub.

Across the country, there are more than two million robots working in China's factories - which is more than anywhere else - and they are continuing to scale up at extraordinary speed.

News.title: The grieving family who say the coroners' courts aren't working
News.content:
Sarah thought she knew what she was getting into when she attended a coroner's court in May 2024 to discuss the death of her second cousin.

Her day job as a murder detective meant she was used to courts, to judges, to legal argument. What she wasn't prepared for was a coroner's court. "I felt like I was on trial," she recalls of her first hearing, in Woking, Surrey. "I remember just feeling completely railroadedâ¦ It [was] far more hostile than I had ever expected."

Her cousin, Daniel Lindsay, died in 2023, aged 41. He had lived at a home in Surrey that specialises in caring for people with learning disabilities. Daniel also had Down's syndrome and type 1 diabetes.

As his death was unexpected, his case was referred to the coroner for an inquest.

What followed was one of the most stressful experiences of Sarah's life. She discovered new details about how her cousin lived, and his cause of death. The family initially thought Daniel died from a heart attack - but over the course of the inquest, they learnt that was wrong. She had expected the process to be emotional; what she didn't predict was just how complex and frustrating it would be, at times leaving her tearful and furious.

Coroners examine deaths that are not straightforward, like unexpected or violent deaths, or those that take place in state custody. Every year, thousands of British families rely on these courts for crucial answers. For many, an inquest provides the key interaction with the arms of the state at a time of trauma.

News.title: Organised crime arrests as police investigate A66 crash that killed two officers
News.content:
Twelve people have been arrested as part of the investigation into the A66 crash that killed seven people, including two police officers.

Nine men and three women, aged between 19 and 61, have been arrested across Teesside on suspicion of a range of offences including possession of a firearm and being part of an organised crime group. One has since been charged.

In the early hours of Saturday, a Volkswagen Passat that had been pursued by police travelled the wrong way down the A66 near Middlesbrough and crashed into an oncoming police car - two PCs and all five Passat occupants died.

Cleveland Police said it was investigating "serious criminal activity that resulted in this fatal incident".

PC Tom Clough, 38, and PC Matthew Blades, 37, died in the crash, as did Michael Robert Cahill, 23, Jacob Matusiak, 23, Makai Saddington, 18, Theo Rae, 17, and 17-year-old Cole Robert Worthy.

Earlier, Cleveland Police released more details of its investigation into the lead-up to the crash and information about the 12 people it had arrested.

The force said:

It received several reports of two vehicles "being driven dangerously" on Saturday morning

The first vehicle, believed to be a Volvo XC60, was seen "ramming properties" in the Middlesbrough area

The second vehicle, a Passat, is believed to have been associated with this activity

Both vehicles were operating with cloned number plates but were picked up by automated number plate recognition technology

The Volvo has been recovered in Middlesbrough

Four of the five people in the Passat had previous convictions

Assistant Chief Constable Wayne Fox said the investigation had been "fast moving and complex".

He said: "The events of that tragic night will have a lasting and profound impact on the Cleveland area and the communities we seek to protect.

"We have a duty to respond to, and thoroughly investigate, the serious criminal activity that resulted in this fatal incident and to bring all those responsible to justice."

News.title: Millions of women who have missed cervical screening in England to be offered HPV home-testing kits
News.content:
Dr Sue Mann, national clinical director for women's health, said: "Offering millions of women an alternative test they can do from the comfort of their own homes will be a game-changer â making it easier than ever for them to get tested.

"There are lots of reasons that may stop women from getting their cervical screening â embarrassment, lack of time or worries about discomfort â and these kits provide a discreet and convenient option we hope will encourage more women to take up the life-saving test."

Health Secretary Yvette Cooper added: "Cervical cancer is preventable - but that's why we want to make it as easy and convenient as possible for women to keep up with their screening."

The kits contain a swab, similar to a long cotton, bud which is used to collect a sample from the vagina.

It is then sent back to the NHS and if high-risk HPV is found, individuals will be invited to book a follow-up cervical screening appointment.

High-risk HPV increases the risk of cervical cancer, but it does not mean a woman will automatically develop it.

Trials of the self-testing in London suggest it could lead to one in 10 women to come forward for screening â boosting uptake by around 400,000 a year.

Other parts of the UK are also looking at introducing self-testing.

Women aged 24 to 64 are invited for cervical screening every five years â or more frequently if HPV is detected.

Through a combination of HPV vaccination, which is offered to teenagers, and improved screening, the NHS is hoping to eliminate cervical cancer by 2040.

The NHS says cervical screening appointments with a clinician is still the best way to prevent cancer â and even if you have missed an appointment you can still come forward for one.

News.title: Burnham refuses to rule out tax rises in autumn Budget
News.content:
Andy Burnham has refused to rule out tax rises in the upcoming autumn Budget, saying he "won't be unrealistic" about the "challenging" state of public finances.

The prime minister said he would take a "careful approach" to the economy, and defended his previously announced cost of living pledges as funded spending commitments.

Burnham became prime minister in July promising to give people breathing space and help with the cost of living, but questions remain over how major policies such as social care reforms will be funded.

Experts have previously warned that he and Chancellor John Healey will have little financial room to manoeuvre in their first Budget on 28 October.

Speaking during his first visit to Ukraine, Burnham said the policies announced so far including capping bus fares at Â£2 and cutting VAT on household electricity bills were "the first steps that I've felt able to make", and were doable because he was able to reprioritise funding from elsewhere.

"I took the decision early on that digital ID wasn't the top priority for now. And so we've reprioritised funding to other priorities," he said in an interview with ITV.

Asked if the public needed to accept some of the new policies would have to be paid for in tax rises, Burnham said they wouldn't necessarily have to accept that.

Pushed on whether he would need to raise taxes to cover spending gaps, he said: "I will always take a careful approach to things. I ran Greater Manchester for 10 years and we ran a very tight ship with rock solid finances.

"Nothing will change as I come into this role as prime minister. I won't take risks with people's jobs or their livelihoods or their family finances.

"I will try to help them in whatever way I can, I have already done some things that will help them."

Burnham previously told the BBC he accepts his earlier announcements aimed at tackling the cost of living are not enough on their own and hinted at further support.

Speaking during his first official overseas visit on Monday, he said while he would do what he could, "I won't be unrealistic and people really need to understand that.

"We are in a challenging position, whatever I do will be carefully thought through, it will be funded and there will be more to come as we go into the autumn."

Last week official figures showed the the government borrowed more than expected in July, despite a record month for income tax receipts.

Inflation also reached a four-month high of 2.9% in July and is expected to rise further due to the ongoing impact of the Iran war, which has hit energy prices and fuel costs.

Experts have warned Burnham and Healey that they need to either raise taxes or cut spending elsewhere as pressure on the public finances has left no room for extra borrowing.

Both the prime minister and chancellor have vowed to stick to the fiscal rules set by former chancellor Rachel Reeves.

The rules are designed to ensure day-to-day spending is funded through tax revenue by the end of the Parliament, and to reduce debt as a proportion of GDP.

Rain Newton-Smith, the chief executive of the Confederation of British Industry, said business owners wanted to create opportunities for young people but "the cost of employing people has gone up so much".

"The business leaders I speak to say that the cost of doing business has gone up so much that it's holding them back from creating opportunities," she told the Today programme.

She said targeted support for businesses would create "more growth and more opportunities that saves money for the government and ultimately leads to higher tax receipts".

News.title: Russian stadium says it won't host Kanye West gigs
News.content:
The Russian stadium that was scheduled to host two shows by Ye, the rapper also known as Kanye West, has said the events will no longer take place.

In a social media post, external, St Petersburg's Gazprom Arena said no rental agreement had been signed with the concert promoters. "Accordingly, the concert cannot take place on our site."

West would have been the first major Western performer to play Russia since it invaded Ukraine in 2022. The rapper is trying to rehabilitate his image after years of antisemitic remarks, for which he recently apologised.

Gazprom Arena acknowledged it had received complaints about West's planned appearance and stressed that it "was not and is not" responsible for his booking.

The stadium said in its statement that the sold-out concerts, scheduled for 10 and 11 October, had been organised by the Moscow-based Say Agency.

Posting on its Telegram channel, Say Agency said the stadium's announcement had come as a surprise.

"We learned about [it] at the same time as you did, through the media," the agency wrote. "As of now, the Ye concert has not been canceled," it added in a follow-up message.

"We are trying to contact the venue to find out the reason for the post and resolve the issue. We will keep you updated."

The BBC has contacted West's publicist for a comment on the uncertainty over his Russian shows.

In its statement, Say Agency said it announced the concerts earlier this month based "on an official letter that was approved by" Gazprom Arena.

The stadium subsequently sent a rental agreement, Say Agency claimed, and the agency acknowledged the contract had not yet been signed but said the deadline to do so did not expire until later this week.

Last week, Gazprom Arena had posted enthusiastically about the concerts on social media, calling Ye "the most influential musical artist of our time".

Fans reacted to its latest announcement with disappointment.

"This was the shortest concert of my life," responded one, under Say Agency's Telegram post. "It's a shame that the government is putting obstacles in your way," added another.

There is no indication that authorities intervened in the shows, but there has been opposition to West's booking from some Russian politicians.

Vitaly Milonov, a notorious conservative lawmaker, suggested the star should perform traditional Russian songs instead of his planned setlist, reflecting the anti-Western views of many nationalists.

"Maybe after this he'll stop his disgusting antics and become a normal person," Milonov added in a video statement.

News.title: Sir Chris Hoy: Campaigning for cancer screening should not be down to me
News.content:
Sir Chris Hoy believes the onus to encourage men to get tested for prostate cancer should not just be on high-profile individuals like him.

Hoy told BBC Scotland he felt privileged to have the public platform to spread awareness and would continue to do so even if there was a national screening system in place.

But he said: "It shouldn't just be down to high-profile individuals like Jeremy Clarkson or myself or any number of men who've been in a similar situation.

"There should be a more systematic and proactive approach to let men know about their own risk."

Sir Chris was diagnosed with stage 4 prostate cancer when was 47. He turned 50 in March.

News.title: Legendary rugby league winger Boston dies aged 92
News.content:
Rugby league legend Sir Billy Boston has died aged 92.

Last year, he became the first player in rugby league's 130-year history to receive a knighthood.

Born in Cardiff in 1934, Boston grew up playing union but - overlooked by his home club - came to the attention of rugby league scouts while on national service in the north of England, signing for Wigan in 1953 as a 19-year-old.

Despite having played just a handful of games in league, the young winger's talent was quickly evident and Boston was picked for the 1954 Great Britain side that went to Australia and New Zealand - becoming the first black British player to tour down under.

He reached the 100-try milestone in just 68 matches after his switch from union.

Boston's scoring ratio is extraordinary, claiming 478 tries in 488 games for Wigan and helping them win three Challenge Cups and the Championship.

News.title: New 10p coin enters circulation - will you spot one?
News.content:
Something new might appear in your change when you pay in cash from now on: a 10p coin featuring the portrait of King Charles and the world's largest grouse.

Sufficient demand for the coins mean newly-minted 10p pieces are entering circulation for the first time for about four years, this time with a new design.

The Royal Mint says shoppers and collectors should discover the coins, which were minted and dated in 2023 and 2026, across the country.

The reverse side of the coin depicts an image of the capercaillie which is found in a small part of Scotland and threatened with extinction.

The redesigned suite of coins to celebrate the King's love of the natural world were unveiled in October 2023 by The Royal Mint.

The tails side of every newly-minted coin from the 1p to the Â£2 now features the country's flora and fauna - from bees to an oak tree leaf.

Coins in circulation in the UK carrying the portrait of King Charles have so far been limited to the 5p, 50p and Â£1.

Old coins with the image of the late Queen Elizabeth II can still be used, so the new coins are only struck in response to demand.

That is why, with 1.4 billion 10p coins in circulation, there has been no need for the new 10p to be released until now by The Royal Mint.

Now. 600,000 of these coins, dated 2023, and 6.5 million dated 2026 have been released to banks and post offices nationwide.

However, King Charles III coins still only represent about 1% of the 24.1 billion coins in circulation across the UK, making any new ones highly sought after by seasoned numismatists and new coin collectors.

News.title: Letting agent accused of not returning deposits to more than 100 tenants
News.content:
Raman Kaur and her family rented a house through Morgan, Payne & Knightly (MPK) until September 2025 when they bought their own home.

They are still waiting for their Â£900 deposit to be returned and have discovered the money was not put in a registered deposit scheme.

"It's not right, he shouldn't be doing that with our money," she said. "That's our sweat, our hard work.

"It's very stressful having a young family and with the financial crisis that we're all going through.

"We've saved that money, we've budgeted and we've had to tell the kids they can't have things.

"I think he should be ashamed of what he's done. It's not his money, he didn't earn it."

Kaur says the family visited the West Bromwich branch of MPK to resolve the matter, but found it had closed, leaving them to try phoning Singh and his staff every day.

The home the family rented is owned by an individual who did not want to be named in this article. We will refer to him as Vikram.

"I'm owed Â£700 and MPK are falsely saying they're registered in a deposit protection scheme, but they're not," he said.

"I've spent months trying to get hold of Tony Singh but the offices have shut down, and nobody answers the phone or emails.

"It feels like nobody can help us, so we contacted the BBC."

Our investigation has since found that individual sums that are owed range from Â£700 to Â£16,000.

Vikram reported his experience to Trading Standards.

Sandwell Council, which covers West Bromwich, said both Singh and MPK were no longer operating in the borough.

Singh and MPK continue, however, to operate elsewhere in the West Midlands, the BBC can confirm.

News.title: Briton fighting for Russia killed in Ukraine
News.content:
A British national has been killed in Ukraine while fighting for Russia.

Bradley Townsend is said to have died following an attack by a remote-controlled FPV drone in Ukraine's eastern Donetsk region. His death, on 10 June, is believed to be the first of a British citizen fighting for Russia in the conflict.

The 33-year-old left his home in Barnsley, South Yorkshire, earlier this year after telling his family he was going to Romania, according to the Yorkshire Post, external.

The Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO) confirmed it was aware of reports a British national had died in Ukraine, adding it was in contact with his family.

The news emerged as Andy Burnham arrived in Kyiv for his first foreign trip as UK prime minister.

The visit coincides with the 35th anniversary of the country's independence from the Soviet Union.

The government has agreed to hand over blueprints for British-made components for the Scalp missile, a French version of the UK's Storm Shadow cruise missile - allowing Ukraine to produce the weapon domestically.

News.title: Boy, 16, arrested after four viable devices found in security alert
News.content:
A 16-year-old boy has been arrested under the Terrorism Act after a security alert in Omagh, County Tyrone.

Police carried out a planned search on Monday at an address in the Gardenville Avenue.

Police said four viable explosive devices were found and removed from the property for forensic examination.

Nearby residents who had been asked to leave their homes during the alert have since returned.

Det Insp Winters urged the public not to speculate about the incident.

"It's important to stress that, while the suspect has been arrested under the Terrorism Act, our investigation to establish a motive remains very much ongoing."

News.title: Man charged with murder after house fire
News.content:
A man has been charged with murder, attempted murder and arson following a fire in west London that left a woman dead and eight others in need of hospital treatment.

Pawel Kulpa, 34, faces one count of murder, eight counts of attempted murder and one count of arson with intent to endanger life.

The charges come after a fire at a residential address on Berkeley Avenue, Hounslow, at about 01:15 BST on Wednesday, 19 August.

A 50-year-old woman, named by the Met Police as Anna Kowalska, died in hospital while another woman, 40, remains in hospital in a life-threatening condition. Kulpa is due to appear at Willesden Magistrates' Court on Tuesday.

News.title: Prince Harry steps down from African wildlife charity board
News.content:
The Duke of Sussex has stepped down from the board of an African wildlife charity whose rangers had been found to have committed human rights abuses against indigenous people.

A spokesman for Prince Harry confirmed he was stepping down after being president for the charity, African Parks, for six years before becoming a member of its board of directors in 2023, but said he remains a "supporter of its mission".

Last year the organisation admitted human rights abuses were committed by its rangers in Congo-Brazzaville.

Prince Harry's resignation comes shortly after it was announced he was relocating with the Duchess of Sussex, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet from California to the UK.

Prince Harry's spokesman said "the Duke is proud of his 10 years with African Parks and fully supports the ongoing strengthening of its board.

"His commitment to conservation in Africa continues, and he remains a supporter of African Parks' mission."

African Parks manages around 20 national parks and protected areas across 12 countries.

It was subject to an independent human rights investigation into allegations guards managed and paid by the charity had beaten, raped and tortured indigenous people in the Odzala-Kokoua National Park.

The charity said in 2025 it had improved its safeguarding processes both in the Odzala-Kokoua National Park and institutionally.

Announcing a "governance refresh of its board of directors", the charity thanked Prince Harry for his association, saying he had "brought global attention to the urgent need for biodiversity protection for the benefit of people and wildlife, and has contributed greatly to promoting philanthropy for the cause of conservation in Africa".

It added: "The duke remains deeply committed to this cause, and remains a strong supporter of African Parks' work."

The charity's website says Prince Harry served as part of the expert team that helped implement the first phase of the 500 Elephants project, which was "one of the largest and most significant elephant translocations in conservation history".

It saw wildlife experts move elephants from a park in Malawi to help increase population in areas where they have been heavily poached.

Prince Harry has said helping move elephants to safer homes was an "amazing" experience.

The Sussexes are back in the spotlight after the revelation last week they were returning to the UK this month after enrolling their children to start at a British school in September.

No change is expected to the official status of Prince Harry and Meghan and they will remain as private individuals.

Their pending return to the UK has raised questions on their security arrangements.

Last year, Prince Harry lost a legal challenge over the levels of security he and his family are entitled to while in the UK.

It is unclear what provisions will be made for their security once they return to the UK.

The couple's plans while they are in the UK are also unclear.

The BBC learned the Duchess of Sussex was in talks to return to acting with a role in Netflix series The Gentlemen, which would be her first significant acting role since her marriage to Prince Harry.

In early 2020, the Sussexes left the UK and stepped back from their royal duties before settling in California in March that year.

News.title: Snooker champion Graeme Dott guilty of child sex abuse
News.content:
Former world snooker champion Graeme Dott has been found guilty of child sexual abuse.

The 49-year-old denied two charges of lewd and libidinous behaviour towards a girl and a boy between 1993 and 2010.

During a trial, the High Court in Glasgow heard that Dott had exposed himself and inappropriately touched a primary school girl in the 1990s and attacked a young boy between 2006 and 2010.

Lord Harrower told Dott, who won the World Snooker Championship in 2006, he would be sentenced at a separate hearing in Edinburgh on 29 September.

Dott, from Glasgow, covered his face with his hands and shook his head while the verdict was delivered by jurors following a five-day trial.

He previously called the allegations made against him "disgusting".

Take That star Gary Barlow has stated his love for wine leaves him feeling as “passionate” as his music, as he returns to the vineyards for a new TV series.

The singer, aged 55, who has hosted several food and travel television programmes in recent years, embarked on his latest "epic adventure" across New Zealand alongside comedian Jason Manford.

During Gary Barlow’s Food And Wine Tour: New Zealand, the pair taste local fare while visiting chefs, winemakers, producers and communities, uncovering how gastronomy connects people, personal stories and the natural world.

Speaking in an interview with the Press Association, Barlow explained the inspiration behind his enthusiasm for travelling across the globe to seek out these novel experiences.

He said: “First and foremost, these shows for me are about the wine, and the food is obviously a pairing with that. Anything that’s homegrown is what attracts me.

“I guess my attraction with wine is the same reason I’m into music. Wine is like a passion. Whenever you go to these vineyards, they’re not there for the money. They can’t be, because it’s very difficult to make money.”

He added: “They’re there because they love it. It’s a passion. It’s the way that music has been for me – that’s what’s always drawn me to wine.”

open image in gallery Gary Barlow’s new ITV show explores the food and wine scene in Australia ( ITV )

“When I’m doing any of these trips to watch and listen to people who are passionate about what they do, I just love that,” he continued. “I want to be constantly surrounded by it.”

Barlow inadvertently became an icon of “hun culture” thanks to the content he has shared about his passion for wine. In 2024, a clip he posted to TikTok went viral in which he grins into the phone camera while standing in a vineyard, before declaring: “This is my idea of a very nice day out.”

Later that same year, he went viral again when he was filmed pouring a cup of tea into a plant pot so he could swap his beverage for a glass of white wine. In another instance, he proclaimed he was “having the time” – pause – “and the wine” – second pause, so the rhyme can sink in – “of [his] life”.

For the six-part series, Barlow has teamed up with Waterloo Road star Manford – who described the experience as “one of the biggest privileges of my life”.

Barlow told PA he chose Manford as his travel companion because he wanted someone he already knew and liked.

He said the decision was made when the comedian told him he knew “nothing about wine”, adding: “Perfect, because then he can learn while the audience are watching. That’s the best thing.

“It just worked brilliantly. When we weren’t being filmed, we were having breakfast or dinner together. It was just a really lovely trip.

“We’ve probably known each other for about 15 years. We knew each other, but we didn’t know each other that well – but we just had a ball.”

Barlow said the two-week experience filming together was “really sweet” and “very special”.

They visited locations such as Auckland, Waiheke Island, Queenstown, Central Otago, Marlborough Sounds and Hawke’s Bay to discover new foods, landscapes and experiences.

They also immersed themselves in New Zealand culture and experienced Maori traditions, taking on new challenges such as zip-lining through a native forest and tandem cycling together through vineyards.

The series comes after Gary Barlow’s Wine Tour: South Africa in 2024, and Gary Barlow’s Food And Wine Tour: Australia – which aired last year.

open image in gallery Gary Barlow launched his own Gary Barlow Wines brand with an Organic Sauvignon Blanc and Blush ( Getty )

The singer described New Zealand as “one of my favourite places”, and when asked where he would like to travel to next he said: “I’ve actually been on tour years ago – at the end of the 90s.

“I’d love to go back now as a someone who loves wine.

“The place is called Chile in South America. Imagine drinking Malbec in a beautiful vineyard with a new appreciation for it.”

Barlow rose to fame in the 1990s as the main songwriter and lead vocalist of pop group Take That, alongside Robbie Williams, Mark Owen, Howard Donald and Jason Orange.

The band achieved 12 UK number one singles with tracks such as ‘Pray’ ‘Relight My Fire and Never Forget’, as well as nine UK number one albums and eight Brit Awards.

Barlow launched a successful solo career after Take That split in 1996, but they eventually reunited in 2005 with a second wave of chart-topping albums.

Gary Barlow’s Food And Wine Tour: New Zealand will air on Sunday August 30 on ITV.

News.title: Apple iPhone Ultra to launch within weeks – here’s everything to know
News.content:
In just a few week’s time, Apple could finally lift the lid on its first foldable iPhone. The device which has reportedly been in the works for years, will see the tech giant take on the likes of Google and Samsung, the latter of which recently launched the Galaxy Z Fold 8, which it could closely resemble in terms of dimensions.

Expected to feature a near crease-free design, rounded bezels and an iPad mini-like inner display, some early testers have reportedly already had their fingers on the device, and it seems they’re rather impressed.

Below, we’re rounding up everything we know so far about the iPhone Ultra, from its expected price and release date to all the latest gossip surrounding its design, cameras and displays.



Latest Apple iPhone Ultra news and rumours

On 23 August, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reported that he had spoken to several people who had used Apple’s foldable iPhone. “People who have tried the Apple model like how it fits in a pocket, the feel and durability of the advanced hinge mechanism and the new iPad-like app layouts that take advantage of the larger internal display,” Gurman wrote.

Gurman says that people he had spoken to said that the foldable iPhone excelled as a camera viewfinder, though it won’t have a telephoto camera. Gurman also predicts that it’ll cost at least $2,000 (£1,466), and the high price tag and lack of a telephoto snapper might put off early adopters.

Apple iPhone Fold release date

Apple has reportedly been working on a foldable smartphone for years. In January 2021, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reported that the tech giant had begun early work on a foldable iPhone and was already testing prototype foldable displays internally.

We’ve been waiting for it to launch ever since. In 2021, Apple analyst Ming-Chi Kuo speculated the folding iPhone could launch as early as 2024. Evidently, that never happened. Due to the challenges in manufacturing a foldable iPhone without a crease, there have been delays, leading Kuo to suggest last year that it would launch in 2026 instead.

Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman gave us a better idea of this potential launch strategy in late 2025. He stated that Apple would move towards a more spread-out launch window from September 2026, only launching the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max in September, as well as the all-new iPhone Fold.

But in March 2026, Barclays analyst Tim Long claimed in a research note that, while the iPhone Fold will launch alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max in September, it won’t be released until December. Apple has used this strategy in the past, delaying the iPhone X launch until December but keeping the iPhone 8 release in September.

While a report from Nikkei Asia claimed in early April that Apple had faced setbacks during the engineering test phase for the iPhone Fold, potentially delaying the phone even further into 2027, Gurman said on April 7 that it was still on track to launch this September.

But another new report from late July threw that into doubt (again). DigiTimes reported that Foxconn, Apple's primary manufacturing partner for the iPhone Ultra, had faced step backs in the mass manufacturing process of the foldable, requiring it to make adjustments. The issues reportedly related to the folding screen’s durability and the hinge.

But once again, we’re being spun round the “will it be delayed or won’t it” merry-go-round. Weibo leaker Fixed Focus Digital reported on 2 August that while there were issues in scaling production initially, those issues have now been resolved, and that, yes, the iPhone Ultra has not been delayed after all. We’e just as dizzy as you are.

In any case, whenever it does launch, it may be difficult to get your hands on the iPhone Ultra. According to reliable Apple insider Ming-Chi Kuo, Apple will be making 8 million units of the iPhone Ultra at launch, and that will be the entire supply for the rest of the year. It may follow a similar release strategy to the iPhone X, which was announced in September, but didn’t ship until November.

According to a report from Nikkei Asia, the tech giant is actually so confident in the iPhone Ultra that it has increased production from Kuo’s rumoured 8 million to a reported 10 million for the rest of 2026.

In any case, it’s certainly on the way. On 9 June, Bloomberg discovered files hidden inside the first developer beta for iOS 27, spotting code that could determine whether a device was folded or unfolded. The code also made reference to different folding states and various angle degrees. Interestingly, Bloomberg also reports that an updated Apple service utility, which is used to repair iPhone displays, mentions a secondary display, as well as a second cover glass and two additional light sensors. It’s the biggest acknowledgement of the iPhone Ultra yet.

In an even bigger indicator that Apple is gearing up to launch the iPhone Ultra was the company’s State of the Union developer keynote at WWDC. During the keynote, it showed off something called “app adaptability”, which will help developers design their apps for various different screen sizes and aspect ratios. Tech YouTuber Marques Brownlee highlighted the biggest giveaway below:

It looks very likely that the iPhone Fold will at least be announced this September, even if shipments could slip to December. I’m expecting the Apple event to take place on Tuesday, 8 September or Wednesday, 9 September, where it’ll unveil the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, alongside the new folding iPhone.

Apple iPhone Fold price

It’s difficult to predict the price of an all-new smartphone, but there are a lot of rumours floating around, and it might not be a great sign for your wallet – the iPhone Fold could be the most expensive iPhone ever.

In early April, Gurman claimed the iPhone Fold could cost more than $2,000 (£1,500). He said that could deter many customers, but should boost the company’s average sales price. In March 2025, Ming Chi-Kuo also speculated that the iPhone Fold could cost between $2,000 and $2,500 (£1,850)

Weibo leaker Instant Digital shared the potential storage options and prices for each one in March 2026. According to the insider, the three prices for the different storage options are as follows:

256GB: $2,320 (£1,720)

$2,320 (£1,720) 512GB: $2,610 (£1,940)

$2,610 (£1,940) 1TB: $2,900 (£2,150)

Apple notably increased prices of iPads and MacBooks in June, stating it was unable to shield customers from the rising costs of memory. According to Ming-Chi Kuo, the iPhone Ultra could cost $2,300–$2,500 (roughly £1,900). The insider previously stated that the iPhone Ultra would start from $2,000, so he’s now predicting a $300 bump in its starting price.

Apple iPhone Fold name

While there have been plenty of rumours about the name of Apple’s folding phone, a report from Macworld claims it may be called the iPhone Ultra. On 27 April, the publication said the device would be only the second to carry the Ultra branding, after the high-end Apple Watch Ultra. Apple could then expand the name to other devices, with a touchscreen MacBook Ultra tipped for next year, alongside a possible iPad Ultra.

But debate around the name of Apple’s first folding iPhone is starting to ramp up again. Just when it seemed like the insiders had galvanised around the name iPhone Ultra, some are starting to get cold feet. While Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman stated last month that “everyone at Apple” called it the iPhone Ultra internally, some leakers are starting to suggest that it won’t have the Ultra moniker after all.

Meanwhile, Weibo leaker Instant Digital has speculated that Apple would be more likely to reserve the Ultra moniker for the 20th anniversary iPhone instead of the folding iPhone. The 20th anniversary iPhone is predicted to be Apple’s first all-glass iPhone.

Instant Digital referenced previous uses of the Ultra moniker, saying the new device was “unworthy” of the Ultra name. The leaker thus predicts Apple will go with iPhone Fold after all. We’ll just have to wait and see.

Apple iPhone Fold design and display

As mentioned previously, Apple has been tinkering with various folding designs for a while now. One of the options was a clamshell-style folding phone. Like the Samsung Galaxy Z Flip line, but according to Ming-Chi Kuo, the tech giant decided on a book-style design, similar to the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold, meaning it’ll open out into a larger tablet when unfolded.

In March last year, Kuo claimed the foldable iPhone would boast a 7.8in crease-free inner display and a 5.5in outer display. That’s interesting because if Apple goes for a 5.5in display, the cover screen will be much smaller than rival foldables.

Kuo also said that it’ll have a crease-free design, a difficult feat that no mainstream phone manufacturer has quite achieved yet. The insider also stated that the hinge will combine stainless steel and titanium alloy, while the casing will use titanium alloy only.

In terms of thickness, Kuo claims it will be between 9 and 9.5mm when folded shut, and 4.5 to 4.8mm thick when unfolded like a tablet. It will, however, only have two cameras on the rear and two front-facing cameras that can be used when folded or unfolded. There reportedly won’t be any room for Face ID, however, with Apple expected to use a Touch ID side button.

In December 2025, The Information leaked more details about the iPhone Fold’s dimensions. According to the outlet, it has a 5.3in display when folded, expanding to 7.7in when unfolded. What’s most intriguing is the aspect ratio, with hints that it’ll be wider than tall. The publication claims it’ll have a 2:3 aspect ratio, expanding to 4:3 when unfolded.

In March 2026, Apple Track created a realistic-looking concept of what the iPhone Fold might look like based on the latest design leaks. The YouTube channel stated that each display will have its own Dynamic Island.

In early April 2026, insider Sonny Dickson leaked dummy pictures of what the iPhone Fold will reportedly look like when it launches in September.

On 16 April, reliable leaker Majin Bu showed off images of what it claimed were the final designs of the iPhone Fold. It shows an almost-square display, with a camera bar that looks similar to the iPhone Air. On 19 April, Bu also leaked the cases, indicating that it will feature MagSafe, so you can charge your phone wirelessly and attach magnetic accessories.

According to Korean publication The Elec, the iPhone Fold will boast two OLED displays that use Samsung Display’s CoE (Color filter on Encapsulation) technology, which has been used on the Galaxy Z Fold series since 2021, which should make the displays more efficient and thinner.

On 22 April, Vadim Yuryev from the Max Tech YouTube channel shared a series of images and videos of dummy units of Apple’s rumoured foldable iPhone. What’s immediately clear is that Apple might not be going tall with its first foldable like Samsung and Google, but opting for something wider and more compact instead, fitting more easily inside a pocket.

When comparing the iPhone Fold to the iPhone 17 Pro Max in its unfolded state, it appears the foldable is roughly the same width as the Pro Max in landscape but significantly taller. That could make it way better for watching content on the go with a 4:3 aspect ratio.

It looks absolutely tiny when closed. According to previous leaks, the iPhone Fold could boast similar dimensions to an iPhone 13 mini when shut, with a 5.5in outer display. Yuryev also demonstrated how easy it is to reach across the screen in its folded state, showing it can be used one-handed. You can also see the power button on the right, predicted to house a Touch ID sensor, as well as the camera control button. Similar to an iPad mini, the volume buttons can be seen on the top edge.

Yuryev also compared the iPhone Fold dummy to an 8.3in iPad mini. Barring the mini’s thick bezels, they look roughly the same size, so it could be like having an iPad mini in your pocket. Interestingly, Yuryev’s dummy is 11mm thick, which is different to previous rumours that suggested it could be 9mm thick when closed.

On 1 May, Macworld revealed the reported colourways for the upcoming iPhone Fold. And it might be disappointing news for those who like a pop of colour. Apparently, the iPhone Ultra will only come in two colours – silver/white and silver/indigo, which reportedly looks similar to the iPhone 17 Pro’s deep blue. Macworld created a mock-up of the indigo iPhone Fold below.

( Macworld )

On 1 June, Weibo leaker Ice Universe released an image of a dummy iPhone Ultra that purports to be one of the two colourways of the upcoming phone. Shown in silver/white, it has reportedly entered mass production. The leaker says it’s the only confirmed colourway so far, though Macworld previously claimed it would also come in silver/indigo.

Another Weibo leaker also claimed on 1 June that Apple's first foldable iPhone will feature a vapour chamber cooling system despite its ultra-thin design. Fixed Focus Digital stated that the vapour chamber cooling system, which Apple introduced on the iPhone 17 Pro, will help move heat away from the processor more efficiently. It also claimed the foldable was still on track for a September launch, despite reports of production challenges.

Sonny Dickson has also shared images of camera protectors reportedly designed for Apple’s upcoming foldable phone.

The images show the camera lens protector in silver and dark blue (the two colours currently tipped for the iPhone Ultra). In the pictures, there’s a long, horizontal oval design with holes for two rear cameras, as well as openings for the microphone and flash, matching previous leaks regarding a dual-lens camera system on the rear.

Apple iPhone Fold cameras

There isn’t a huge amount of detail about the cameras just yet, but Ming Chi-Kuo stated in 2025 that it will feature a dual lens setup, rather than a triple lens rear.

In June 2025, Weibo leaker Digital Chat Station claimed the dual camera rear setup will feature 48MP, matching the iPhone 17 Pro’s main cameras.

According to a JP Morgan industry report, seen by MacRumors, the iPhone Fold’s outer display (when folded) will feature a 24MP under-screen camera built into the inside display. This would be huge if true, given that many under-display sensors are notoriously bad in terms of picture quality.

iPhone Fold specs and battery life

There’s even less information about the iPhone Fold’s specs. According to analyst Jeff Pu, the iPhone Fold will boast Apple’s A20 chip, built on TSMC's 2nm process. It will reportedly be 15 per cent faster and 30 per cent more efficient than the A19.

In March 2026, Korean outlet The Bell claimed the iPhone Fold will feature 12GB of RAM, something supplied by Samsung

Battery life is expected to be absolutely mammoth, however. A post from a leaker on the Korean Naver blog claimed in November 2025 that it will boast a huge 5,400 to 5,800mAh battery – the biggest capacity of any iPhone ever.

Thunderstorm warnings have been issued across parts of the country as the Met Office warns of flooding and disruption.

Yellow warnings for storms will be in place across the West and East Midlands, as well as the North West, South East, South West and east of England, and parts of Wales. The warnings will hang over England and Wales from 3am until 10pm on Wednesday, and 6am until 10pm on Thursday.

The Met Office warned there is a “small risk of flooding and disruption from thunderstorms“ on Wednesday. Thunderstorms and heavy rain could also bring disruption on Thursday.

open image in gallery A thunderstorm warning is in place across England and Wales ( Met Office )

A band of heavy showers and thunderstorms is expected to move northwards on Wednesday morning, the forecaster warned, adding an intense downpour of 20 to 30mm of rain could fall in less than an hour.

Some spots could see 40 to 50mm in two to three hours, leading to some surface water flooding, with the possibility of large hail and frequent lightning.

These showers and thunderstorms are expected to drift northwards and ease during the evening.

On Thursday, another band of thunderstorms and heavy rain is expected to move slowly across England and Wales. The Met Office said that 20-30 mm of rainfall is expected to accumulate in three hours across the affected areas and up to 50 mm in a 12 hour period can be expected in places.

open image in gallery Some area can expect up to 50 mm of rainfall in a 12 hour period on Thursday ( Met Office )

There is a small chance that some places may see more than 50 mm in three hours and more than 75 mm through 12 hours, especially over east facing high ground. Lightning and hail of 1-2 cm will also be hazardous, the forecaster warned.

Homes and businesses could be flooded quickly, the forecaster said, with damage to some buildings from floodwater, lightning strikes or hail. Flooding and lightning could cause delays and cancellations to train and bus services.

The risk of spray and sudden flooding could also lead to road closures and difficult driving conditions, the forecaster added, with a chance of power cuts for some parts of the country.

Met Office deputy chief forecaster, Mark Sidaway, attributed the unsettled weather to warmer and more humid air moving north across the UK.

open image in gallery Rain is expected across parts of the country on Wednesday ( Met Office )

"While many areas will see dry and increasingly warm conditions at the start of the week, attention is turning to the potential for heavy rain and thunderstorms from Wednesday onwards,” he said.

"As warmer and more humid air moves north across the UK, there is an increasing likelihood of some heavy rain developing. Some places could see 20 to 30mm of rain in just a few hours, while there is also the potential for higher totals where thunderstorms repeatedly affect the same locations.

"The detail of which areas will see the heaviest rainfall is still uncertain, so stay up to date with the forecast this week to keep updated on the increasing risk of impactful weather during the latter part of the week."

By Thursday, a band of heavy and thundery rain is expected to move northwards through England and Wales slowly, which could lead to substantial rainfall totals.

open image in gallery People under an umbrella in the rain on Sunny Sands Beach in Folkestone last week ( Getty )

The incoming downpour comes as England and Wales are expected to record one of the driest summers on record. Almost three-quarters of England is designated as under drought, as is the entirety of Wales.

Scientists previously warned that a heavy downpour could cause more harm than good following the dry and hot summer, as it could lead to flash flooding in parts of the country.

The Environment Agency flood forecast for the next five days suggests that local flooding from surface water is “possible more widely on Wednesday”, which could bring deluge to land, roads and some properties.

News.content:

Director James Cameron’s acclaimed sci-fi movie Aliens turns 40 in August. It’s a sequel to Ridley Scott’s claustrophobic breakout hit Alien, made in 1979. Where the original featured one terrifying creature, Cameron’s movie features hundreds – and pits them against a squad of space marines.

A host of intriguing technologies make an appearance, including interstellar travel, hypersleep (where humans are preserved in stasis for long space journeys) and terraforming (making other worlds liveable for humans).

Some of the technologies in the film have already come to pass – or look likely to soon. But others were missed and some remain firmly in the realms of science fiction.

In Aliens, the marines travel to a distant moon to investigate the disappearance of over 100 human settlers. Ellen Ripley (Sigourney Weaver), the main protagonist of the first film, goes along to advise.

On arrival, they run into a six-year-old girl, called Newt, who managed to escape the grisly fate of the other colonists. When the marines encounter the alien hive, chaos and carnage ensue.

open image in gallery The film is set in 2179, 153 years into our future ( 20th Century Fox )

The technology featured in Aliens appears to be there to support the wonderful storytelling, rather than predict the path of innovation, as a futurologist might.

But let’s take a look at it. The film is set in 2179, 153 years into our future. Journeying 153 years into the past would land us in 1873, when common technologies were horse drawn and steam streetcars and gas lighting. Typewriters with Qwerty keyboards went on sale the following year.

Industrial aesthetic

We’ve moved on considerably, but the future world of Aliens feels less distant in many respects. Company executives use clunky business cards to trigger low-resolution video calls and wave computer printouts during meeting room showdowns.

For modern audiences, however, the lack of personal electronic devices may be jarring. One can only assume that they must have fallen out of favour by 2179.

The gritty, industrial visual style established in the first film was taken further here. Aliens introduces a variety of military vehicles that contain futuristic elements while drawing on real hardware used in the Vietnam war. The movie’s look influenced later films, but it has also been described as “everyday” and “ugly”.

open image in gallery We’ve moved on considerably, but the future world of Aliens feels less distant in many respects ( 20th Century Fox )

An exception is the tracking technology: the motion detectors, wearable cameras and biosensors embedded into wristbands. These feel broadly “current”. But if we extrapolate from the present day, one might expect engineers in 2179 to make greater use of surveillance cameras and computer vision (a sub-field of AI where machines are trained to “understand” images and video).

A network of “smart cameras” throughout the moon colony could have tracked both the aliens and humans. Similar networks today monitor crowds and individuals – and watch for suspicious behaviour – on city streets and public transport.

Sentry guns and exoskeletons

The robots of Aliens are striking. Some are not so far removed from hardware used today, but with notable differences. In two separate scenes, Ripley straps into a massive mechanical suit known as a “loader”.

They are mainly used to move cargo, but, conveniently, can be appropriated for fighting xenomorphs. The loaders are a type of exoskeleton, real life wearable tech that may enhance human strength or movement.

Exoskeletons aren’t generally used for this kind of task yet. Large autonomous or teleoperated factory robots are the go-to technology for lifting heavy hardware. This is safer than having humans operate in such hazardous environments.

Current exoskeletons are smaller in scale than the loaders. They are helping people walk again after traumatic injury and commercial versions are available to support those with mobility issues to hill walk.

open image in gallery Director James Cameron’s acclaimed sci-fi movie Aliens turns 40 in August ( 20th Century Fox )

The war in Ukraine, meanwhile, has familiarised us with autonomous combat robots. One or two share a striking resemblance to the film’s automated sentry guns, which guard an entrance passage in the colony. But drone aircraft, in heavy use today, are notable by their absence.

However, one robot in Aliens operates at a level far beyond the rest: the android Bishop, played by Lance Henriksen. Bishop looks like a human on the outside and is referred to in the film as a “synthetic”.

By 2179, synthetics appear to be approaching human levels of cognitive function – something known as artificial general intelligence (AGI). They even seem to observe the laws of robotics devised by scientist and author Isaac Asimov. In one scene, Bishop tells crew members that he cannot harm a human or allow one to be harmed – Asimov’s first law.

Synthetics occupy capable and realistic bodies which seem to incorporate soft robotics. In this real research area, scientists create robots with flexible materials instead of hard ones, such as metal. Fluids or pressurised air generate movement rather than conventional electric actuators.

The synthetics probably have soft robotic systems overlaid on a rigid framework, similar to flesh on bone. They are therefore likely to be a mixture of soft and conventional robotics.

Tech conundrum

Some of the tech in Aliens remains well out of reach. We don’t have propulsion systems capable of sending crews to other stars and back within a lifetime. As regards hypersleep, in rare cases, humans have survived extreme hypothermia for over an hour, but this is not recommended. Terraforming, meanwhile, remains resolutely theoretical. But what of the synthetics?

About the author Steve Benford is a Professor of Collaborative Computing at the University of Nottingham. This article is republished from The Conversation under a Creative Commons license. Read the original article.

Rightly or wrongly, many researchers and companies aspire to create humanoid robots and achieve AGI. We are bombarded with visions of their latest efforts on social media. But some proportion of those working on such ventures are looking to raise money. Many experts would argue that synthetic humans like those in the Alien movies are still far beyond today’s capabilities.

This leads us to a striking conundrum at the heart of Aliens. Why aren’t there more synthetics? Why not send a population of them to terraform worlds or fight aggressive ETs?

Perhaps humans are more expendable: maybe we will end up doing AI’s dirty work because we are the cheaper commodity. But there is a more optimistic answer. Maybe, despite all of our apparent failings and weaknesses, humans are the more capable being.

After all, it is Ripley – not Bishop – who, wildly improvising with available technologies and driven by her unstoppable desire to protect Newt, defeats the alien queen. Perhaps there is hope yet for our species.

Meta appears to be working on a “kill switch” for its controversial smart glasses.

The company first launched the smart glasses in 2021, in collaboration with Ray-Ban. They include a camera in their front to make it easy to take photos and videos, and have undergone a number of iterations since.

In recent months, however, they have been subject to sustained criticism and scorn for making it easier for people to film others without their consent or even knowledge. The outrage has been such that the eyewear has been informally branded “pervert glasses”.

A new patent, filed earlier this year by Meta and granted last week, appears to suggest that the company could be working on new ways of restricting the amount of filming that the glasses are able to do. While it was filed before the current outrage reached its peak, it may be a response to ongoing questions about whether the glasses are a threat to people’s privacy.

The new patent would allow Meta to switch off one or more sensors in the glasses in the hardware itself. ( AFP/Getty )

The patent describes a feature for “consumer devices, such as augmented reality devices”, and though it does not name Meta’s smart glasses specifically it includes a number of illustrations that look notably similar to the products currently on sale. It describes a “hardware privacy mute circuit”.

That would allow it to switch off one or more sensors in the glasses in the hardware itself. That would “provide tamper-resistant privacy controls that cannot be compromised through software exploits”, the patent says.

Such a system would mean that the glasses would be physically unable to record, in a way that could not be switched on through a hack or other attempt to break into the software that powers them.

Meta’s glasses already include some features aimed at limiting their use for photos or videos without the knowledge of the people being filmed. They include a light that appears on the front of the glasses when the camera is on, though guides online offer a variety of ways to hide it.
