The areas in line for a multi-billion pound boost in housing funding have been revealed as the government promises the “biggest council housebuilding revival in decades”.

Around £10bn has been pledged to deliver 70,000 homes across England, the Ministry for Housing, Communities and Local Government (MHCLG) has announced.

This will spread between 33 ‘strategic partners’, including councils, housing associations and other providers. Six local mayors outside of London will receive around £2.5bn.

The funding is being delivered as part of the government’s £39 Social and Affordable Homes Programme (SAHP). The ten-year sum was first agreed by Sir Keir Starmer and Rachel Reeves in 2025, alongside housing secretary Angela Rayner during her first term in the role.

Ms Rayner said: “Families can’t be left raising children without a place to call home, and none of us should spend years waiting for somewhere safe and affordable to live.

“That’s why the Prime Minister and I are doing everything we can to get councils building once again – it’s fundamental to turning the housing crisis around, helping families out of temporary accommodation and into a secure home.”

Around 134,000 households housing over 176,130 children are currently living in temporary accommodation, as of the latest statistics.

At the same time, over 1.3 million households are on their local authority’s waiting list for social housing.

Through the SAHP, 60 per cent of homes built are expected to be for social rent. This is the most affordable form of rented housing, typically costing 50 to 60 per cent of local market rates for long-term tenancies.

Andy Burnham’s previous mayoralty, Greater Manchester, will receive the largest share of funding at £529m to support around 4,400 new homes.

The other mayoral authorities which have had funding announced through this first wave are West Midlands, North East, West Yorkshire, Liverpool, and South Yorkshire.

Announcing the pledge, the prime minister said: “No child should be raised in a hostel room and no family should wait ten years for a front door of their own. I have said from my first day in this job that everything starts with a good home.

“Councils built this country out of a housing crisis once before. Backed properly, and trusted to get on with it, they will do it again.”

Mr Burnham said: “Councils built this country out of a housing crisis once before. Backed properly, and trusted to get on with it, they will do it again.” ( PA )

Council housebuilding across the UK has faltered in recent years, with just 2,000 completions annually in the five years leading up to 2025.

This compares to a postwar peak of an average 103,000 homes every year in the late 1970s.

Earlier this month, local leaders and house builders told The Independent that increased costs in the sector and a lack of support from central government was stifling ambitions to build more council homes.

Today’s announcement comes after Mr Burnham pledged in June – shortly before becoming prime minister – to oversee the “biggest council housebuilding drive since the postwar period”.

However, experts have said that reaching levels seen in the 60s and 70s is almost impossible under current conditions.

Through the SAHP, the government intends to deliver 300,000 homes for mixed affordable rent by 2036.

It would require an £8bn funding boost to make all of these social rent homes, research from the Resolution Foundation has found, which would still only be delivered at a rate of 30,000 a year – far below the postwar peak.

A final funding settlement for London has not been announced by MHCLG. However, the Greater London Authority is expected to offer at least £6bn through the programme, with councils expected to deliver half the homes built.

Responding to the latest funding announcement, mayor of London, Sadiq Khan said: “Thousands of Londoners will benefit from this new wave of new social and affordable homes, which will help people out of temporary accommodation and provide good, affordable homes to live in for the long-term, as we build a fairer, better London for everyone.”

Former captain Michael Vaughan believes a strong penalty is needed after Brydon Carse became the latest England cricketer involved in a drinking incident.

Carse was pulled from England’s squad for the second Test against Pakistan after a nightclub incident in Derby on Saturday night resulted in his brief arrest.

Video footage captured the pace bowler handcuffed by police officers, while Durham team-mates Ben Stokes and Matthew Potts were also present.

England white-ball captain Harry Brook, opener Ben Duckett, Stokes and pace bowler Gus Atkinson have all faced alcohol-related controversies since last autumn.

open image in gallery Michael Vaughan has called for a significant punishment to be handed down (Nick Potts/PA) ( PA Archive )

Vaughan told BBC Radio 5 Live: "Someone is going to have to get a punishment that sends a shiver down the whole England cricket team and right down through the programme, so that everyone knows that if you misbehave or bring any kind of bad reputation on to this team, you know what’s going to come.

"It’s the only punishment that will really hurt players."

Independent body the Cricket Regulator confirmed it will investigate, with Vaughan noting it would be harsh if the 31-year-old is singled out.

Vaughan added: "I hope Carse is getting good support around him. He is a character who can be a little bit loose and if you give him a bit of rope he’ll take a huge amount of it. He needs people around him who are giving him better advice.

"I would feel for Carse if he is the one who takes the rap for what has happened over the past nine months, but somewhere, somehow, something has to be done to set a precedent that they won’t stand for that behaviour any more."

Carse has been replaced by Hampshire pace bowler Sonny Baker in England’s squad for the second Test against Pakistan, which gets underway at Lord’s on Thursday.

Joe Root’s side will be looking to wrap up a series victory after thrashing Pakistan by an innings and 103 runs in the first Test at Headingley last week.

After opting to leave out Carse, England’s bowling attack delivered in Leeds, with Ollie Robinson, Josh Tongue, Jofra Archer and Gus Atkinson all among the wickets.

News.title: Three generations of family killed alongside two friends in Oregon quintuple homicide
News.content:

Read our Privacy notice

The five people found dead at a rural Oregon property have been identified as the suspected killer’s girlfriend, three generations of her family and two friends, authorities said Monday.

Investigators are treating the deaths as a quintuple homicide after the bodies were discovered Saturday at a property near Forest Grove, about 30 miles west of Portland.

The suspected killer, 36-year-old Benjamin Charles Parker, was found dead Sunday inside his car in Enumclaw, Washington, about 187 miles from the crime scene. Authorities believe Parker killed himself and said there is no continuing threat to the public.

open image in gallery Oregon Quintuple Homicide ( The Oregonian )

The Washington County Sheriff’s Office identified the victims as Parker’s girlfriend, 26-year-old Stella Jade Kimsey; her mother, Rowan Karla Kimsey, 60; and her grandmother, Mary Elizabeth Kimsey, 85.

Stella Kimsey’s best friend, Linsey Mae Haraldsen, 26, and Haraldsen’s partner, Alvin Raymond Chu, 27, were also killed.

Authorities said Rowan Kimsey owned the rural property and lived there with her daughter and Parker.

Two dogs and two cats were also found dead at the scene. Another cat was taken to a veterinarian but was later euthanized because of the severity of its injuries.

Authorities have not disclosed how the five victims or the animals died.

open image in gallery Oregon Quintuple Homicide ( Mark Graves/The Oregonian )

The investigation began early Saturday when emergency crews responded to reports of a vehicle fire at the property. They subsequently discovered the five bodies and several animals, triggering a sprawling homicide investigation.

Investigators announced Sunday that they were searching for Parker before he was found dead in Washington state.

Authorities have not said what evidence led them to identify Parker as the suspect or disclosed a possible motive for the killings.

Sheriff Caprice Massey described the crime scene as extraordinary in its scale and complexity.

“I will say that in my 22 years here, I have not been a part of or witnessed a scene quite this complex involving this type of an investigation,” Massey said.

Officials faced questions over why the discovery of the bodies was not publicly announced until Sunday. Detective Shannon Wilde said investigators had been working to identify the victims, notify their families and pursue an active investigation before releasing details.

“Any time you have one person deceased, let alone five, that's a logistical challenge,” Wilde said.

The sheriff’s office is continuing to investigate the deaths and has asked anyone with information about the case to contact authorities.

News.title: Help us test binoculars with the RSPB and birding experts
News.content:
At Telegraph Recommended, we test hundreds of products each year, and we rely on our community members to help verify our experts’ findings.

We currently have an upcoming opportunity for Telegraph readers to help test the latest binoculars for birdwatching with the Royal Society for the Protection of Birds (RSPB).

Selected readers will be invited to RSPB’s The Lodge nature reserve in Sandy, Bedfordshire, where Jamie Wyver, editor of the RSPB magazine, and Tim Jones, otherwise known as ‘Begin Birding’ on Instagram, will host two binocular testing mornings.

Taking place on September 23 and 24, Jamie and Tim will lead each group on a morning ramble across the heathland, offering the chance to spot local bird species, including Nightjars, Hobbies and Spotted Flycatchers.

News.title: Palmer and Rogers show promise of star double act for Chelsea
News.content:
“I am very happy for Cole,” Alonso said. “I have really enjoyed seeing him play with the dynamism and the freedom and the responsibility... when Cole feels this way we have a better team and a better Cole.”



Palmer makes it look very easy in this form, capable of switching the direction of play a beat before anyone else spots the opportunity. He and his old Manchester City academy friend Rogers came off before the end, Palmer having demonstrated some discomfort chasing a ball. Asked afterwards how ready he felt, Palmer responded in kind. “Did you not watch the game? I’m only joking, I’m ready... it was a difficult season with injuries and whatnot, but through the summer and since I’ve been back I’ve worked extra hard.”

If there was an attacker to compare with him on the other side it was King, who looks even better. The 19-year-old was way ahead of Arbeloa’s two young Real Madrid imports. García toiled away and took his chance, but César Palacios struggled for any impact in a position tucked in on the left. Oscar Bobb and King gave Fulham some edge but the concern, as ever, will be where Fulham get their goals.

Arbeloa pushed his full-backs high and encouraged Sander Berge to drop deep to get on the ball in the first passing phase. The Norwegian delayed too long in challenging João Pedro for Chelsea’s third – backing off and allowing Palmer to overlap to receive the pass.



Sánchez had not been the only concern for Chelsea. Back in the team, Levi Colwill misjudged a challenge on King in the first half and was relieved that the card was only yellow. Roméo Lavia took a wild swing at Calvin Bassey and was also booked. Moisés Caicedo was not fit to play. Enzo Fernández was on the bench and would come on in the second half to the kind of reception from opposition fans to which he will quickly become familiar.



There was a grin from the Argentine at those who berated him from the home stands when he returned at half-time. Fernández worked hard to transmit a general sense that the abuse did not land, although he will be relieved that the Chelsea fans were supportive. His future still feels very much in play.



It was Palmer’s subtle ball through that gave João Pedro the chance with 32 seconds of the game played. The ball came forward immediately from Lacroix’s firm header from defence. The Frenchman delivered a very accomplished assist for Rogers’s first-half goal. Before that King had equalised. There was an exchange with Timothy Castagne, and King looked up just inside the box and decided to have a swing at it. Sánchez was close enough to grasp the ball and somehow failed to do so.

Sánchez would later push a Castagne shot in the direction of García, who stooped and nodded the ball over the goalkeeper after Palmer had scored Chelsea’s third. This second error was unfortunate, but it is the kind of thing that happens to a goalkeeper as erratic as the one for whom Chelsea’s hierarchy seem to have such patience.

News.title: This summer’s wildfire epidemic is one of the worst in decades – so why are deaths so low?
News.content:
Wildfires in Britain and Europe this year are among the worst in decades, yet direct deaths are at some of the lowest levels, according to a Telegraph analysis.

As of early August, 505,683 hectares of land have burned across Europe, forcing the evacuation of more than 360,000 people as uncontrollable flames reach major cities, towns, and villages.

The problem is global – in the US, Nevada declared a state of emergency over the weekend after a wildfire caused more than 42,000 people to evacuate their homes.

But what sets 2026 apart isn’t just the vast areas of land burned, but how few deaths have been caused by the fires.

This summer, just 14 people are reported to have died in European wildfires, the vast majority in a single blaze in Almería, southern Spain.

By comparison, more than 130 people were killed in the summer of 2017 – a toll driven largely by the Pedrógão Grande disaster in Portugal, where more than 60 people died on a single stretch of road.

In 2018, at least 100 others died in a single afternoon in the Mati disaster near Athens, despite total hectares burned that year being roughly a third of current levels.

Since the modern phenomenon of summer wildfires exploded in Europe a decade ago, the direct death toll has broadly trended downward, as the chart below shows.

News.title: Swine flu outbreak in Delhi swamps clinics and hospitals
News.content:
India is battling a surge in H1N1 flu infections, prompting the federal health ministry to step up surveillance and hospital preparedness.

The national capital New Delhi has recorded 1,777 cases this year, almost eight times the number (229) reported during the same period in 2025.

Dr Randeep Guleria, a senior pulmonologist and director of Medanta Medical School, Gurugram, says the H1N1 cases are much higher than reported.

“It’s quite likely that the reported numbers are an underestimate because they depend on how many people are tested,” Guleria said. “If you speak to patients admitted to hospital who test positive for H1N1, you often find that other members of their family have similar symptoms, although they have not been tested.”

“There is a surge and we are seeing a lot of patients. We are testing only those who come to hospital and are more seriously ill,” Guleria said.

H1N1, commonly known as swine flu, is a subtype of influenza A. It is a contagious respiratory infection that can cause fever and cough and in severe cases it can lead to pneumonia and respiratory failure.

Officials at the Indian Council of Medical Research said the rise did not mean the emergence of a new strain of the virus.

The surge comes during India’s rainy season, when seasonal influenza and other respiratory infections typically increase.

Doctors in Delhi say they are seeing more patients with high fevers, persistent coughs and flu-like symptoms, although most cases remain mild.

The H1N1 cases have been reported beyond New Delhi. The metro cities like Mumbai, Chennai and Bangaluru have reported a high number of cases, although the pattern is not uniform across the country.

Doctors in Bangaluru have reported more influenza A infections among children, with some developing pneumonia and respiratory distress.

India’s health minister JP Nadda said there was a need for continued vigilance and robust surveillance. He has asked officials to monitor unusual increases and clusters of cases and ensure hospitals could respond quickly.

“Swine flu (H1N1) can show up through symptoms such as fever, cough, sore throat, headache, runny nose, body aches and fatigue… If you experience these symptoms, seek medical advice at your nearest healthcare centre,” the health ministry said on X.

Delhi’s health minister, Pankaj Kumar Singh, said the capital had enough beds, doctors, medicines and medical equipment to manage the increase. “Delhi is fully prepared to deal with the present health situation,” Singh said.

India has had several waves of H1N1 since the virus emerged globally in 2009.

The infection, commonly called swine flu, became a recurring seasonal respiratory illness after the 2009 pandemic rather than disappearing from circulation.

India recorded 3,320 H1N1 cases and 14 deaths in 2025, according to Ministry of Health data.

News.title: Newcastle and Liverpool serve up thrilling tribute to Kevin Keegan
News.content:
It is fitting that Newcastle United vs Liverpool is a Premier League opening weekend fixture following the death of Kevin Keegan at the age of 75 last month.

All corners of St James’ Park will pay tribute and show their appreciation for the former player and manager who means a great deal to both sets of supporters.

Fans will find a printed message from the Keegan family on the back of black and white cards on their seat, which they will hold up to display a mural before kick-off.

As well as playing for both clubs, Keegan was Newcastle’s manager when they were beaten by a last-gasp Stan Collymore goal at Anfield in April 1996, a 4-3 defeat remembered as one of the great Premier League games.

This fixture usually delivers entertainment, and with new managers Matthias Jaissle and Andoni Iraola promising front-footed, ‘vertical’ football, there should be goals. That was certainly the case last August, when Newcastle fought back from two down with 10 men, before Rio Ngumoha scored a memorable winner.

It has been a summer of tumult for Newcastle, losing manager Eddie Howe, as well as key players Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes. There has been bullish talk of “Newcastle 2.0” from David Hopkinson, the club’s chief executive, and the club believe they have found a promising coach, but fans have understandably revised expectations downwards.

Liverpool are a difficult team to read; champions only 18 months ago but brittle last season, which resulted in Arne Slot’s dismissal. Iraola’s appointment is a shift back towards Jurgen Klopp’s style. That will be music to the ears of Anfield regulars, but holes remain in the squad. Central midfield has not been replenished; they need a Mohamed Salah replacement, and their strength at full-back is questionable. Much will depend on how 21-year-old central defender Jérémy Jacquet fares alongside Vigin van Dijk but he impressed in pre-season.



Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Frustrated Russell fails to make up ground as Norris wins incident-packed Dutch GP
News.content:
George Russell had another frustrating Sunday as the Dutch Grand Prix weekend slipped by with him failing to reduce his deficit to leader Kimi Antonelli. In a thrilling finale to the 72-lap race at the Dutch seaside, Lando Norris took his second victory in a row with two bold overtakes in one lap.

Yet compatriot Russell was irritated by Mercedes team orders for him to let Antonelli through into second place in the closing stages. It was a decision he believed risked a double podium for the team and threatened to put him even further behind his team-mate in the standings, with two charging Ferraris close behind. It was a race that, once again, fell away, despite Russell doing little wrong.

“Is he [Antonelli] fighting for the win or is he planning to catch Norris?” he asked, when the McLaren driver was 11 seconds down the road – the margin he would win by. “Yeah – we just lost a double podium here, mate,” was his response after moving aside.

Whilst Norris, who lost his lead from pole to Antonelli on the first lap, sealed the victory with two superb overtakes on lap 54 – first the Italian and then Lewis Hamilton – Russell had to mount a stout defence from Hamilton to secure third. It was against the odds, as both Ferraris, like Antonelli, were on fresh rubber after pitting under a late virtual safety car. Like Russell, Hamilton was critical of his team for their strategy choices.

Russell’s first podium finish since Silverstone – with his sprint victory on Saturday – means he at least retakes second place in the championship from Hamilton, but trails Antonelli by the same 59 point-gap he had after Hungary. That is despite him looking the faster and more comfortable Mercedes driver on Friday and Saturday.

News.title: Enzo Maresca tinkers his way to nervy Man City win
News.content:
Few in elite sport have the luxury of managing their own endings as Pep Guardiola did at Manchester City, yet no one can ever fully control a beginning. Enzo Maresca’s City started their Premier League season with a win, in the end, but three points masked the scale of the job he faces.

The narrative focus has been the impossibility of filling the personality void Guardiola leaves at a club sculpted in his image. That macro reading overlooks the number of distinct issues with City that Maresca must fix. A new midfield has to be recruited then blooded, a jittery defence needs settling down, and Phil Foden clearly requires help to recover the form which made him Premier League player of the year as recently as 2024.

All of that can wait after this victory against Bournemouth, which quietened some of the alarms from last weekend’s 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in Cardiff. Josko Gvardiol scored an injury-time winner after City had trailed for most of the match, much of it a sloppy slog for the home side, who went behind in the 26th minute. The introduction of Rayan Cherki for Nico O’Reilly revived some familiar attacking effusiveness.

A lesser-spotted VAR-aided double celebration capped a tense but ultimately joyful day for Maresca. Marc Guéhi equalised from Cherki’s well-taken corner in the final minutes, then the expanded Etihad Stadium rapturously celebrated Gvardiol’s apparent winner, only to see it flagged offside. Video assistant Paul Howard intervened to show Gvardiol was onside from Cherki’s pass, before City’s fans, players and staff shouted twice as loud for twice as long to salute a morale-boosting victory.

Sports.title: John Terry claims Jose Mourinho rewarded him with a Dubai holiday for getting booked deliberately but fans smell a rat
Sports.content:
JOHN TERRY has claimed he was given a Dubai holiday by Jose Mourinho for getting a yellow card, but clued-up fans have questioned that version of events.

Chelsea and England icon Terry was chatting to Jimmy Bullard about his time at Stamford Bridge under the Portuguese boss.



And the 45-year-old regaled Bullard with a story of how he was given a holiday to Dubai after picking up a deliberate yellow card to ensure he was not banned for a match against Manchester United in the league.

Speaking on the first episode of FC Bullard The Show, Terry said: “We played, I think it was like the second round of the FA Cup, might have been, I don’t know, Walsall away or something.



“Three Premier League games before, I’m on two bookings. He comes to me and he was like, ‘You have to miss that one because we play Man United at home after Walsall. I want you to miss the FA Cup game, so you have to get booked the next three league games.’

“So I get booked the first game, get booked the second game. I’m on four bookings. I’m one booking away from having a one-game suspension, which would be Walsall away.”



Terry continued by explaining how, in said game, he took a throw-in and was told to get booked.

He added: “There’s a throw-in in the left corner and I said to one of the boys, ‘Leave it.’ Leaves it, and I’m standing there with the ball like this. I’m not throwing it because I know the ref’s going, ‘Come on.’

“We’re winning the game, and he’s going, ‘Come on, throw it.’ And I’m going, ‘There’s no option. I got no options, Ref, mate.’

“I’m waiting about two minutes. In the end, he comes over and books me. I drop the ball and just go running back.

“He sends me to Dubai for four days after. Just… mate. Little bits like that. It was just so good.”

However, fans believed Terry might have forgotten some key details about his career, or at least combined different stories into one.

Indeed, the former Blues captain never picked up three yellow cards in a row in the league under Mourinho.

Terry also never played against Walsall in the FA Cup, though did play against them in the League Cup and pick up a booking in the 52nd minute of a third-round clash in 2015.

Another fan highlighted how Terry might have combined three memories into one, writing: “He’s mixed up three events into one. Scunthorpe 2005: Rested before the Man Utd game.



“Huddersfield 2006: Dubai break with Super Frank.

“Wolves 2011: Deliberately got a 90th-minute 5th yellow to miss a cup tie. This was under Villas-Boas.”

Then Chelsea boss Andre Villas-Boas denied the booking against Wolves, which allowed him to serve a ban in a quarter-final tie against Liverpool before a tough run of games against the likes of Newcastle, Manchester City and Tottenham, was intentional.

Sports.title: Jamie O’Hara will be a dad for the 4th time as he reveals wife is pregnant – and has rare birth condition

JAMIE O’Hara has revealed he will soon become a dad for the fourth time just months after marrying stunning wife Keziah Grubb.

The former Premier League footballer, 39, coined the nickname “Daddy O’Hara” as he made their happy pregnancy news public on Instagram.



While he confessed the couple, who said I Do in April, would be keeping the gender of their first tot together secret, he went on to reveal his stunning spouse Keziah’s hidden health condition.

Alongside an image of their baby scan, the clearly-chuffed TalkSPORT anchor wrote: “Daddy O’Hara is backkkkk can’t wait to make special memories with you, we aren’t finding out the gender but all I know I will love you with all my heart.



“My wife has Uterus didelphys which only 0.3 per cent of women in the world have so it’s a special baby already, only two months left we can’t wait to meet you, you are already kicking us constantly”.

Uterus didelphys is where a woman is born with two uteruses and two cervixes.

According to the World Health Organisation, it affects around one in 3,000 women across the world and occurs when the uterus fails to fuse properly during development in the womb.

Jamie, who is dad to sons Archie, Harry and George with ex wife Danielle Lloyd, was flooded with messages of congratulations from his famous mates.



Former footballer-turned-manager Robbie Keane wrote: “Congrats guys”.

Hollyoaks‘ Gary Lucy quipped: “He shoots … He scores,” before he added the tot would be a “Little Gooner”.

TOWIE‘s Dan Edgar then posted: “Congratulations guys”.

It is the next happy chapter for the ex-Spurs star after the couple’s low key wedding in Kent this spring.

The couple said their vows at St Mary’s Church in Dartford before heading to a modest reception at The Moat in Wrotham.



The couple looked happier than ever as they smiled in the back of a car following their nuptials.

At the time, Jamie penned in his caption: “Mr and Mrs O’Hara I’m so lucky to have the most incredible person in my life forever. What a day”.

Jamie proposed to Keziah last March.

He was previously wed to former Miss England model Danielle Lloyd in 2012.

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher blasts Liverpool’s £445m transfer window last summer as ‘arguably the WORST in Premier League history’
Sports.content:
JAMIE CARRAGHER has sensationally claimed Liverpool might have had the worst transfer window in Premier League history.

Liverpool laboured to a 2-2 draw on the opening day away at Newcastle, with Dominik Szoboszlai scoring an equaliser from the penalty spot with the last kick of the game to rescue a point in Andoni Iraola‘s first game.



However, a number of stars who were backed to have better seasons ended up having particularly poor games against the Magpies.

That included record signings Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz, as well as full-back duo Milos Kerkez and Jeremie Frimpong, who all arrived at the club in the summer of 2025.



They were joined on the incoming list by goalkeeper Giorgi Mamardashvili, Hugo Ekitike, Giovanni Leoni for a total outlay of £445million in Arne Slot‘s final summer transfer window at the club.

However, with Mamardashvili looking dodgy at best when he does play in Alisson‘s absence and both Ekitike and Leoni missing at the start of this season due to injury, Carragher has not reflected on the window kindly.

Speaking on Sky Sports Monday Night Football, Carragher said: “My fear watching Liverpool, listen its the first game of the season, is this window (2025) could set Liverpool back a year or two.

“Don’t forget, last season it was not about these players. You (Gary Neville) said on the podcast yesterday these players had got off lightly, and you’re right.

“Because it was all about Arne Slot and his style of play, and he’s not like Jurgen Klopp, and he’s holding his players back.

“Yes it’s one game under Iraola, but we’re talking 12 months of underperformance from all of these players except him (Ekitike).

“If this doesn’t change in the next two or three months under Iraola and these players improving, I think we’re at that as arguably the worst transfer window in Premier League history.”

“Let’s not forget, Liverpool won the league two years ago.

Sports.title: Leeds and Rangers co-owner York arrested
Sports.content:
Jed York, who owns San Francisco 49ers, was initially charged with engaging in prostitution, but prosecutors amended that to disorderly conduct; York was arrested Sunday morning at a mobile home community in East Palestine, Ohio; He was sentenced to one day in jail for both offences

Leeds and Rangers co-owner Jed York arrested in Ohio and pleads no contest to misdemeanour charges of disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools

Leeds United and Rangers co-owner Jed York was arrested over the weekend in Ohio and pleaded no contest to misdemeanour charges of disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools.

Court records show that York, who owns the San Francisco 49ers, was initially charged with engaging in prostitution, but prosecutors amended that to disorderly conduct.

York was charged with possessing criminal tools for using his phone to respond to an undercover online prostitution , according to prosecutors.

York was arrested Sunday morning at a mobile home community in East Palestine, Ohio, near where he was born and raised in Youngstown. He was released after posting a $5,000 bond.

He was sentenced to one day in jail for both offences to be served concurrently and was credited with one day served when he pleaded no contest Monday morning. He was also fined $1,150.

Records also show that York had his cell phone returned to him and that $160 that was seized was to be given to the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force as part of the plea agreement. York also completed an online course.

Columbiana County Prosecutor Vito Abruzzino said most of these prostitution cases typically end in plea agreements.

"Each case is looked at individually and for specific facts of the conduct, what evidence the police provide, and input from the arresting officer," he said in an email.

"You also have to factor in criminal history of the defendant, and whether or not they have committed these types of offences in the past, and importantly, what the judges will allow."

The 49ers Enterprises - who are the investment arm of York's San Francisco 49ers - own Leeds United. The Premier League club have declined to comment.

They are also part of the US consortium who acquired a majority shareholding in Rangers last summer. However, York is not listed on the club's list of board members.

When contacted by Sky Sports News, Rangers chose not to comment.

The NFL issued a statement saying the league was aware of the arrest and would review it under the personal conduct policy.

Owners are subject to possible fines or suspensions for violating the personal conduct policy.

Sports.title: NRL to allow Arrow to reach Rabbitohs century after MND retirement
Sports.content:
The NRL is planning an exception to its rules to allow Jai Arrow to reach the 100-game milestone for the South Sydney Rabbitohs after retiring earlier this year due to a motor neurone disease diagnosis.

MND Australia describes it as an umbrella term for a group of progressive neurological conditions in which the motor neurones degenerate. Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is the most common form, and is often called Lou Gehrig's disease.

As part of an agreement with the Rabbitohs, the NRL granted South Sydney special dispensation to include Arrow, 31, as an extra player on Tuesday's official team list and an additional interchange in their rotation for Saturday's game against the Gold Coast Titans.

A similar dispensation will be granted for South Sydney's final regular-season game against the Sydney Roosters.

According to the NRL, Arrow will get dressed in South Sydney playing kit on both matchdays, join the Rabbitohs in the dressing room, lead the team onto the field, become the team's first interchange within seconds of the opening whistle without taking part in any play, and then remain on the interchange bench in his playing kit for the rest of the game.

It will take Arrow's tally to 180 career NRL games and 100 for the Rabbitohs, in addition to his representative appearances for Queensland in the annual State of Origin series.

Australian Rugby League Commission chairman Peter V'landys said it was a chance for the sport to be a "conduit to bring out the best of humanity".

Image: Arrow has announced his immediate retirement from rugby league after being diagnosed with Motor Neurone Disease

"This thoughtful gesture by the South Sydney Rabbitohs shows the true heart of our game," V'landys said. "Jai has inspired millions of people around the world with the courage and strength he has shown in his fight with MND. He is not only a great player, but an extraordinary person.

"Reaching 100 games for the Rabbitohs is a special achievement, one that Jai, his family and everyone who has supported him should be incredibly proud of. The entire rugby league community stands with Jai and is honoured to celebrate this remarkable milestone with him."

Rugby league star Rob Burrow and Scotland rugby union great Doddie Weir are among the high-profile sportsmen to have died from the illness in recent years.

Sports.title: Arsenal and Al Hilal make progress on Martinelli deal
Sports.content:
Arsenal and Al Hilal have made progress in the last few days over a deal for Gabriel Martinelli.

Martinelli is seriously considering joining Al Hilal if a deal can be agreed between the clubs.

As an agreement on the fee nears, there is also expected to be a sell-on clause involved to the tune of 20 per cent of any future profit.

Arsenal are looking at potential new forward options themselves before the deadline, with Atletico Madrid's Julian Alvarez still their top target.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Sam Blitz takes a closer look at the future of striker Julian Alvarez and where he may end up should he leave Atletico Madrid.

Reports have linked them with Juventus forward Kenan Yildiz, but he has picked up a left foot injury and could face a lengthy spell on the sidelines, according to Sky in Italy.

Sky in Italy are reporting that Juventus' medical staff are looking at various methods to find the best possible solution - but are not ruling out surgery that could rule him out for several weeks.

Martinelli was not named in the Arsenal matchday squad for the Community Shield win over Manchester City or the opening day victory over Coventry.

Analysis: Are Arsenal risking being short at left wing?

Sky Sports' Sam Blitz:

Arsenal started last season with Leandro Trossard and Martinelli as their two main left wing options. Should Martinelli's move to Al Hilal go through, they will start this season with neither of them.

Mikel Arteta's side are undergoing a slight revolution in that left-wing role, with Christos Tzolis set to be the only recognised left winger in the Arsenal squad.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Premier League match between Arsenal and Coventry.

The Greek winger has started his career in north London on fire - but with a week of the window to go, Arsenal could risk leaving themselves short on that flank.

Eberechi Eze came on as a left winger in Friday's win over Coventry, so there is cover in a makeshift area. The same applies to Noni Madueke, who has also featured on the left for Arsenal.

But Madueke and Eze both have an important role in providing cover and competition for Bukayo Saka and Martin Odegaard - who both don't have the best injury record. They may be needed elsewhere.

Arsenal's attacking targets are also slimming down. There is still interest in Atletico Madrid's Alvarez but that is far from a guarantee, with the Argentine's heart set on a move to Barcelona.

With Juventus' Yildiz now injured, sporting director Andrea Berta may have to produce a major move in the last week of the window.

Martinelli, meanwhile, departs Arsenal as a cult hero. He is one of three Arsenal players - alongside Saka and Reiss Nelson - who was in the Gunners squad when Arteta first took charge in December 2019.

He remained a popular player despite only scoring one Premier League goal last season - albeit an important one against Manchester City.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking from Arsenal's trophy parade, Gabriel Martinelli says there are 'no words to describe this moment'. Watch the Champions Live From N5 parade live on Arsenal club channels.

His record in the Champions League was much better, scoring six goals in his first seven matches in the competition last season - but consistency and confidence was lacking at the end of the campaign.

And Martinelli may be the player who takes the fall to improve Arsenal's overall transfer business. Any deal involving the Brazilian would surely break Arsenal's sale record - which has stood for nine years since Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain departed for Liverpool in 2017.

Arsenal need to sell better as a football club - does that start right now with the Brazilian?

Wright: Martinelli deserves to be treated with more respect

Former Arsenal striker Ian Wright speaking to Sky Sports:

"The way Martinelli is being treated at the moment, it really makes me feel uncomfortable.

"I know they might want him out, and a lot of people might say, 'yeah, it's time for him to move him on'. But there's ways of doing that and it should suit him as well, how he wants to leave.

"Not being involved in the squad, not being spoken to, he doesn't know what's going on. And yes, I know this - he doesn't know what is happening.

"He's done enough with this squad to be treated with a little bit more respect than he's being treated with at the moment.

"If you bring Vini in, Martinelli can say to himself, 'OK, they've brought him in, they've brought Tzolis in, I might be third [in the pecking order].

"But if you bring Tzolis in and have [Noni] Madueke on the other side, you're thinking to yourself, 'I can still have it with these two, I've got something to offer'. For him to be nowhere near it, it just makes me feel a bit sad for him."

Sports.title: Cameron: It will take someone special to beat me - Mayer's not that
Sports.content:
Chantelle Cameron is aiming for a career-best performance when she takes on Mikaela Mayer in their blockbuster main event unification bout in Birmingham on Saturday.

British world champion Cameron (22-1, 8 KOs) faces American Mayer (22-2, 5 KOs) at the bp pulse LIVE arena in Birmingham on August 29 - live on Sky Sports - with every bout on the MVPW-06 main card pitting a UK fighter against a US opponent.

Cameron maintains Mayer - who holds the WBC and WBA belts - is not "special" enough to threaten her chances of victory.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mayer says she and Cameron are at the peak of their powers

"I really do believe this is going to be a great performance by me - I think it's going to be my best performance of my career, I really do," Cameron told Sky Sports.

"I feel like everything's gone well and there's no reason for it to fall apart on fight night. When I'm like this, and I've put the work in and my mindset is where I want it to be, nobody's beating me.

"I know that all I have to do is do what I've been doing in the gym. I've done everything.

"I'm heading into fight week in such a good place - confident and knowing that it's going to take someone really good and special to beat me, and I just don't think that's Mikaela.

"When I'm thinking like that and acting that out in the gym and everything else, I just know that I'm not going to be denied the victory."

Sports.title: Chelsea's electric front three edge out Fulham in pulsating MNF opener
Sports.content:
Cole Palmer was back to his best to get Xabi Alonso's Chelsea career off to a winning start in a chaotic 3-2 victory at Fulham on Monday Night Football.

The Blues' attacking trio of Palmer, Joao Pedro and Morgan Rogers looked every bit the most potent in the Premier League as all three scored in a game where entertainment reigned and defending was an afterthought.

Palmer, finally injury-free and all the better for a summer off from England's World Cup campaign, scored one and made another in the kind of performance he had found so difficult to reproduce last season.

If his confidence on the pitch was not evidence enough, his response when Sky Sports asked how ready he was for the new season was emphatic. "Did you not watch the game?"

It took just 31 seconds for him to lay down a marker by teeing up an opener for Joao Pedro - himself refreshed after his surprise Brazil omission. The front three never looked back from there.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Following his side's 3-2 victory over West London rivals Fulham, Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso says he's very happy Cole Palmer is playing with freedom, after the England midfielders' dominant display at Craven Cottage.

Rogers got in on the act on debut with a late run to finish Maxence Lacroix's cross just before half-time, before his flick-on released Joao Pedro to set up Palmer for a third shortly after the break.

Chelsea would have had an easier night despite the surprise absence of Moises Caicedo without a nightmare performance from goalkeeper Robert Sanchez, whose mistakes twice let Fulham back into the game.

The Spaniard, whose position as the Blues' No 1 has long been questioned, let Josh King's powerful but saveable drive in at his near post to level matters midway through the opening period before spilling a shot straight into the path of Goncalo Garcia to allow Fulham to make it 3-2.

The first taste of the Alvaro Arbeloa era suggested the Cottagers will play on the front foot regardless of opposition and they created plenty against their west London rivals - but will need to significantly improve their defensive discipline after being cut wide open for each of Chelsea's goals.

On this evidence they will have score plenty too - and could have snatched a late equaliser when Antonee Robinson horribly miscued a chip with Sanchez in no man's land. But anything less than an away victory would have been harsh on Chelsea, who ran out deserved winners thanks to their electric front three.

Arbeloa: If we play like that, we'll win games

Fulham head coach Alvaro Arbeloa on Sky Sports:

"It's a new project. Time is something we coaches don't have. But if we continue to play in that way, we're going to win a lot of games.

"I'm really happy and proud of my players, what I saw from them. This is the way I want to play. And we're going to play [this way] no matter who is in front of us."

Alonso refuses to criticise Sanchez despite errors

Chelsea head coach Xabi Alonso on Sky Sports:

"It's not about talking about individuals, their situations. It's about understanding what it takes.

"For sure, the first goal we can do better than that. But it's a process. It's day one. And normally it's easier to learn with three points."

The key moments from Craven Cottage

1: GOAL! Lacroix's header from his own half splits Fulham's midfield before Palmer finds Joao Pedro to open the scoring after just 31 seconds.

23: GOAL! King's powerful drive goes through Sanchez at his near post to level for the hosts.

41: GOAL! Rogers' late run to the back post is found by Lacroix's cross and finished off by the record signing, who is left totally unmarked.

49: GOAL! Calvin Bassey needlessly pushes up and is beaten by Rogers to a flick-on towards Joao Pedro, who tees up Palmer to add a third.

54: GOAL! Goncalo Garcia nets his own debut goal as Sanchez pushes Castagne's effort straight at the summer signing.

65: BOO! Enzo Fernandez is met by huge jeers as he replaces Romeo Lavia after his antics for Argentina against England at the World Cup.

78: BIG CHANCE! With Sanchez off his line, Robinson's attempted chip lands well wide in a huge change to equalise.

82: INJURY? Shortly after telling the bench he needs to come off and pulling up mid-dribble, Palmer is replaced by Estevao.

What's next?

Rate the players...

Sports.title: Post-Pep Premier League era begins with blast of hyper-managed shock and awe | Barney Ronay
Sports.content:
There has been something oddly narcotic and moreish about the drip‑drip of fresh Pep Guardiola content either side of the start of the new Premier League season. Eras come and go. Everything dies, baby, that’s a fact. But four‑part Amazon Prime documentaries make angels of us all.

So we have continued to feast on the Pep-at-City visuals: dead jeopardy, reheated beefs, the uplifting team talks of a departed manager to the departed players of a departed team, and moments that often feel far more gripping than the daily churn of what we must, out of habit, call the real world.

The thought occurred watching all this: has the Premier League found its Tupac? Is Pep just going to keep on doing this, dropping new material, fresh hits, posthumous platinum albums? A bald, thin charismatic man who keeps on releasing his lost tapes. We have exactly the thing, sir. Is he even actually dead?

Probably this won’t happen. But a profound absence is still a profound presence at moments like these. The ghosts continue to pull the strings. This weekend was the first of the new Premier League season. More significantly, it was also the first of the post‑Pep era.

And this has been a genuine era, 10 years in the game and an entire tactical culture shift in the making. Unsurprisingly, there was an odd sense of lightness across those nine fixtures on Friday through to Sunday, of old bonds cast aside, even a little giddiness. Suddenly dad isn’t home. The chair by the door is empty. Let’s all just rip it up a bit, shall we?

This relies on a slightly out‑of‑date notion of what Guardiola‑ism became in its later years. But the fact is, something interesting did happen in those Friday‑to‑Sunday games. Think of pure Pep-ball and what are you seeing? Possession. Cold, high‑craft control. This is a coach who famously said: “My desire is to have 100% possession,” after a 5-1 thrashing of Arsenal in Munich during which Thiago Alcântara complete 122 passes.

View image in fullscreen Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca acknowledges the fans before City’s opener against Bournemouth. Photograph: Simon Stacpoole/Offside/Getty Images

Admittedly, Guardiola was speaking out of frustration that day, talking more about not losing the ball at key moments, possession as defence. But these ideas did have a profound mimetic effect in England. During Guardiola’s decade at Manchester City the team that had the least possession in the Premier League would win, on average, only 30%-35% of games, a figure that fell as low as 28% in 2021‑22 but which had begun to pick up in the last two seasons as even City’s own version of Pep‑ball became more mixed and next‑gen.

But this weekend the opposite thing happened. In six of nine games played from Friday to Sunday one team took significantly more possession while failing to win. Liverpool had 60% possession plus 27 shots but still just scrambled a draw and looked, frankly, pretty wild. Manchester United had 71% possession and were well beaten by Hull. Tottenham had 60 % possession and lost 3-0. Nottingham Forest had 56% and lost. Sunderland had 62%, Crystal Palace 58%, and both lost.

There were three exceptions to this, all outliers in their own way. Manchester City had 66% possession and won at home against Bournemouth, but spent 84 minutes looking like they were losing. Brighton had 73% possession and beat an Aston Villa team that had made a collective decision to play with their eyes closed and their legs on the wrong way round. Arsenal dominated every metric against a promoted Coventry team that looked, frankly, a little spooked by their first sight of that fresh Everest.

So, a tiny sample size. It may mean absolutely nothing. It could get flipped on its head before we hit September. Also, it is important to note that pure possession stats have rarely dictated with any certainty who will win a game. The top teams always tend to have most of the ball, thus skewing the overall stats.

Otherwise, possession has been a far less reliable guide to victory than, say, expected goals, which speaks clearly to the effectiveness of a system. Whereas simply keeping the ball is often a sign of the opposite of good health, of football as a collective anxiety attack, out there playing with your worry beads, tramping a horseshoe shape into the grass while your opponents mass for the decisive blitzkrieg.

Quick Guide Play our football trivia game, On the ball Show The Guardian's daily football game, On the ball, is now live in the app for both iOS and Android. Can you identify the Premier League star from the clues? Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

But it wasn’t just the possession numbers that were notable this weekend. The rhythms of the matches were striking. All three Sunday games featured nine or 10 substitutes in the last 40 minutes or so, and a sense of two separate halves, of finishers brought into play, of a broken, episodic tactical to‑and‑fro in response to shifts in the scoreline and the flow. The World Cup also had that pattern. Maybe this is what football is now.

Mainly there was a striking level of targeted physicality, rehearsed blitz-transitions, groups of players running suddenly forward quickly in formation at certain triggering events. Anthony Elanga’s opener for Newcastle captured this best: 12 seconds, two passes, 70 metres covered in a single perfectly straight line, no off‑the‑cuff inventions or what you might call conventional “creativity”, but a perfect moment of planned collective intelligence and breathtaking athleticism.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

This was the pattern elsewhere too, games defined by rapid breaks, by powerful players sourced for their ability to win duels and to carry the ball, and a weekend that felt like another ratcheting up in the Premier League’s journey into hyper‑physicality.

Isn’t it a trend? Is this the next stage in the league’s narrow but furiously intense evolution? There are several managers in new jobs who have reputations for the game of sprints, blitz‑ball: most notably Matthias Jaissle at Newcastle and Roberto De Zerbi at what was, on Saturday, the least De Zerbi‑ish of Spurs, a Spurs that seemed to have absorbed only the mouse part – play dead, hide, roll over – of that fast‑breaking cat‑and‑mouse football.

There are two things worth saying about this. This is not a rejection of Guardiolaism and positional play. Keeping the ball was always about preparing for the moments when you don’t have it. Guardiola’s later Manchester City team would often win by direct means.

But pure possession can also be boringly risk-averse, a kind of footballing atrophy where everyone just sits quivering on the touchline like a swarm of beached jellyfish at dusk. The spectacle is more gripping when the emphasis is on those transitions either side of the passing patterns.

More specifically, it is also an interesting development for Pep’s successor at City, Enzo Maresca, Coolio to his Tupac, whose methods are still very much pure Pep origins, based in control of the ball and rigid positionism, like the last soldier still fighting the second world war from inside a bush on Iwo Jima in 1976.

View image in fullscreen Newcastle’s Anthony Elanga celebrates his superb strike against Liverpool. Photograph: Simon Davies/ProSports/Shutterstock

Is Maresca ready for this? Is he even ahead of it? He gave a televised interview at the weekend where he spoke about the tension between control and risk, possession and creativity, and where he defined players being encouraged to run into unexpected positions as “chaos”. On Monday morning there were headlines describing the Premier League weekend in those terms. But this isn’t chaos. We’ve seen chaos. We’ve seen attack ships on fire off the shoulder of Orion, jinking wingers, dogs of war, hitting the space, Lee Chapman, Rod Wallace and Eric Cantona making heavy metal music with two bass guitars and an antique viola. You want chaos. We can give you chaos.

What the Premier League brought at the weekend, the quick breaks, the freedom to attack at selected moments, was more a kind of hyper-managed shock and awe, targeted speed and physicality born out of calculated risk, numbers, data, heavy briefings.

It was also exciting to watch, which is no bad thing in the world’s most tightly contested, space‑averse league. No doubt there will be tightening, a reaction to the reaction, instant counter‑moves and contingency planning. August can also be odd and silly season-ish, the dog days of a World Cup summer. But it did at times feel as if we were in a post‑something moment. If not quite post‑Pep, whose influence will continue to loom, a tactical Machiavelli with plenty of tapes still left in the vault.

Sports.title: ‘Enough is enough’: players pile pressure on under-fire Gianni Infantino to resign
Sports.content:
A group of influential current and former footballers have added to the pressure on Gianni Infantino by calling for change at the top of Fifa, saying “enough is enough” in a statement shared widely across social media.

The intervention is particularly significant given some of those behind its circulation have undertaken ambassadorial activities for Fifa as part of its “Fifa Legends” programme. Among them is the former Manchester United and Arsenal defender Mikaël Silvestre, who also sits on the governing body’s 16-member players’ voice panel designed to assist with anti-racism initiatives.

Others to have shared the statement include the England defender Lucy Bronze, the former England keeper David James and the France 1998 World Cup winner Emmanuel Petit. More signatories are expected to follow in a concerted reaction to Infantino’s ill-fated attempt to sell stakes in the World Cup.

“We share the exact same concerns as the millions of fans around the world,” part of the statement read. “Like them, we have watched the game we love drift away from its core values under Fifa’s current leadership. For too long, we’ve seen major decisions taken without players being consulted or considered, and without any regard for the fans who sustain the sport.

Quick Guide Play our football trivia game, On the ball Show The Guardian's daily football game, On the ball, is now live in the app for both iOS and Android. Can you identify the Premier League star from the clues? Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

“Change is necessary. Power has blurred the current leadership’s ability to distinguish between its own interests and what is best for football. Recent events have made silence impossible. Enough is enough.”

The group called for efforts to “reshape the future of our sport”, adding: “There are good people within Fifa who want to rebuild trust, but a new era requires a structured change: a real, direct say for players and fans in how football is run. Those who step on to the pitch and those who sit in the stands deserve a genuine voice to help reshape football’s future together.”

Infantino has resisted calls to resign and spent Saturday at a youth tournament in the Dominican Republic, attempting to smooth relations with some of the smaller Caribbean member associations on whose support his fate may hinge.

One former player with a different perspective on Infantino is the former Real Madrid, Barcelona and Chelsea striker Samuel Eto’o, who is president of the Cameroonian football federation. In an interview with CNN, Eto’o said Infantino had not committed any missteps and called for the Fifa Forward Enterprise scheme to be put back on the table if Infantino is re-elected next March. He said the money from FFE would “reset the balance of power” in football and ensure African countries avoided losing top players to other national teams.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“I don’t think that [Infantino] has done anything wrong,” he said. “All of this has happened because there’s an election coming out, that’s all there is.

“I want to see all of my colleagues, all of the presidents, re-reading the project. After president Infantino is re-elected, we will have the strength to ask for this project to be put back on the table for discussion. I remain convinced that, if there is a democratic vote, this project will be adopted because it’s good for the majority.”

Sports.title: San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York pleads no contest after arrest at Ohio trailer park
Sports.content:
The San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York has pleaded no contest to two criminal charges after being arrested at an Ohio trailer park over the weekend.

KRON4 News in San Francisco reported that York was initially arrested on suspicion of engaging in prostitution but that count was amended to a charge of disorderly conduct. He was also charged with possessing criminal tools.

A no contest plea is not an admission of guilt but the defendant in question does accept the punishment for the alleged crimes in question. York was sentenced to a day in jail for each count to be served concurrently and was released on Monday morning. He was also fined a total of $1,150 and ordered to complete an online course. The arrest report does not specify what the criminal tools were in York’s case.

According to the New York Post, court documents say York responded to an advert on a website and “arranged to have sexual activity with [a] female in exchange for $140.” York was arrested later arrested at a trailer park in East Palestine, Ohio, on Sunday morning. The East Palestine Police Department and the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force were involved in the arrest. York, 46, was born and raised in Youngstown, a 30-minute drive from East Palestine and still has a home in the area.

York is the nephew of former 49ers majority owner Edward J DeBartolo Jr. York took day to day control of the 49ers in 2008 when he became the team’s CEO. After acquiring his mother’s shares, he became the team’s principal owner in 2024.

“As this is a legal matter, which has been resolved, we will not be providing any further comment at this time,” the 49ers said in a statement. The NFL said in a statement that it is “aware of the matter which will be reviewed under the personal conduct policy.”

Since York took over as CEO, the 49ers have reached three Super Bowls but lost each time.

He also owns stakes in the Premier League’s Leeds United and Scotland’s Rangers through 49ers Enterprises. He filed for divorce from his wife, Danielle, in May.

Sports.title: Glaring weakness in goal remains but early signs Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea should be fun | Jonathan Wilson
Sports.content:
After a weekend on which pretty much every potential challenger to Arsenal had demonstrated their flaws, there was a sense, perhaps even a need, for Chelsea to emerge as a serious contender – if only to prevent the title race becoming a procession. And while they were far from flawless, there were at least some indications that they could mount some kind of challenge.

They looked extremely dangerous in the final third, and Cole Palmer was involved in all three Chelsea goals, perhaps benefiting from a first summer off in three years. But they were rather less impressive through midfield or at the back, despite Josh Acheampong’s all-action performance, while goalkeeper remains the problem it has been since Thibaut Courtois left.

It could easily have gone wrong: in the final quarter-hour; Antonee Robinson lofted an effort wide with Robert Sánchez off his line and Ryan Sessegnon smacked a shot from a narrow angle straight at the Spanish keeper. But neither opportunity was taken and so Chelsea got Xabi Alonso’s reign off to a winning start.

At this stage, performances and learning the system are probably the most important thing, but if there is to be some sort of dart at the title, results matter if only to keep Chelsea somewhere near the race until the point at which Alonso’s principles are absorbed and they do find something close to top form.

Perhaps what’s most striking, though, is how different the approach is to Enzo Maresca’s. Where Maresca prioritised control to often stultifying effect, Alonso’s game is based on rapid turnovers and transition. It’ll probably settle down as his systems become deeper rooted but there was a sense of recklessness at times to their play. It was harum-scarum, end-to-end, thrilling stuff, which is all very well to watch, and may even come as a relief after the sterility of Maresca and the shambles of Liam Rosenior, but may not be great for consistency or sustained runs of form.

Alonso could hardly have dreamed of a quicker start, João Pedro putting Chelsea ahead after 31 seconds, matching the record for the quickest goal scored in the reign of a Premier League manager, David Unsworth’s goal – also against Fulham – in David Moyes’s first game in charge of Everton in March 2002. João Pedro had scored eight goals in eight pre-season games; and this a player Maresca told not to focus on scoring goals shortly before he went on a run of seven games without a shot. That was a first indication of a forward line starting to show signs of an impressive understanding. All three combined for the third goal, Morgan Rogers flicking on for João Pedro who held the ball up for the overlapping Palmer to slip his shot cleverly between Bernd Leno’s legs.

View image in fullscreen João Pedro (second from left), Cole Palmer (second from right) and Morgan Rogers (right) combined impressively on their first outing as Chelsea’s front three. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

Alonso’s first go at finding a pattern amid the legions of players assembled by BlueCo involved a midfield made up of two players who, despite being at Chelsea together for the past three years, had never previously been paired in the centre: Roméo Lavia and Reece James. It was not entirely by choice: Moisés Caicedo was left out as a precaution while Enzo Fernández remained on the bench until the 65th minute as Manchester City continue their pursuit of him. And it didn’t entirely work. It may look a defensively robust pairing but there were long spells when Fulham had control of midfield.

A feature of Alonso’s approach, and one of the reasons it takes time and commitment to learn – qualities that were notably lacking at Real Madrid – is that players can emerge in unexpected positions. Which doesn’t entirely explain how the right-sided centre-back Maxence Lacroix found himself running on to Palmer’s pass in the Fulham box but, having got there, he demonstrated great poise to skip around Jorge Cuenca and cut the ball back for Rogers to score his first Chelsea goal.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Yet for all that was new and positive, and for all that was raw and unintentionally exciting, there was one glaring and inexplicably familiar failing for Chelsea: in goal. Sánchez’s positioning seemed very strange for Fulham’s first goal, drilled in at his near post by Josh King (who also benefited from a bizarrely ineffectual attempt to track from Rogers), and while it was a far less glaring error, he pushed Timothy Castagne’s shot straight to Gonzalo García for Fulham’s second.

Although Sánchez doesn’t perhaps quite deserve the negative reputation he has among certain Chelsea fans, he did make a league-high five errors leading to goals in 2024-25 and three last season. It remains mystifying that a club that signs wide forwards by the dozen continues to refuse to invest in a top-class goalkeeper. That may yet hold Chelsea back.

Generally, though, Alonso can be satisfied with his start: a win against Chelsea’s local rivals, an impressive display from Acheampong, a number of fluent interactions from his front three and plenty of signs of his system beginning to take hold, with a few obvious improvements to be made. And from the point of view of fans and casual observers, it looks like it should be fun.

Sports.title: Football transfer rumours: Manchester City and Spurs chase Cody Gakpo?
Sports.content:
After Aston Villa endured a day to forget on the Premier League’s opening weekend, it only stands to reason that they must sign players, and ideally good ones. Milan wide man Rafael Leão has flirted with a move to England in the past and he could be the answer to Unai Emery’s attacking troubles, if that answer is not named Nicolas Jackson or Jean-Philippe Mateta.

And Villa are not just concentrating their efforts on reshaping their forward line. Rangers’ Nicolas Raskin could fit the bill in midfield, where they looked light in the shellacking by Brighton, while Club Brugge centre-back Joel Ordóñez looks to be coming in after Southampton pushed back on Taylor Harwood-Bellis.

The Chelsea head coach Xabi Alonso has repeatedly refused to rule out an exit for Enzo Fernández, and it seems Manchester City have been listening the whole time and they could try again for the popular Argentinian. The Blues still like Alex Scott as a midfield replacement, though time may be running out to snap up the Bournemouth star. It’s claimed Chelsea have seen three bids for Scott rejected this summer, so could turn their attention to Real Madrid’s Eduardo Camavinga instead.

City also appear to have joined Tottenham in their admiration of Liverpool’s Cody Gakpo – though without any incoming forwards at Anfield, the Dutchman probably won’t be going anywhere. The Reds are struggling to progress on a deal for Bradley Barcola, but have been linked with Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara, who would plug an important gap in the middle of Andoni Iraola’s side.

Down in the Championship, Sheffield United have drawn their first two league games 0-0, so Chris Wilder has clearly identified central defence as an area that needs strengthening. Adam Webster is a free agent after leaving Brighton and is of interest to the Blades.

Wrexham, meanwhile, want to sign Pavel Sulc, who is valued at around £10m by his current employers Lyon. The Welsh club have obviously spent big on their French scouting budget this summer given they also covet Jacques Ekomié, the Angers left-back, though may face competition from West Ham. The Hammers are preparing for the possibility of Brentford snapping up El Hadji Malick Diouf.

And could Dele Alli be set for another return to Serie A? Monza apparently want to take a gamble on the midfielder, who has been training with West Ham this summer. The former Tottenham prodigy is now 30 and was last seen in March 2025 getting sent off on his only appearance for Como.

Sports.title: Manchester City agree £34m deal for Allan Elias as Nico González nears Newcastle move
Sports.content:
Manchester City have agreed a €37.5m plus €2.5m (£34m) deal for the Palmeiras winger Allan Elias, with the club also in advanced negotiations to sell Nico González to Newcastle.

The 22-year-old Elias – known as Allan – made his senior debut for Palmeiras last year and has made 96 appearances for the club, scoring nine goals and making 12 assists. He is yet to play for Brazil.

Allan’s arrival will clear the way for the sale of his countryman Savinho to Tottenham for £75m plus £10m. Spurs also want to sign City’s Omar Marmoush, with the fee for the forward expected to be £75m. While Savinho has informed Enzo Maresca he wishes to leave, City’s manager said on Friday that the Egyptian had not done so.

González is expected to be sold to Newcastle for a fee in the region of £50m, a price almost identical to the £49.8m City paid Porto for the midfielder in the January 2025 window. Newcastle are understood to be confident of signing the 24-year-old.

The money from his proposed sale may be used by City to make an official bid for Chelsea’s Enzo Fernández. While Chelsea set a deadline for any offer for the midfielder of 14 August, which was not met, City may test their resolve, as the player is open to a move and a reunion with his former coach Maresca.
