City have so far made only one senior signing in the window, the £116m purchase of Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest, but are close to sealing the €95m (£81.4m) plus €5m deal for Ayyoub Bouaddi. The Lille midfielder is thought to have undergone his medical on Monday.

City are also thought to retain an interest in Liverpool’s wide forward Cody Gakpo with Spurs also closely monitoring the Dutchman’s availability. If Liverpool sign Bradley Barcola and another winger, they may be open to Gakpo’s departure. Liverpool are pondering a third bid for Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh while they continue to talk with Paris Saint-Germain over Ibrahim Mbaye and Barcola.

Sports.title: Women’s Super League 2026-27 preview No 4: Brighton
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 6th (NB: this is not necessarily Sophie Downey’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 7th

Prospects

A first FA Cup final was a historic moment for Brighton. Despite losing to Manchester City at Wembley, it will have filled Dario Vidosic and his team with the belief that they are on the right track.

It has been a summer of relative stability on the south coast. While there are seven new faces, departures have been limited to four. The arrivals of Lia Wälti and Gabby George bring vast experience and increased defensive acumen to the ranks while the Republic of Ireland’s Emily Murphy and Poland’s Nadia Krezyman are young attacking talents who have started to make a name for themselves.

Brighton’s inconsistency was their downfall last season. They were seriously hampered by the lack of an out-and-out centre-forward after the anterior cruciate ligament injury suffered by the Arsenal loanee and England Euros hero Michelle Agyemang. Kiko Seike finished as their highest scorer in the league with eight and she was their only representative in the Women’s Super League’s top 20 for goals and assists. That problem remains unsolved and will surely be a focus for the remainder of the transfer window.

The conclusion of their season certainly gave Brighton something to build on over the summer. They secured an impressive league victory over City and a draw against Arsenal and will hope to outdo the latter when they host Renée Slegers’s side at Crawley in their opener on 6 September. That on paper is the toughest of Brighton’s opening four fixtures.

Off-field picture

Pinterest has become the first solo sponsor of the women’s team with a four-year partnership. The deal pivots around the concept of ‘matchday style’, bringing to life the way fans show support for their team. Plans continue for the construction of Europe’s first purpose-built women’s football stadium. Located next to the Amex Stadium, the hope is it will open for the start of the 2030-2031 campaign.

The manager

Now entering his third season, Vidosic is the second-longest serving manager in the WSL, a period that has brought much-needed stability to the club and allowed the Croatian-born Australian time to fully implement his aggressive pressing and possession-based style. He has been on a journey, developing an out-of-possession style to help his team deal with some of the bigger clubs in the WSL The 39-year-old has never hidden from his desire to bring silverware to Brighton and last season’s FA Cup final will have given him a taste of the steps required to realise that ambition.

Star signing

The acquisition of Wälti remains one of the biggest coups of the summer. The 33-year-old Switzerland captain returns to England after a year in Italy with Juventus, bringing with her a wealth of experienceand, from her seven years with Arsenal, a WSL title and a Champions League winners’ medal. Wälti’s technical ability is second-to-none, as is a level of intelligence that allows her to dictate play from the middle of the park. She leads by example and guided Switzerland to the quarter-finals at Euro 2025. If Wälti can stay injury-free, she could play a significant role this season.

View image in fullscreen Lia Wälti should bring quality and know-how to Brighton. Photograph: Neil Holmes/Focus Images Ltd/Shutterstock

Stat attack

Brighton had a finishing problem in 2025-26. Not in terms of hitting the target – no other side had as strong a shot accuracy – but only three teams converted a lower proportion of their on-target efforts. If the Seagulls can fire towards the corners of the goal rather than close to the goalkeeper, they could fly this season.

Set for a breakthrough

Sophie Peskett has already made history when in 2021, aged 18, she became Ipswich’s first professional player. The winger spent the best part of seven years at Ipswich, making 127 appearances and helping them earn promotion to the WSL 2 twice. Now 23, it would have been a big decision for her to leave, but Brighton seems like a sensible next step. A nifty player with an eye for goal, Peskett will prove useful to Brighton’s attacking output.

What they say …

“Brighton is not a team that has to hide. In the last couple of years, they’ve been able to hurt the big teams in many moments, and they reached the FA Cup final last season as well. We’re not going to be favourites in every single game, but that’s a nice position to be in.” – Lia Wälti

Where are they playing their home games?

Brighton will continue to play most of their home games at Crawley’s Broadfield Stadium although four of their six opening home fixtures will be at the Amex. The club have added an Amex 4-Match Pack to their ticketing options, priced at £45 for adults. The club have also launched ‘Built For Her’, their dedicated women’s football membership option that offers a bundle of exclusive perks as they look to build their fanbase before the stadium move.

Sports.title: Liverpool are still haunted by the mess of last summer | Jonathan Wilson
Sports.content:
The good news for Liverpool is that, Arsenal aside, every other team with vague title aspirations who played over the weekend looked undercooked, and that Andoni Iraola’s men did, in the end, come away from Newcastle with a point. But the vulnerability to the counter that undermined them so often last season has not gone away, and nor have they suddenly found a new creativity under Iraola.

The main theme of the first three days of the new season was the value of stability. Manchester City under a new manager were poor and fortunate to overcome Bournemouth. Aston Villa, after big changes of players and backroom staff, were hammered at Brighton. Tottenham, midway through yet another overhaul, were dismal in losing at Brentford. Manchester United at least provided a degree of stability by looking very much like the United of the past decade in their defeat to Hull.

Liverpool, for much of the first 96 minutes of their fixture at St James’ Park, looked like joining the list of challengers struggling to emerge from a summer of churn. Arne Slot spent much of last season complaining about how opponents always scored with their first chance and about Liverpool’s inability to deal with direct attacks, and as Anthony Elanga put Newcastle ahead, it seemed that not much had changed. Joe Willock’s goal to restore the Newcastle lead was much the same: opponents running at pace through vacant space.

What is odd is how pressing the need for a replacement for Fabinho has been since the defensive midfielder left in 2023. Even as Liverpool won the league under Slot in 2024-25, the discussion was of how the squad needed of an overhaul, and how a dedicated holding player to operate alongside Ryan Gravenberch was a priority. Which was what made the spending spree of last summer so surprising: it wasn’t so much who came in as who didn’t.

Without a holding midfielder, the flaws of the centre of defence, where Virgil van Dijk’s lack of pace on the turn is becoming increasingly obvious, are magnified. Liverpool could perhaps get away with it were he prepared to operate 10 yards higher in possession but the 35-year-old, aware of his ageing legs and worried about balls played in behind him, instinctively drops deeper, giving opponents just the sort of opportunities that Yoane Wissa kept exploiting on Sunday.

Iraola insisted it wasn’t “just about personnel” – which itself seemed an implicit acknowledgment that it is in part about personnel. Had he scored, Iraola said, everybody would have praised Gravenberch, who had advanced to the edge of the Newcastle box in the attack that led to the first Liverpool concession. “I don’t want us to take that from his game but we have to adapt as a team to these situations,” said Iraola. “We have to know these situations can happen.”

Of Newcastle’s second goal, he said: “It wasn’t like they caught us by surprise. We should compete for the first ball and probably make a foul – be a bit more aggressive against the ball carrier. There were different reasons for both the goals which happened in transition. We have been preparing in the week for these transitions but there’s a reason why Newcastle are so good at them. It’s not just because one person is playing there. It’s something we have to correct between a lot of players.”

But conceding on the break isn’t the only familiar issue for Liverpool. Their full-backs, Jeremie Frimpong and Milos Kerkez, were unconvincing. Alexander Isak, booed throughout by the home fans, rarely looked dangerous in the first full 90 minutes he has completed since his British record transfer from Newcastle last summer. Florian Wirtz produced a characteristic performance full of neat touches and little incision.

Iraola’s career suggests it often takes him time to instil his ideas at clubs. There is no reason for panic. Liverpool at least had the resilience to come back and pinch the draw. It’s not like any side other than Arsenal has looked particularly impressive. But perhaps there does need to be a reconsideration of what has gone before.

The familiar narrative is that Slot drove the car that Jürgen Klopp had put together to a league title and was then found wanting. But while the Dutchman cannot escape blame for last season, an equally valid interpretation might be that Slot coaxed an ageing team to an unexpected league title. Then, with an overhaul badly needed – Jamie Carragher wasn’t alone in speaking towards the end of that season of Liverpool needing half a dozen new players – he was let down by those charged with recruitment.

Michael Edwards left his role as chief executive for football at Fenway Sports Group, which owns Liverpool, in July, but the mess caused by last summer’s spree endures. Of the six most expensive signings of last summer for a combined fee of around £410m (about $560m), the only one who has looked remotely impressive, Hugo Ekitike, is still out for months with a ruptured achilles. Rarely has so much been spent in football to such destructive effect.

Sports.title: Tottenham get Cody Gakpo boost as Liverpool push for Bradley Barcola
Sports.content:
Tottenham get Cody Gakpo boost as Liverpool push for Bradley Barcola

Tottenham are still pushing to sign Liverpool winger Cody Gakpo, talkSPORT understands.

Liverpool's stance had been that they were reluctant to sell Gakpo, however that could change to help fund their quest to sign Paris Saint-Germain's Bradley Barcola.

4 Gakpo could be heading to Tottenham before the window closes next week Credit: AFP

The France international remains the Reds’ top summer transfer target.

But they are yet to find a breakthrough in negotiations with the Champions League holders.

However, PSG insiders expect Barcola to leave before next week's transfer deadline and talks with Liverpool continue.

A deal to bring the 23-year-old to Anfield could lead to a domino effect regarding Gakpo.

Which clubs are interested in Cody Gakpo?

Manchester City are also interested in Gakpo as they look to bolster their attack.

But sources have played down the chances of the Dutchman moving to the Etihad.

talkSPORT told you last month how the 27-year-old is on Spurs' radar as they plot an audacious move.

And it is now believed that Gakpo - capable of playing as a left winger of striker - is understood to be making the move to north London.

He could be the latest forward to join Roberto De Zerbi's project as Spurs close in on the signing of Citizens winger Savinho in an £85million deal.

Savinho isn't the only City star that Spurs are keen on, with striker Omar Marmoush also in advanced talks to head down south.

4 Barcola has been Liverpool's top target throughout the summer Credit: Getty

Having strengthened their midfield with the £100m addition of Sandro Tonali and £85m arrival of Mateus Fernandes, Tottenham are now prioritising their attack.

Spurs could be set for a new-look front three following their 3-0 defeat at Brentford in their opening Premier League fixture.

Question marks remain surrounding the future of centre-forward Richarlison, while Mikey Moore could be heading to Germany to link up with FC Koln on loan.

While the duo drew a blank in west London over the weekend, Gakpo opened his account for the new season in fine fashion.

He fired in a long-range stunner in Liverpool's 2-2 draw away at Newcastle.

While fellow Spurs targets Savinho and Marmoush played no part in City's 2-1 comeback victory over Bournemouth.

4 Savinho and Marmoush could be joining Spurs in a mega double deal

What has been said about Cody Gakpo leaving Liverpool?

Despite heavy interest in Gakpo, talkSPORT co-host Jeff Stelling doesn't believe that Liverpool should be parting ways with the ex-PSV man.

Speaking on the Sports Breakfast show, Stelling was asked about City's interest in the Netherlands international.

To which he said: "Liverpool are not going to sell Cody Gakpo to Man City, they're just not.

"Liverpool need to bring players in, not get rid at the moment. And where is Cody Gakpo going to play for them?"

On Spurs' interest in Gakpo, Stelling again stressed that the Merseyside outfit should not be entertaining any bids.

He remarked: "I don't think [so], I thought Cody Gakpo was Liverpool's best player at Newcastle at the weekend.

4 Gakpo has scored 51 goals in 181 games for Liverpool in all competitions since joining in January 2023 Credit: Getty

"Why would you want to sell him? And why would he want to leave Liverpool to go to Spurs?

"I don't get it at all, so no, I don't really see that there's a race for Cody Gakpo."

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso told he must make ruthless decision to make Chelsea’s title dream come true
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso told he must make ruthless decision to make Chelsea’s title dream come true

Chelsea will not win the Premier League title this season with Robert Sanchez in goal - they have to sign a new goalkeeper.

That's the opinion of Jamie Carragher and Gary Neville, who think the Blues have no choice but to act in the transfer market.

3 Sanchez made a huge error to hand a goal to Fulham at Craven Cottage Credit: AFP

Sanchez started for Xabi Alonso's side in their Premier League opener on Monday night, as they beat Fulham 3-2 in a thriller.

However, things weren't all positive in the victory, as the Spanish goalkeeper made a huge error to let in a goal.

Fulham's Josh King burst into the box on the right and unleashed a powerful low strike that headed straight for Sanchez.

The keeper was expected to make a simple save, but he instead seemed to dive too late and let the ball through his hands.

That has led to some backlash - and speaking post-match, Carragher called on Alonso to make a needed change in goal.

Chelsea must drop Sanchez to win title

He believes that it will be 'impossible for Chelsea to win the title' with Sanchez starting and made reference to other successful teams, pointing out that their silverware stemmed from their No.1.

"Alisson comes in for Liverpool, they win the league," Carragher started on Sky Sports. "Arsenal don't win the league if they have Aaron Ramsdale in goal and not David Raya.

"So, one of the biggest reasons why Arsenal won the league last year was Raya, they wouldn't have won it without him.

"You can go back through history and every team that wins the league, 99 times out of 100, the manager has gone and got a good goalkeeper to win him the league."

Neville agreed and added: "It's a massive personality, a massive character and a great goalkeeper that wins a league title.

3 Sanchez conceded two and looked nervy throughout the match on Monday Credit: Getty

"I just think that the back line of Chelsea's isn't perfect, but if they have a goalkeeper behind that's making them a little more nervous, it's going to be a bigger problem.

"The reality of it is, Chelsea do need a new goalkeeper and it's one thing I'm surprised they haven't dealt with in this transfer window... that's the last piece."

Danny Murphy: The keeper's a problem

Dropping Sanchez is something that talkSPORT's Danny Murphy thinks is a must for Chelsea this season too.

But he also questioned the Blues' defence after they conceded two goals and other big chances to Fulham on Monday.

One thing he didn't have an issue with though, was the attack of Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro, who all scored and combined for five goal contributions in total.

Murphy said on talkSPORT commentary from Craven Cottage: “Chelsea’s front line at times was unplayable.

3 Alonso has been told to bring in another goalkeeper to replace Sanchez Credit: Getty

"It's going to be really difficult, however good your back line is and whatever quality you've got there to keep those three quiet.

“Because if one of them's not at it, the other two are more than capable of winning games on their own.

"They really are a brilliant three and it's going to be interesting to see how Chelsea evolve in terms of those wing-back areas because they can have a crucial role in feeding those three."

Murphy then added: "Defensively, there are problems, the keeper’s a problem, of course he is. And I'm not convinced by the three centre-halves after tonight either...

“I know they've got other players to come back in, but I've said it before and I'll say again there’s not that one standout centre-half who you think he’s the leader.

"He's the one that's gonna organise the others, he's the one that, in times of difficulty, he's the one that will keep us going. He's the one that will carry us through, calmly get us back into games.

“Lots of excitement at Chelsea this season. I think they'll have games where they're really hurting score lots of goals, but as for title contenders, no.”

Sports.title: Leicester to break long-standing transfer record with new signing that topples EFL cult hero
Sports.content:
Leicester to break long-standing transfer record with new signing that topples EFL cult hero

Leicester City are reportedly closing in on signing Finnish centre-back Ilari Kangasniemi.

The Foxes have agreed a £2million deal to sign Kangasniemi from Finnish outfit Inter Turku, which will be a new transfer record in the Veikkausliiga.



3 Leicester are set to sign Kangasniemi (right) in a Finnish top-flight record deal Credit: Shutterstock

According to local outlet Yle Urheilu, the 19-year-old defender will arrive in England and undergo a medical imminently.

He is expected to complete his move to Leicester this week.

Kangasniemi joined Inter Turku last summer after previously playing for Inter Milan's youth team for a year from 2024.

The Finland U21 international played 28 times for Inter Milan's U18s before heading back to his home country.



He has featured 32 times in all competitions for Inter Turku since his move, with six appearances coming in qualifying for the Europa Conference League this summer.

New transfer record

Should Kangasniemi join Leicester as expected, he would become the most expensive ever transfer in the Finnish top flight.



The current record is long-standing, with EFL cult hero and Norwich legend Teemu Pukki holding it for 15 years.

Pukki's £1.5m move to German side Schalke from HJK Helsinki in 2011 is the largest ever deal in the Veikkausliiga.



But the Foxes are now set to topple the former Premier League striker with the signing of Kangasniemi.

He will become Russell Martin's tenth signing of the summer so far, amid a major squad turnover for the club.

3 Ex-Norwich star Pukki is going to be toppled as the most expensive Veikkausliiga player Credit: Getty

Leicester's latest move

Leicester are bringing in Kangasniemi amid a nightmare start to their League One season following back-to-back relegations.



They drew with Notts County in their opener before losing 2-1 at home to Burton Albion in their second game on Saturday.

That has led to some backlash already coming manager Martin's way - but he's going to add another new face to his squad.

Speaking in recent days, Martin hinted that he wanted to sign a new defender, as well as multiple other players.

He said: "I think we'll probably - without giving really specific positions - I still think we'll end up with three or four players coming in the building before the end of the window.



"I think we have to strengthen in certain areas that we don't feel as strong as others. So nothing's really changed."

3 Leicester boss Martin wants to sign multiple new players before the deadline Credit: Getty

The Foxes take on Ipswich on Tuesday night in the Carabao Cup, with a clash against MK Dons coming up in League One on Saturday.

And Kangasniemi could well be involved should his record transfer get over the line in time this week.

Sports.title: Man City consider shock move for Liverpool star wanted by Premier League rival
Sports.content:
Manchester City are exploring a shock move to sign Liverpool star Cody Gakpo.

Gakpo has been linked with a departure from Anfield throughout the summer transfer window, with Tottenham interested.

3 Gakpo is contracted at Liverpool until 2030 Credit: AFP

But a new club has entered the race for the Netherlands forward in Man City, who are a little light up front, the Athletic reports.

It's understood City have made contact with Gakpo's camp, although Liverpool do not plan to sell the 27-year-old.

He is contracted at Anfield until the summer of 2030, having signed a new deal last summer and the Reds would only consider a sale if they were to add new forwards to their ranks.

City's pursuit of Gakpo comes as they look set to say goodbye to two forwards of their own; Savinho and Omar Marmoush.

Both Savinho and Marmoush are closing in on moves to Tottenham, with City believed to be after £150million for the pair.

Spurs want to sign Gakpo as they look to revamp their forward line, which looked threadbare during their 3-0 defeat at Brentford in their opening match of the season last weekend.

Man City are set to have a busy end to the summer window with the signings of Morocco midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi and Brazilian Allan Elias from Palmeiras.

Gakpo in demand

Subject to huge criticism for his performances, Gakpo endured a tough season last term.

In a campaign which was hugely frustrating for Liverpool, the winger could only manage nine goals in all competitions, having scored 18 the previous season.

Liverpool limped into the Champions League spots and many fans called on the club to sell the 54-cap Dutch international.

3 Gakpo had a good game in what was a far from perfect performance by Liverpool Credit: Getty

However, the interest from two of the Premier League's 'Big Six' may have caught them by surprise and perhaps the critical Liverpool fans may now have changed their stance.

Gakpo got off the mark for the season in Liverpool's opening match, scoring the team's first goal during their 2-2 draw at Newcastle last weekend.

When asked about Gakpo's future, Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola said before the game: "Cody is performing really well. I think he has been training very well from the first day and understanding everything we need from his position.

"When you talk to him, you can feel that he understands the game and he is very smart. He has been one of our best players in the friendlies and performing very well.

"I cannot tell you the starting XI, the players don't know it, but he is definitely in a great spot."

Liverpool's transfer business

The two-time Premier League winners have signed Vicor Munoz and Ronald Araujo this summer, while Jeremy Jacquet arrived after the deal to bring him in was put in place during the January transfer window.

3 Iraola is seeking reinforcements to his thin-looking Liverpool squad Credit: AFP

But they're hoping to do more business before the deadline on September 1 with Paris Saint-Germain duo Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye rated.

Meanwhile, Liverpool have had two bids for Brighton winger Yankuba Minteh rejected, with their next offer set to be their final one.

Gakpo joined Liverpool from Eredivisie club PSV Eindhoven with the Reds hijacking Manchester United's move for the player.

He has 51 goals and 23 assists in 181 appearances for Liverpool, winning the Premier League and Carabao Cup during his three-and-a-half years at the club.

Sports.title: Simon Jordan warns Ian Wright over ‘uninformed’ and ‘biased’ take on Gabriel Martinelli saga
Sports.content:
Simon Jordan has suggested Ian Wright would be in better mind to keep quiet about his claims about Arsenal's treatment of Gabriel Martinelli.

Wright admitted he felt 'uncomfortable' with how the forward's future is being dealt with at the Emirates Stadium.



3 Wright says he has behind-the-scenes knowledge of what is happening with Martinelli's transfer saga Credit: Getty

The Brazil international is set to join Saudi club Al Hilal having turned down a move to join Turkish champions Galatasaray earlier this summer.

The winger was omitted from the matchday squad for both the Community Shield victory over Manchester City and the Premier League opening night win against Coventry City.

Instead, summer signing Christos Tzolis featured in the starting lineup on the left-wing in both clashes.



Speaking after the game against the Sky Blues, Wright voiced his frustration on Sky Sports, saying: "With respect to Martinelli and the way he's being treated at the moment, it really makes me uncomfortable.

"He always gives 100 per cent. We're not saying he's the greatest, but he's come up with some big moments for Arsenal in big games, and the way he's being treated at the end here.



"I know they might want him out, and there's a lot of guys saying it's time for him to move on, but there are ways of doing that should suit him as well."

Wright elaborated on the cold shoulder treatment Martinelli is receiving, adding: "Not being in the squad tonight, not being spoken to, he doesn't know what's going on."



He also added he had direct knowledge of the situation, saying: "Yes I do know this. Not being involved in the Community Shield squad, not being involved tonight, he doesn't know what's happening, and he's got a year left.

"If you bring Vinicius Jr, Martinelli can say to himself, 'okay they've brought him in and Tzsolis, so I might be third option'. But if you're bringing in Tzolis and Noni Madueke's there, you're thinking to yourself, 'I've got something to offer here'.

"So for him to be nowhere near it just makes me feel a bit sad for him. I think he's done enough in this squad to be treated with a bit more respect than he's being shown at the moment."

3 Martinelli has played 278 times for Arsenal in seven season Credit: Getty



Jordan fires back

Former Crystal Palace owner Jordan expressed his confusion over the Wright's comments, beginning on White and Jordan: "I don't imagine it's particularly informed.

"Unless he's across the exact details of Arsenal's behaviour, and the players' perspective, which he may well be if he's indicating it appears that he's well aware of the players' perspective.

"If so, maybe he'd be better served to perhaps keep his own counsel, because I'm not entirely sure what it's got to do with him. I'm not entirely sure why he would think that Arsenal and Mikel Arteta aren't capable of managing their players in an appropriate fashion.

"I don't know what expertise he has in this, in his varied career of football administration that gives him this credence, besides the fact that people like Ian Wright and they take him at face value.



"I know him, so I have a different view of him. But the bottom line is, I think his opinion is rather uninformed and rather biased, and one-dimensional, because I don't think there's any indication that Arsenal don't conduct themselves properly."

The fee for Martinelli joining Al Hilal would push the Gunners' summer sales into record territory, surpassing Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain's £40million departure to Liverpool in 2017.

3 Arteta has frozen out Martinelli at the start of the season Credit: Getty

Jordan continued his defence of the Gunners' management, as he said: "What he's indicating is that this football club which is considered one of the statesmen of English football, isn't acting properly. And I think that's a rather strong allegation and I think he should wind his neck in a little bit.



"But maybe he thinks he's in a position because of his new contract with Sky that people are going to hang on his every word.

"Guess what Arsenal do? They pay the player's wages. So they've earned the privilege of either accepting a transfer for him, or while he's not paying, he'll be getting his £100,000 a week or whatever it is.

"Arsenal will, I suspect, conduct themselves appropriately, and have we got any evidence to suggest otherwise?"

Ian Wright defence

Martin Keown stepped in to partially side with his former teammate, noting: "I don't think he needs to be battering Ian Wright. Ian loves the players — he's shown that — and maybe he's just taken it a step too far."



Jordan held firm on his stance: "I think battering him is not what we're doing here."

He added: "I'm holding him to account for the things that he said. If you want to characterise what I've said, that's up to you.

"What he has spoken about is the football club that he played for, and that you [Keown] played for, which you would think conducts itself appropriately."

Sports.title: Nottingham Forest close in on Liam Delap signing as they win race against Premier League rivals
Sports.content:
Nottingham Forest close in on Liam Delap signing as they win race against Premier League rivals

Nottingham Forest are closing in on the signing of Liam Delap, talkSPORT understands.

Everton and Leeds United also hold historical interest in the Chelsea striker but Oliver Glasner's side are set to snap the striker up.

3 Delap may cost Forest a pretty penny, though Credit: Getty

Delap is keen to make the transfer to the City Ground after being told that he doesn't have a future at Chelsea.

Chelsea are believed to value the 23-year-old at £50million this summer.

Delap joined the Blues from Ipswich Town for £30million last summer following the Tractor Boys' relegation from the Premier League.

The former England Under-21 international went on to score just one goal in 28 league appearances last term, though.

He has not been named in Chelsea's matchday squad for their season opener on Monday night, which sees them face Fulham live on talkSPORT.

As a result, Delap is now one of several centre-forwards at the club under consideration for an exit despite his deal running until 2031.

Chelsea are also willing to listen to offers for Nicolas Jackson and Marc Guiu.

Delap to leave Chelsea

The latest interest in Delap comes after he was stripped of his shirt number ahead of the new season. Joao Pedro has been handed his No.9 jersey.

Delap had held the shirt since his arrival at Stamford Bridge, but has now been switched to the No.12, although that shirt is set to be vacated soon.

talkSPORT previously revealed Delap's preference was to remain in the Premier League if he was to leave Chelsea.

3 Delap has really struggled to establish himself at Stamford Bridge Credit: Getty

Italian side Como have also shown an interest in signing him this month.

Cesc Fabregas' side will play Champions League football this term following their fourth place finish in Serie A.

Premier League clubs eye striker

Meanwhile, Leeds may be on the lookout for a new forward following Joel Piroe's departure to West Ham.

The Suriname international joined the Hammers on a season-long loan with an obligation to buy if they win promotion. Piroe scored on debut during West Ham's defeat at home to Charlton last weekend.

His exit leaves Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Lukas Nmecha as the only fit senior centre-forwards at Daniel Farke's disposal.

Forest have also allowed a striker to leave with Taiwo Awoniyi joined newly-promoted Coventry City.

3 Delap has also attracted interest from Como this summer but would prefer a Premier League move Credit: Getty

Chris Wood and Igor Jesus remain at the City Ground, whilst Arnaud Kalimuendo has returned from his loan spell with Eintracht Frankfurt.

As for Everton, the Toffees can call upon Thierno Barry and Beto in the No.9 position, with the pair scoring a combined 17 league goals last term.

Sports.title: 49ers owner Jed York tried to pay $140 for sex at Ohio trailer park... as humiliating details of his prostitution arrest emerge
Sports.content:
The owner and CEO of the San Francisco 49ers allegedly attempted to pay a woman $140 for sex in a trailer park in Ohio, according to court documents.

Jed York, who is worth $500 million and also co-owns Premier League club Leeds United and Scottish giants Rangers, was arrested in East Palestine on suspicion of engaging in prostitution at 9.35am on Sunday. He was released after posting a $5,000 bond.

Court documents obtained by The Daily Mail reveal York, 46, 'arranged to have sexual activity with the female in exchange for $140.' He responded to an undercover ad placed on a known prostitution website by law enforcement.

When York arrived at the arranged location, believed to be the Wheat Hill Mobile Home Community in East Palestine, York was greeted by a law enforcement sting operation.

He was taken into custody when an agent with the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force discovered York had 'in his possession his cellular device which was used to arrange a criminal act', the court documents show.

Court records also show that York, who was born 20 miles away from East Palestine in Youngstown, Ohio, was initially charged with engaging in prostitution, but prosecutors amended that to disorderly conduct. He was also charged with possessing criminal tools.

49ers co-owner Jed York - above with wife Danielle - allegedly attempted to pay a woman $140 for sex in a trailer park in Ohio

York, 46, was arrested Sunday in East Palestine, Ohio, and booked into Columbiana County Jail

York is believed to have been arrested at Wheat Hill Mobile Home Community in East Palestine

York was sentenced to one day in jail for both offenses to be served concurrently and was credited with one day served when he pleaded no contest Monday morning. He was also fined $1,150.

Records also show that York had a cellphone returned to him and that $160 that was seized was to be given to the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force as part of the plea agreement. He also completed an online course.

It comes after York filed for divorce from his wife, Danielle, back in May and cited irreconcilable differences.

The San Francisco Chronicle has reported the couple are still waiting for a court date for their dissolution of marriage case to be heard.

The couple, who got married in 2011, have two sons, Jaxon and Brixton. They have agreed to legal and physical joint custody.

The NFL said in a statement: 'We are aware of the matter, which will be reviewed under the personal conduct policy.'

The 49ers said in a statement: 'As this is a legal matter, which has been resolved, we will not be providing any further comment at this time.'

The Daily Mail has reached out to East Palestine Police and the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force, as well as York's attorney for comment.

York is the son of Denise DeBartolo York and John York. They took control of the 49ers when DeBartolo's brother, Eddie, was convicted in a gambling fraud scandal.

York has been married to Belluomini since 2011 and they have two sons together

Eddie, who owned the 49ers during their 1980s-1990s dynasty, pleaded guilty in 1998 to failing to report a felony when he paid $400,000 to former Louisiana Governor Edwin Edwards in exchange for a riverboat gambling license.

DeBartolo, whose 49ers won five Super Bowls under his leadership, stepped down as owner in 1997 after two Louisiana newspapers reported he would be indicted for gambling fraud.

He avoided prison, was fined $1 million and was suspended for a year by the NFL but the episode effectively ended his NFL career. President Donald Trump pardoned him in February 2020.

Jed began working for his father in the early 2000s and was eventually named the franchise's CEO in 2008. He then became the principal owner in 2024 after acquiring enough of his mother's stake.

During his tenure, the Niners have experienced great success, having won five NFC West titles, advanced to seven NFC Championship Games and three Super Bowls, although the team has not won the NFL's biggest prize since 1994.

York also oversaw the building of Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, California. The team moved from San Francisco to the new stadium in 2014. The stadium has hosted two Super Bowls, a World Cup and a College Football Playoff title game.

It is the latest episode in what has been an offseason plagued with problems for the 49ers, who are expected to compete for a playoff spot again this season. They play their opening game against the Los Angeles Rams in Melbourne on September 10.

Head coach Kyle Shanahan was involved in an offseason car crash that left him unable to coach in training camp and with several serious injuries.

The 49ers play their play their first game against the LA Rams in Melbourne on September 19

The July 14 incident has been shrouded in mystery after the police refused to release an accident report or bodycam footage from the scene and officers initially blamed the other driver, only for Shanahan to take responsibility.

He collided with a car driven by a 21-year-old woman in Palo Alto last month, saying it happened when he reached for his phone.

The incident left Shanahan with a concussion, broken ribs, a broken nose, a broken hand and more than 40 stitches were needed to close a cut over his eye.

He also explained that he was driving at around 20mph with his Tesla in autopilot mode when the crash happened.

In autopilot mode, Tesla 'matches the speed of your vehicle to that of the surrounding traffic' and 'assists in steering within a clearly marked lane, and uses traffic-aware cruise control.'

Shanahan was the only person who needed to be hospitalized and police didn't issue him a ticket for the cellphone use.

Sports.title: Man City expected to go back in for Enzo Fernandez - despite missing Chelsea's deadline to bid £120m for star
Sports.content:
Man City expected to go back in for Enzo Fernandez - despite missing Chelsea's deadline to bid £120m for star

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Manchester City are expected to go back in for Chelsea’s Enzo Fernandez.

The Blues previously set City a deadline of 5pm on August 13 to pay £120m to get the deal done - a deadline City did not meet.

But contact has continued with his agent Javier Pastore so City know the 25-year-old is open to coming and now they are set to come back in for the midfielder, who played the final half-hour of Chelsea's 3-2 win away at Fulham on Monday night.

The Argentina midfielder shared a strong relationship with City's new boss Enzo Maresca when he was Chelsea coach and has six years left on his contract.

However, Chelsea will now demand more than £120m as the clock ticks down on the window.

The Blues will also need to secure a replacement before agreeing to sell the Argentine.

Man City are expected to go back in for Enzo Fernandez despite missing Chelsea's deadline

Fernandez enjoyed a strong relationship with City boss Enzo Maresca when he was at Chelsea

When asked about Fernandez's future after the win at Craven Cottage, Xabi Alonso told BBC Match of the Day: 'In football, I am not surprised by anything. We will see.

'My wish is that we know what will happen for the future but we will see this week.'

Representatives of alternative midfield targets for both clubs anticipate City trying for Fernandez first before other matters can fall into place.

City have agreed to sign Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille and are in the process of selling Nico Gonzalez to Newcastle United for £50m.

They have also agreed to sign winger Allan Elias from Palmeiras but hold interest in Liverpool’s Cody Gakpo too.

Reece James and Romeo Lavia started in central midfield for Chelsea at Fulham on Monday, while Elliot Anderson and Marc Guehi got the nod for City in their 2-1 win over Bournemouth on Sunday.

Sports.title: TRANSFER CONFIDENTIAL: Everything YOUR club is doing with one week to go - including latest on Arsenal's Julian Alvarez hunt, the three potential Enzo Fernandez replacements on Chelsea's radar and Leeds eye four more signings
Sports.content:
TRANSFER CONFIDENTIAL: Everything YOUR club is doing with one week to go - including latest on Arsenal's Julian Alvarez hunt, the three potential Enzo Fernandez replacements on Chelsea's radar and Leeds eye four more signings

Unlock more of the best of our journalism with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight and the writers you love every day

There's one week to go in the transfer window and every Premier League club still has a lot to do before it slams shut.

The 20 clubs have already spent more than £2billion combined this summer, topped by three deals within the division – Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa to Chelsea (£117million), Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest to Manchester City (£116million) and Sandro Tonali from Newcastle United to Tottenham Hotspur (£100million).

But no club is closed for business yet and in the rush to ready a squad before the deadline passes, there is a huge amount of transfer activity left to go.

Here, SIMON JONES explains what your club still needs, who they're in for and who might go...

Arsenal

They want a striker. The dream is Julian Alvarez from Atletico Madrid, except the player's dream is to join Barcelona. Atletico ideally don't want that to happen so Arsenal still have a chance if the relationship continues to sour. Galatasaray's Victor Osimhen is an alternative.

A left winger. Al Hilal are closing on a £50million deal for Gabriel Martinelli while Ethan Nwaneri is expected to go out on loan and Reiss Nelson is poised to join West Ham.

Everton's £80million-rated Iliman Ndiaye is among those Arsenal admire for left wing.

Atletico Madrid forward Julian Alvarez is Arsenal's dream striker target, but the Argentina is more keen on a move to Barcelona

Aston Villa

A striker and centre-back. They are primed to bid for Chelsea's Nicolas Jackson with Ollie Watkins poised to join Al Hilal and have had bids rejected for Taylor Harwood-Bellis at Southampton.

Enquiries are ongoing for Joel Ordonez of Club Brugge and Tosin Adarabioyo of Chelsea.

Free agent Leon Goretzka is poised to add experience in midfield.

Bournemouth

Bournemouth are considering adding a No6 and a No10, plus a winger. Main objective has been to keep their squad together with clubs circling for Alex Scott, Tyler Adams, El Junior Kroupi and Marcus Tavernier. Juventus goalkeeper Michele Di Gregorio flew in on Monday ahead of completing his loan move.

The option to buy is £12.5million plus £2million in bonuses and there is a £1million penalty if that option is not taken up.

Brentford

A left wing-back is the target and West Ham's El Hadji Malick Diouf has been one throughout the summer.

Defender Ethan Pinnock is joining Coventry City for £6million. They would like another midfielder and have considered a loan for Chelsea winger Mykhailo Mudryk. Also wary of late bids for Igor Thiago.

Brighton

A winger or two. Liverpool want Yankuba Minteh but there is some distance between valuations.

Amario Cozier-Duberry also has offers from Rangers and Wolves. Brighton have asked about Femi Azeez at Millwall and Deportivo La Coruna's Yeremay Hernandez.

The club are working on a deal for BSC Young Boys left-back Jaouen Hadjam.

Chelsea

Focus has been on getting players out. However, if Manchester City firm up interest in Enzo Fernandez they would want a replacement in first.

Monaco's Lamine Camara, Adam Wharton of Crystal Palace and Bournemouth's Alex Scott are admired.

Their £100million valuation of Pedro Neto and £75million price tag on Malo Gusto have deterred bids but both have interest from rival clubs. Juventus winger Conceicao is on their radar should anyone match their Neto price.

Nottingham Forest spoke to Chelsea on Monday night about a deal for striker Liam Delap.

Real Sociedad are pushing to sign Mamadou Sarr on loan from Chelsea.

Brentford have considered a move for Chelsea's Mykhailo Mudryk

Coventry City

Coventry are open to late opportunities to strengthen across the team but would like more options in defence and wing. They had interest in Milan's Fikayo Tomori plus Porto's Francisco Moura and are closing on a £6million deal for Brentford’s Ethan Pinnock. But Stephen Mfuni’s loan move from Manchester City is off.

Crystal Palace

They would like a forward, winger, midfielder and centre-back.

Galatasaray continue to circle for Ismaila Sarr and Adam Wharton is a last-minute option for some despite Palace saying they won't sell. Palace have also rebuffed Aston Villa interest in Jean-Philippe Mateta.

Axel Disasi is due to sign from Chelsea while they want a midfielder after Monaco rejected their offers for Lamine Camara. Auxerre's Kevin Danois and West Ham's Soungoutou Magassa are among their targets.

They have also checked on Roma midfielder Neil El Aynaoui.

Everton

A right-back, left-back, midfielder, winger and striker. David Moyes wants more quality in depth after they fell short of Europe last season. Chelsea's Liam Delap is among the forwards being considered.

Fulham

A centre-back, midfielder and winger. They have had bids rejected for Rennes defender Abdelhamid Ait-Boudlal and Trabzonspor's Chibuike Nwaiwu. Ethan Nwaneri of Arsenal is admired.

Hull City

A forward, a winger, and goalkeeping cover are the targets. They are progressing for Mohamed Ali-Cho from Nice and Union Berlin forward Ilya Ansah.

Ipswich Town

Defence, midfield and attack is where Gary O'Neil would like to add. Bayer Leverkusen midfielder Exequiel Palacios is one he is chasing while they are one of many keen on Liam Delap.

Chelsea's Liam Delap is admired by many clubs and Forest are holding talks over a move

Leeds United

A winger, striker, defender, goalkeeper. Chelsea have rejected their latest loan bid for Mykhaylo Mudryk. They may add free agent defender Diogo Leite. Frankfurt 'keeper Michael Zetterer has held talks over a £4.3m move.

Leeds have held talks with Eintracht Frankfurt goalkeeper Michael Zetterer (right)

Liverpool

They are chasing two wingers. Bradley Barcola at Paris Saint-Germain and Yankuba Minteh of Brighton are the current targets. If there is no breakthrough on fees soon they will have to consider alternatives, but both players want to join.

Manchester City

A forward, midfielder, and right-back are on the list. Ayyoub Bouaddi is on his way from Lille and winger Allan Elias is set to join from Palmeiras after the clubs agreed a £34m deal.

Enzo Fernandez remains an expensive option for City who also admire Roma's Manu Kone and Adam Wharton of Palace. Jack Grealish could stay as Omar Marmoush follows Savinho to Spurs.

Manchester United

They would like a left-back and a forward. An enquiry for Newcastle's Lewis Hall was rejected and despite a limit on what iis left to spend, they have checked on Barcelona's Alejandro Balde and Jorge Salinas of Santander. Juventus or Aston Villa could bid for Joshua Zirkzee to provide funds for a new forward.

Newcastle United

A midfield organiser is the key and they are closing in on an agreement for Manchester City's Nico Gonzalez. They have also asked about Tottenham's Archie Gray.

Versatile Lille forward Matias Fernandez-Pardo is also one they are discussing.

Talks have advanced between Newcastle and Manchester City over a move for Spanish midfielder Nico Gonzalez

Nottingham Forest

A striker, right-back and midfielder. They are talking to Chelsea about Liam Delap and have also discussed Everton's Beto and Igor Thiago of Brentford for the striker option. Spurs' Lucas Bergvall and Barcelona's Marc Casado plus Auxerre's Kevin Danois are in the mix too and Fiorentina right-back Dodo is the latest in their sights.

Sunderland

Their midfield has been bolstered by the arrival of Jules Ahoka for £8million from Royal Antwerp. They are also working to add a right winger with talks ongoing over a £30million deal for Sporting Lisbon's Geny Catamo. Goalkeeper Robin Roefs is in talks over a new contract.

Tottenham Hotspur

Wanted are two forwards and right back cover. Savinho has joined from Manchester City and Omar Marmoush will follow on an initial loan. Spurs are also trying an ambitious move for Cody Gakpo from Liverpool but hold interest in Chelsea's Pedro Neto among others as a back-up .

Sports.title: Sky Sports pundits make their MNF predictions for the season: Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher are torn on Man United and Liverpool and name the 'best signing by a mile'
Sports.content:
Sky Sports pundits make their MNF predictions for the season: Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher are torn on Man United and Liverpool and name the 'best signing by a mile'

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher's competitive sides came out once more on Sky Sports' Monday Night Football as they made their annual Premier League predictions at the start of the season.

The long-time adversaries now pundits and friends revealed their thoughts after their post-match analysis of Chelsea's 3-2 win at Fulham.

And as you would expect the pair didn't see eye-to-eye - especially when it came to their own beloved clubs: Manchester United and Liverpool.

However, the pair were in unison when it came to deciding who would be crowned Premier League champions this season - with both backing holders Arsenal to successfully defend their title.

'One hundred per cent Arsenal,' said Neville. 'They're way out in front and the squad they have assembled with the signings of [Ezri] Konsa, [Bruno] Guimaraes, [Christos] Tzolis and maybe one more - what a squad they have.'

In the race for the top four, the duo both had Manchester City and Chelsea but differed with the final teams in their selections as Neville backed United and Carragher chose Liverpool.

Gary Neville (left) and Jamie Carragher have made their annual Premier League predictions

The Sky Sports duo both have Arsenal down to successfully defend their Premier League title

In fact their top-four orders were different as Neville had Chelsea second, Manchester City third and then United; while Carragher feels City will finish as runners-up ahead of Chelsea and then Liverpool.

'If I'm being honest I can't separate United and Liverpool in fourth place, I have no idea,' conceded Neville.

'A couple of weeks ago I had United in third and Chelsea not in the top four but as you get nearer towards the season you then start to look at the squads and think about it, such as Chelsea having no European football - which will give them a big edge - and I think City are in a better position than United. At the moment I'm not convinced by United or Liverpool but I'm going for United fourth as I'm purely a fan.'

In fifth, Carragher went for United and you guessed it... Neville went for Liverpool.

Tottenham come sixth in Carragher's predictions, while Brentford who thumped the London rivals 3-0 on Saturday - but in truth it could and perhaps should have been more - are his European contender.

Neville has Brighton finishing sixth - highlighting the continuity under Fabian Hurzeler and has Spurs as his European contender.

All three promoted sides in Coventry City, Hull City and Ipswich Town are tipped to go straight back down by Neville; while Carragher believes Coventry will stay up.

The side to go down in his estimation? Sunderland.

Despite losing at Hull City, Neville predicts Manchester United will finish fourth this season

The Black Cats finished seventh last season to qualify for the Europa League and Carragher believes their European commitments this season will prove their downfall domestically.

'They're going to be doing a lot of Thursday-Sunday,' he began his reasoning with. 'I think Sunderland last season reminded me a little bit of Sheffield United under Chris Wilder when they came up and had a really brilliant and finished high up the table.

'But a lot of the games, like Sunderland last season, were won by the odd goal. When you look at their underlying numbers last season they were pretty close to relegation and I think with the European football it could be a problem for them.'

Both see Fulham at risk of relegation, while Carragher also adds Crystal Palace to that mix.

In terms of individual accolades, the duo have Manchester City striker Erling Haaland as top goalscorer.

As for impact signing, both chose players in north London with Tottenham's Mateus Fernandes earmarked by Carragher and Arsenal's Guimaraes highlighted by Neville.

Speaking about the Gunners' midfielder, Neville was effusive in his praise.

Neville hailed Arsenal summer signing Bruno Guimaraes as the 'best signing by a mile'

Carragher and Neville's predictions were shown in full at the end of the Monday night show

'I think it's the best signing by a mile,' Neville declared. 'If you take an outfield player out of Arsenal's team there wasn't a massive drop off between the first and second team apart from Declan Rice. If Rice gets injured for three months that would be a risk to Arsenal but the signing of Guimaraes removes that.

'He is a massive personality and believes he can win every single match for his team. He's somebody you would want alongside you. For £75million that is value in this market.'

For player to watch, Carragher opts for Jeremy Jacquet, while Morgan Rogers was Neville's pick.

Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle was the manager to watch for Carragher, while Xabi Alonso got the nod for Neville.

Sports.title: Revealed: Ollie Watkins returned to Aston Villa to apologise to team-mates for missing Brighton defeat as Saudi move draws closer - and Villans begin talks with AC Milan over Rafael Leao
Sports.content:
Revealed: Ollie Watkins returned to Aston Villa to apologise to team-mates for missing Brighton defeat as Saudi move draws closer - and Villans begin talks with AC Milan over Rafael Leao

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Ollie Watkins returned to Aston Villa training on Monday and apologised to his team-mates for missing their 4-0 defeat by Brighton - but is still expected to leave for Al Hilal.

Villa have turned down a series of bids for Watkins but the England forward is keen on the move to Saudi Arabia.

The club, meanwhile, have contacted AC Milan over a potential move for Portugal international Rafael Leao.

Villa are exploring the financial details for the 27-year-old who has been talking to Turkish clubs in recent weeks and has been on the radar of a number of Champions League sides this summer.

Unai Emery wants to strengthen his attacking options after losing Morgan Rogers to Chelsea. Rogers scored on his Premier League debut for the Blues in the 3-2 win over Fulham on Monday.

Unai Emery gave a frosty response when asked about Ollie Watkins' absence at Brighton

Villa have contacted AC Milan about a move for winger Rafael Leao as they look to strengthen

Villa boss Emery hinted that Watkins had been reluctant to play in their Premier League opener on Sunday.

When asked about Watkins' absence following the 4-0 defeat at the Amex Stadium, Emery said: ‘This question is for him. I can answer only with my silence.’

Pressed on whether the striker was refusing to play, Emery said: ‘I think you can call him, you can call his agent and he can respond.’

Villa have long held interest in Chelsea's Nicolas Jackson and were rebuffed in a call for Jean-Philippe Mateta of Crystal Palace, as Daily Mail Sport revealed.

Villa have also held further talks with Club Brugge for defender Joel Ordonez.

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso urges Robert Sanchez to 'relax and carry on' after Chelsea goalkeeper endured a nightmare Premier League opener at Fulham
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso urges Robert Sanchez to 'relax and carry on' after Chelsea goalkeeper endured a nightmare Premier League opener at Fulham

Xabi Alonso responded ‘relax and carry on’ when asked about Robert Sanchez’s mistakes in his Premier League win as Blues boss, insisting it is not only in goal where Chelsea can do better.

Sanchez stirred up the debate surrounding how far the Blues can go with their 28-year-old Spaniard in goal. He conceded a weak strike from Josh King before parrying another shot for Fulham’s £34million summer signing from Real Madrid, Gonzalo Garcia, to head home the rebound.

Towards the end of this first victory for Alonso, Sanchez was fortunate that Antonee Robinson lacked the accuracy to lob him for an equaliser after he had charged out of his goal.

When asked about Sanchez afterwards, Alonso said: ‘It's about the team, it's not about the individual. The first goal, we can do better to defend, we can do better to avoid, but it's part of the game. We need to accept and to learn. This is going to be a process. All the lines, from the strikers, the midfielders, the defence, the goalkeepers, we want to do better in everything. The goal was to start good, and we've been able to start well. Relax and carry on.’

Chelsea have insisted throughout this summer that they are happy with goalkeeper set-up, with Sanchez as their No 1 and 21-year-old Belgian Mike Penders as his understudy. Goals from their fearsome front three in Joao Pedro, Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer made sure Chelsea won at Craven Cottage against Alvaro Arbeloa's Fulham.

Robert Sanchez has been urged to 'relax and carry on' by Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso

The Blues stopper had a night to forget at Fulham, where he was unable to keep two goals out

Enzo Fernandez was introduced as a second-half substitute. While Fulham’s fans booed his every touch – and chanted ‘England, England’ at the Argentinian – Chelsea's supporters sang his name. It was a show of support from the away end despite his intense links to Manchester City.

‘In football, I am not surprised by anything,’ Alonso said about Fernandez and the speculation. ‘We will see. My wish is that we know what will happen for the future, but we will see this week.’

On Joao Pedro, Rogers and Palmer, Alonso added: ‘They need to take responsibility, they need to lead the rest, they need to inspire the rest. If they do, great, other ones will follow.’

Meanwhile, Fulham boss Arbeloa said: ‘We conceded goals in the first minute, at the end of the first half and at the beginning of the second half. There are not worse moments to concede.

‘But we showed character and personality and I am very proud of how my players responded. We deserved a little more but football is not about what you deserve, it is about what you take. For me, they are easy goals for them and mistakes we cannot make. We need to improve and be more ready in the first minute, that is for sure.’

Sports.title: Arsenal star Gabriel Martinelli closes on £55m move to Saudi Arabia... as Al-Hilal plot double swoop from Premier League
Sports.content:
Arsenal winger Gabriel Martinelli is closing on a £55million move to Al-Hilal. The Saudi club are working to sign the Brazilian alongside Aston Villa striker Ollie Watkins. Martinelli has still to finalise personal terms but talks are understood to be progressing. Turkish club Galatasaray made a £38.5million bid for Martinelli earlier this month but the 25-year-old would not consider a move to Istanbul. Gabriel Martinelli did not want to move to Turkey but talks over personal terms with Al-Hilal are progressing Martinelli, who joined from Brazilian side Ituano for £6m in 2019, has just 12 months remaining on his Arsenal contract. Ituano are due a sell-on percentage of the profit. He made 53 appearances in all competitions last season, scoring 11 goals, as the Gunners won the Premier League title but he was left out of the squad for their league opener against Coventry on Friday. Arsenal are maintaining contacts with Atletico Madrid for Julian Alvarez though the Argentine remains intent on joining Barcelona. With Atletico reluctant to sell to Barca, Arsenal are waiting for the player's camp to indicate he would want to join them.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
