World.title: Nigeria: 150 Terrorists Surrender As Military Pressure Mounts in North-East
World.content:
ABUJA -- More than 150 terrorists, including commanders, fighters and affiliates, have surrendered to troops of the Joint Task Force North East, Operation Hadin Kai (OPHK), in the past week, the military has said.

The figure represents a significant increase from the more than 50 terrorists who surrendered in the previous week, according to the Acting Military Information Officer, Captain Mohammed Goni.

Goni, in a statement on Monday, attributed the surge to sustained intelligence-led operations, intensified military pressure and coordinated kinetic and non-kinetic efforts aimed at degrading terrorist capabilities and encouraging voluntary disengagement.

He said the development indicated growing pressure within terrorist formations, particularly on their freedom of movement, logistics, supply chains and ability to retain personnel in their enclaves.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

"The significant increase reflects the cumulative impact of sustained intelligence-led operations, intensified military pressure and coordinated kinetic and non-kinetic efforts aimed at degrading terrorist capabilities and encouraging voluntary disengagement from terrorism," he said.

Goni added that the recovery of weapons and ammunition from some of the surrendering terrorists further demonstrated the impact of sustained military pressure on terrorist networks.

He said the increase in surrenders also reflected the effectiveness of Operation Hadin Kai's counter-insurgency strategy, which combines intelligence-led operations with strategic communication, civil-military engagement and other non-kinetic measures.

According to him, the measures were disrupting terrorist activities and support networks, weakening hostile narratives and encouraging more members of the groups to abandon terrorism.

He said strategic communication remained central to the military's efforts by conveying credible messages to those willing to renounce terrorism and highlighting the consequences of continued association with terrorist groups.

Goni said all persons who surrendered were profiled, documented and handled in accordance with established procedures and applicable laws.

He said the theatre command would sustain the current momentum to encourage further disengagement and weaken terrorist recruitment and sustainment mechanisms.

The Military High Command, he added, commended troops for their resilience, discipline and operational effectiveness, urging them to maintain pressure on terrorist elements and deny them freedom of action across the theatre.

Close 

"Operation Hadin Kai remains resolute in its mission to sustain pressure on terrorist networks, disrupt their capabilities and support structures, protect civilians and create the conditions necessary for the restoration of lasting peace, security and normalcy across the North-East region," he said.

World.title: Zimbabwe: Mnangagwa Dragged to Constitutional Court, Accused of Packing Senate With Zanu-PF Politicians
World.content:
President Emmerson Mnangagwa has been dragged to the Constitutional Court over his appointment of 10 senators, with two applicants accusing him of packing the Upper House with politicians instead of independent professionals as required by the Constitution.

Thamsanqa Ncube and Ibhetshu LikaZulu are seeking an urgent order blocking the nominees from being sworn in and ultimately declaring their appointments null and void.

The respondents are Mnangagwa, the Speaker of Parliament, Justice Minister Ziyambi Ziyambi, the Attorney-General and the 10 nominees, Jabulani Sibanda, Makhosini Hlongwane, Mary Mliswa, Nokuthula Matsikenyere, Kudakwashe Tagwirei, Godwills Masimirembwa, Lucy Chitaga, Gen Gibson Mashingaidze, Brilliant Dube and Iren Mutumbwa.



The applicants argue that Section 120(1)(e), introduced through Constitution Amendment No. 3, requires the President to appoint 10 senators based on their "professional skills and other competencies" and after consultation with the National Assembly.

But they claim the nominees are predominantly Zanu-PF politicians or closely linked to the ruling party, defeating the purpose of the amendment.

The application says the appointments are "the precise opposite" of assurances given by Justice Minister Ziyambi during debate on the amendment.

Ziyambi had told Parliament: "The appointment power is not unbounded. The text requires that these 10 Senators be chosen for their professional skills and competencies."

He said the new senators were intended to bring expertise "in finance, in science, in law, in technology, in public health".

The applicants also challenge the consultation process, saying Mnangagwa's nominees were simply announced in Parliament before the Speaker declared: "Recommendations put and agreed to."

"There was no debate, no question, no point of order, and no opportunity for meaningful consultation," Ncube says in the founding affidavit.

The applicants further argue that there is no legislative or parliamentary framework regulating the consultation process, making the appointments premature and unconstitutional.

They fear the dispute will become academic if the nominees are sworn in and begin voting in the Senate.

"The ten individuals are awaiting swearing-in. Once sworn, they will sit and vote in the Senate with full rights," Ncube says.

The applicants want the court to stop the swearing-in and order that any fresh appointments only be made after proper procedures are established to ensure the nominees have the professional expertise required by the Constitution.

The case comes shortly after Constitution Amendment No. 3 increased the Senate from 80 to 90 members by creating the 10 presidentially appointed seats.

World.title: Congo-Kinshasa: DR Congo Peace Roadmap - Will the Fighting Finally End?
World.content:
Eastern DR Congo has seen repeated waves of violence and displacement. Pictured here, families sheltering at an IDP camp in Ituri province in September 2025.

A new roadmap sets out the conditions toward peace in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). But disagreements over M23 rebels, Rwanda's role and security concerns remain, and could still derail the process.

Representatives of the Congolese government and the Rwanda-backed M23 rebel group agreed on a roadmap for peace after negotiations in Geneva.

It builds on the US-brokered framework signed in Doha last year, and sets out steps and timelines for negotiations and implementation: a ceasefire monitoring mechanism is also due to receive support from the UN peacekeeping mission, MONUSCO.

The United States, Qatar, the African Union (AU) and Switzerland have all expressed their support for the process as brokers of the push for peace.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

However, it is not a full peace plan with bindíng resolutions and terms; rather, many aspects of the push will still need to be fine-tuned.

The new diplomatic initiative could nevertheless be offering fresh hope following years of bloody conflict in eastern DRC; fighting in the region has killed hundreds of civilians and displaced millions since 2022. The M23 rebel group continues to control large parts of North Kivu and South Kivu — two provinces in eastern DRC that are highly coveted for their minerals.

As disagreements remain over key issues, doubts continue to cast a shadow over the prospect of a lasting peace.

From signature to implementation

"There are likely to be many more bumps on the road — disagreements remain over issues including sanctions against M23, the release of detainees and the timing of political reforms. So this remains a very fragile commitment," Alex Vines, Africa program director at the European Council on Foreign Relations, told DW.

Conflict analyst Clifton Chifuwe, executive director of the Centre for Peace Research and Advocacy (CPRA), a local NGO that focuses on conflict management, agrees with that assessment, pointing to the presence of multiple armed groups in the area, the deep level of mistrust between DRC and Rwanda, and competition over eastern Congo's mineral wealth.

He believes that the biggest of the challenges across the board is to turn this roadmap into action.

"Signing it is easier than implementing it on the ground," Chifuweexplains.

Chifuwe told DW that independent monitoring mechanisms and the involvement of all key stakeholders will be essential for any peace to hold.

Rwanda's role in the conflict

Rwanda has repeatedly rejected accusations that it backs M23 rebels — though international groups maintain the view that the small neighboring nation is deeply entrechned in the conflict.

Kigali's relationship with the rebel group therefore remains central to the peace process, says Vines:

"Rwanda's good faith and its relationship with M23 is a really key consideration. Kigali's buy-in to any agreement and influence over M23 is key."

Rwandan President Paul Kagame's comments at a press conference on August 24 further underline the complexity of the issue; Kagame rejects the narrative that Rwanda is responsible for the current conflict, blaming factions within the DRC instead.

He links any Rwandan involvement in the conflict to what he describes as a longstanding security threat from the other side of the border, naming the Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Rwanda (FDLR) armed group — which fights against M23 rebels alongside the Congolese military — as his main target.

Kagame said that "if this problem of the FDLR is not resolved," Rwanda would act to protect itself "at any cost."

Mixed messages of hope and skepticism

There also are signs and reasons for cautious optimism: Chifuwe highlights that the roadmap focuses on a sequenced implementation plan, with monitoring initiatives to be put in place to help identify warning signs before any violence resumes.

These international mediators will also have to maintain pressure on the parties while ensuring regional concerns are heard.

In this context, Vines believes that US and Qatari involvement remains important, while stressing that African input through the AU must not be ignored.

All parties involved have signed off on a pledge to "pursue negotiations towards comprehensive peace and conflict resolution" — for now.

Close 

What does peace mean for the displaced?

Ultimately, the roadmap will not be measured by the signatories' attitudes but by results for thousands upon thousands of people in the eastern DRC, who remain displaced.

"The real test is ... whether ordinary Congolese people become safer and better off," Chifuwe says emphatically, highlighting also the restoration of state authority and the management of mineral resources as key objectives that need to be achieved.

For Congolese civilians, the diplomatic language carries a personal meaning: One refugee named Linda Kasongo finds herself stuck in Zambia five years into the conflict.

She told DW that she wants to return home, but can't even entertain the thought, since violence on all sides continues to wreck lives and livelihoods in her war-torn home region.

"I hope it works out because I want to go home," Kasongo says. "I want to be with my people. I miss my people. I miss my home."

Edited by: Sertan Sanderson

World.title: Sudan: US Proposes Expanding UN Arms Embargo
World.content:
A woman stands outside her tent four months after fleeing the city of from El Fasher in Darfur following an attack.

The US has called for a UN arms embargo for Darfur to be broadened to the whole of Sudan. The change would require Security Council approval, with Russia warning it would hurt the Sudanese army.

The United States on Monday proposed expanding an existing UN arms embargo for Darfur to cover all of Sudan.

The proposal was put forth by US Envoy Massad Boulos during a UN Security Council meeting in New York.

"The brutality of the war waged by the Rapid Support Forces [RSF] and the Sudanese Armed Forces has discredited their claims to be legitimate governors of the Sudanese people," said Boulos, who warned that "external financial and military support is fueling the conflict and risks drawing neighboring states deeper into war."

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Boulos said the US wants to expand the embargo geographically as well as materially in order to cover unmanned aerial vehicles and related technologies. Moreover, the US plan would see the number of experts monitoring the embargo increased.

The Darfur embargo has been in place for two decades and will expire on September 12, 2026, if not amended or renewed.

An expansion would require a Security Council vote.

Sudan wants 'technical extension' but warns against hampering army

Sudan's UN envoy urged members to endorse a "technical extension" of the existing embargo while warning against changes that would hamper the army.

"Sudan suffers the most from weapons and their illegal flow. However, expanding such a sanctions regime will weaken the protection of civilians," said Al-Harith Idriss al-Harith Mohamed.

Russia, which holds veto powers in the Security Council, has voiced skepticism over changes to the existing deal, saying that expanding the embargo could impact the Sudanese army's effectiveness.

UN Sudan experts say sophisticated weaponry suggests 'external support'

Before Boulos articulated the US position, UN Under-Secretary-General for Political and Peacebuilding Affairs Rosemary Di Carlo warned that a "worrying aspect of the conflict in Sudan is its increasing complexity."

"Sophisticated weaponry," she said, "continues to point to ongoing external support to both parties."

The UN's humanitarian chief, Tom Fletcher, also made note of the fact that, "in recent weeks, fighting in Sudan has been characterized by the heavy use of drones and localized ground combat in areas less affected by rainy season conditions."

The war in Sudan, now in its fourth year, has killed tens of thousands and displaced millions of civilians.

While Sudan's army holds sway in the country's central and eastern regions, western and parts of southern Darfur are under control of rival Rapid Support Forces.

Close 

Darfur, a vast western region the size of France, has seen some of the worst violence of the conflict, with repeated attacks on displacement camps and ethnic massacres that kill thousands at a time.

Edited by: Rana Taha

World.title: Tanzania: Presidential Commission Begins Investigation of Law Violations During the 2025 Elections
World.content:
Dar es Salaam — THE Presidential Commission of Inquiry into the Individuals Involved in Violence and Violations of the Law during and after the October 2025 General Election has officially begun preparations to carry out its mandate.

The Commission seeks to establish the individuals who planned, participated in and coordinated incidents of violence, crime and violations of the law that occurred during and after the election.

Speaking to journalists in Dar es Salaam today, August 24, 2026, the Commission's Chairperson, retired Court of Appeal Judge Shaban Ali Lila, said the Commission was ready to begin its work by collecting evidence from members of the public and other stakeholders.

He said the Commission would receive oral testimony, examine various documents and visit locations identified as having been connected to the incidents under investigation.

Judge Lila said the Commission would comply with the country's laws and regulations in collecting, analysing and assessing the information and evidence submitted to it.

The Commission was established by President Samia Suluhu Hassan to investigate incidents of violence and violations of the law that occurred during and after the October 2025 General Election.

World.title: Kenya: Gachagua Defends Right to Run for President in 2027, Shrugs Off 'King Maker' Label
World.content:
Nairobi — Former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua has vowed to defend his right to contest the presidency in the 2027 General Election, maintaining that his impeachment does not automatically bar him from seeking elective office while his legal challenges remain pending.

Gachagua spoke as opposition parties gathered at a Windsor event to sign a unity pledge ahead of the 2027 elections, with DCP Deputy Leader Clephas Malala attending in his place.

The development underscored a growing tension between Gachagua's insistence on preserving his presidential ambitions and efforts by opposition parties to forge a common front against President William Ruto.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Gachagua said he would pursue his case through the Court of Appeal and, if necessary, the Supreme Court, maintaining that the Constitution requires all available legal remedies to be exhausted before an individual facing integrity-related questions can be disqualified from running for office.

"Let nobody tell you that because I was removed from office, I cannot run," Gachagua said on Monday, arguing that the relevant provisions of the Constitution must be read together.

The Democracy for Citizens Party leader was speaking as he defended his presidential ambitions while intensifying his opposition to President William Ruto and positioning himself as a potential candidate in the 2027 race.

His remarks come days after he filed an appeal challenging the High Court judgment that upheld his impeachment while finding that his right to a fair hearing had been violated during the Senate proceedings.

The High Court, in a June 8 judgment, upheld the impeachment but awarded Gachagua Sh50 million in constitutional damages after finding that the Senate had infringed his fair hearing rights by proceeding without granting him an adjournment while he was unwell.

The former Deputy President has now taken the fight to the Court of Appeal, arguing that the finding of a constitutional violation should have had consequences for the validity of his removal from office.

Gachagua said he was confident the appellate court would overturn what he described as an "absurd" outcome in which the High Court found that his rights had been violated but allowed the outcome of the process to stand.

"The High Court pronounced itself that I was taken through an unfair process and I did not get the right to fair hearing. Then the same court allows the product of an unconstitutional process to stand is what you call a constitutional absurdity," he said.

He maintained that he had another avenue before the Supreme Court if the Court of Appeal ruled against him.

"We are in court in the Court of Appeal. We believe the Court of Appeal will give justice to Gachagua's supporters. In the unfortunate event that they also pronounce themselves in an absurd manner like the High Court, we still have another chance at the Supreme Court. In the meantime, we are preparing for elections," he said.

Gachagua's interpretation of the law has received backing from senior lawyers, although the question of his eligibility is likely to remain a subject of legal contest as the 2027 elections approach.

Law Society of Kenya President Charles Kanjama has argued that Gachagua remains eligible to contest for public office while the appeal process is ongoing, citing Article 99(3) of the Constitution.

Senior Counsel Nelson Havi has similarly argued that Gachagua can remain eligible until he exhausts the available avenues of redress, including an appeal to the Supreme Court.

The High Court did not, however, overturn the Senate's impeachment. The three-judge bench held that the removal could not be reversed after the process was completed and Gachagua's successor, Kithure Kindiki, was lawfully appointed.

'Gachagua is king'

Gachagua also rejected attempts by sections of the opposition to portray him as a political "kingmaker" whose primary role should be to help unite the opposition before backing another presidential candidate.

He said he had seen supporters of his political allies making the argument on social media and other public platforms.

"Many people, including supporters of my colleagues in the United opposition, I have seen them on social media and in public platforms advancing a ridiculous proposition: that his work is to remove William Ruto and give leadership to others," he said.

Gachagua said his political ambitions went beyond helping another politician defeat Ruto.

"Rigathi is not a kingmaker. Gachagua is king," he said.

The declaration further underlines the former Deputy President's intention to remain a principal player in the opposition's efforts to challenge Ruto in 2027 rather than automatically surrender his presidential ambitions in favour of another candidate.

Gachagua has previously said he would be willing to work with other opposition leaders to produce a single candidate to challenge Ruto, but has maintained that he could himself be considered for the position.

His latest remarks come at a critical stage in the opposition's attempts to build a united front ahead of the 2027 elections.

The former Deputy President has increasingly presented himself as an alternative to the Ruto administration, accusing the government of failing to meet its promises while mobilising support across different parts of the country.

'I have nothing personal against Ruto'

Gachagua also sought to explain his increasingly aggressive opposition to President Ruto, insisting that his campaign to mobilise Kenyans against the administration was not driven by personal bitterness following his impeachment.

He said his opposition was motivated by what he described as poor governance and his desire to see the country under better leadership.

"I am not mobilizing Kenyans to remove William Ruto as president because of bitterness. No. It's my desire to have a good country," he said.

Gachagua described himself as a patriot seeking to use his political influence for what he considers the country's benefit.

Close 

"I have nothing personal against William R. I have everything against what he stands for and what he does. I want good leadership in this country. And I'm offering myself for that position of president," he said.

He defended his record against the allegations that led to his impeachment, arguing that he had committed no offence that should prevent him from seeking the presidency.

"Gachagua has killed nobody. He has raped nobody. He has displaced nobody," he said.

He attributed his removal from office to his political positions, including his defence of young Kenyans involved in the Gen Z protests and his criticism of what he termed corruption and forced evictions.

"All he has done--he has been punished because of standing with the people of Kenya. Because of saying Gen Zs are not criminals. Because of saying we should not steal from the people of Kenya. Because of saying people should not be evicted," he said.

His legal battle over the impeachment now adds another dimension to the 2027 contest, with the outcome of the Court of Appeal and potentially the Supreme Court expected to have a direct bearing on his eligibility.

For now, Gachagua insists he will continue preparing for the election while pursuing his legal challenge, setting the stage for a political and constitutional battle that could shape the opposition's strategy ahead of the August 2027 polls.

World.title: BRUCE PEARL: Conservatives are attacking the very college sports bill that protects women
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Men don’t belong in women’s sports. That isn’t complicated, but some conservative influencers and interest groups are allowing it to become complicated through careless claims about legislation designed to protect college athletics.

I spent nearly five decades coaching college basketball. I know the difference between winning a possession and winning the game. Conservatives now face a similar choice: We can chase applause by attacking allies and mischaracterizing the bill, or we can unite around the facts and win the larger fight for women, fairness and the future of college sports.

Some organizations and women’s-sports advocates claim the Protect College Sports Act would "gut" Title IX or invalidate state laws that reserve women’s teams for women. They are wrong. The text says the opposite.

REPORTER'S NOTEBOOK: COLLEGE SPORTS BILL ENTERS LEGISLATIVE 'RED ZONE' AS SEASON KICKS OFF

Section 127 explicitly states that nothing in the bill will "override, modify, or amend" Title IX. Female athletes would retain their current legal protections and ability to bring sex-discrimination claims. Section 120 also protects athletes, employees and others from retaliation for reporting discrimination or participating in Title IX proceedings.

I spent nearly five decades coaching college basketball. I know the difference between winning a possession and winning the game. Conservatives now face a similar choice: We can chase applause by attacking allies and mischaracterizing the bill, or we can unite around the facts.

Critics also claim the bill would erase state laws keeping men out of women’s sports. It would not. The legislation establishes national standards for Division I and Division II competition on limited eligibility questions, including academics, professional status, legal violations, age and years of eligibility. It neither creates a federal right for men to enter women’s competitions nor pre-empts state laws establishing sex-based athletic categories.

REPUBLICAN SENATORS FILE AMENDMENT TO STOP COLLEGE SPORTS BILL FROM OVERRIDING STATE WOMEN'S SPORTS LAWS

The bill does not expressly create a federal right for biological males to compete in women’s sports, and Section 127 states that nothing in the bill overrides, modifies or amends Title IX. Critics seem to be grasping at anything and eager to disregard the Title IX provisions here. Especially since the Supreme Court ruled in June that schools may keep men out of women’s sports.

It also requires governing bodies to enforce rules related to state and federal law and allows individuals to sue when the law is violated.

CONGRESS MUST FIX THE PROTECT COLLEGE SPORTS ACT BEFORE GIRLS PAY THE PRICE

The bill also gives schools a powerful incentive to invest in women’s and Olympic sports. It creates a $22.5 million athlete-retention fund and allows schools to unlock up to an additional $5 million through eligible NIL investments in women’s, Olympic and non-revenue sports. A school seeking the full $27.5 million retention allowance would first need to invest $5 million in those sports. That is an ingenious way to ensure continued investment in programs that might otherwise be left behind.

And every year Congress waits, the financial pressure on college athletics grows, and the programs with the fewest resources become even more vulnerable. My 2025 Final Four team had a total NIL budget of approximately $4 million. By the 2027 Final Four, some teams could be operating with budgets approaching $30 million.

Conservatives should debate legislation, demand improvements and scrutinize every line. But facts must guide us. Too many Washington organizations would rather score points against perceived rivals than secure lasting victories for women and college athletes.

CRUZ AND CANTWELL REFUSE TO BEND TO SEC AND BIG TEN CONCERNS IN REVISED COLLEGE ATHLETICS LEGISLATION

Outrage is easy; turning shared principles into law is harder. Infighting only helps the left, which has spent years undermining Title IX while conservatives battle over legislation that expressly preserves it. If we can’t unite and get this done, we will lose college sports as we know them, and women’s and Olympic sports will continue to be among the first casualties.

The stakes extend beyond Title IX, and the crisis is no longer theoretical. Thirty-two Division I Olympic-sports programs were cut between the announcement of the House settlement and May 2025. WRAL reported that more than 40 Division I Olympic-sports programs were cut between May 2024 and July 2025, even though 75% of American Olympians in 2024 competed in collegiate athletics. NCAA data

Even the University of Arkansas, backed by SEC resources, announced plans to eliminate its tennis programs before donors intervened to save them. If programs at schools like Arkansas are vulnerable, imagine the danger facing smaller schools, women’s teams and non-revenue sports nationwide.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

Credit where credit is due: Sens. Ted Cruz, R-Texas, and Eric Schmitt, R-Mo., and others have stepped up to move this legislation forward. President Trump has also led from the front by restoring the biological meaning of sex in federal policy, taking action to save college sports and backing this bill. Now, those who claim to support the America First movement should get in the game, help Congress finish the job and deliver this win for women and college athletes.

Congress now has the opportunity to take important steps to stabilize college sports, support educational opportunities for young women and men, and provide protections for the uniquely American experience of intercollegiate athletics.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

There is broad agreement that college sports cannot go on with no meaningful guardrails around eligibility, transfer policy and NIL oversight. The Protect College Sports Act is an important step in the right direction, and Congress needs to keep the positive momentum moving forward.

Winning the point may feel good. Winning the war matters more.

World.title: Democrat mayor blasted by DHS for 'hunting down' property owners leasing to ICE: 'Unhinged'
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

The Department of Homeland Security is calling out Boston Democratic Mayor Michelle Wu’s "unhinged" effort to dissuade business owners from leasing to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) in the city, equating it to "hunting down" private property owners.

After Boston banned ICE vehicles from using city-owned parking lots to stage operations, ICE issued a notice seeking to rent hundreds of parking spaces in the city for five years. In response, Wu, an outspoken opponent of President Donald Trump’s immigration enforcement agenda, issued an open letter to parking garage and lot owners throughout Boston in which she revealed the city had submitted a Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request "for any local responses to ICE."

DHS fired back in an X post, writing that "these actions by sanctuary Mayor Michelle Wu are unhinged."

"She knows she has NO authority to block us from using private property. So, she’s hunting down private property owners and threatening them for working with ICE — because she’d rather intimidate law-abiding Bostonians than get criminal illegal aliens OFF the street," wrote DHS.

TOM HOMAN FIRES BACK AT FLORIDA DEMOCRAT OVER 'RIDICULOUS' ICE RACIAL PROFILING CLAIM

ICE issued a "sources sought" notice last month for "surge parking" in 14 cities across the country. The notice revealed ICE was seeking 249 contiguous parking spaces in Boston.

In response, Wu issued an official appeal from the city of Boston for garage and lot owners to "reject ICE staging facilities." She wrote that "were ICE to procure such resources, it would constitute an unprovoked and unwarranted escalation, creating potentially significant risks to public safety and halting economic activity across our entire region."

She boasted that she "joined together with six other cities across Greater Boston and signed Executive Orders prohibiting ICE from staging its operations on municipal property and parking lots," adding, "Today, I ask you to join us: Reject any proposition by ICE to facilitate an attack on the people of Boston."

Wu also noted that the same day, the city submitted a FOIA request for any local responses to ICE. She told the garage and lot owners, "We will keep you updated as we push for a response," adding, "Thank you again for your partnership."

EXCLUSIVE: 5-TIME ILLEGAL ENTRANT ADMITS ‘MISTAKE’ THAT FINALLY GOT HIM BUSTED BY ICE

In its FOIA request, which was submitted to ICE and reviewed by Fox News Digital, the city of Boston states that it is seeking "all submissions and/or responses to ICE Sources Sought Notice with Notice ID ‘DHS-ICE-SurgeParking.’"

DHS responded to Wu’s FOIA request by calling her a "pro-criminal illegal alien politician" in another X post. The agency said the request also indicates that Wu "admits she has no authority to block ICE from utilizing private property."

"If private citizens want to allow federal law enforcement onto their own property, they should be allowed to do so—free of threats, intimidation and coercion from their radical left-wing mayor who shamelessly compared ICE agents to a neo-Nazi group," wrote DHS.

Fox News Digital reached out to Wu’s office and the city of Boston for comment.

Wu’s FOIA request came after the Boston City Council adopted an "emergency resolution" earlier this month urging the city to "explore all avenues to oppose" proposed parking leases for ICE in downtown Boston.

World.title: Darline Graham faces make-or-break GOP runoff in historic bid to keep brother’s Senate seat
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

President Donald Trump isn't on the ballot, but his clout over the GOP and the immense power of his endorsements in Republican primaries are on the line Tuesday in statewide runoff elections in South Carolina and Oklahoma.

Trump is backing Sen. Darline Graham in the Republican Senate nomination runoff in South Carolina, in the race to succeed her late brother, GOP Sen. Lindsey Graham, who unexpectedly died this summer at age 71.

And the president is supporting former state budget secretary and former state Sen. Mike Mazzei for the Republican gubernatorial nomination in Oklahoma, where GOP Gov. Kevin Stitt is term-limited.

Both Trump-backed candidates are facing off in competitive contests on that day that also includes a special election runoff in Georgia to fill a congressional seat left vacant following Democratic Rep. David Scott’s death in April. The two candidates are Democrats, which means the winner will further reduce an already extremely fragile Republican majority in the House.

DEMOCRACY ’26: STAY UP TO DATE WITH THE FOX NEWS ELECTION HUB

In South Carolina, Darline Graham is facing off with conservative Rep. Ralph Norman, with the winner replacing the late senator as the Republican Senate nominee on the midterm ballot in reliably red South Carolina.

Graham and Norman finished first and second in a special Senate primary two weeks ago, but with neither candidate landing a majority of the vote, they advanced to a runoff from a field that also included Rep. Russell Fry and former governor and former Rep. Mark Sanford.

"We need every South Carolina patriot to go to the polls and vote for Darline Graham," Trump urged on Friday as he headlined a rally for Graham in Myrtle Beach. "What I really want you to do is pretend, please, that I'm on the ballot. Just come and vote. It's so important."

Graham is backed by term-limited South Carolina Gov. Henry McMaster, who last month appointed her to fill the rest of her late brother's current term in the Senate. She also has the backing of Fry, a top Trump ally in the House, as well as the support of Sen. Tim Scott, South Carolina's other senator and chair of the National Republican Senatorial Committee.

WHAT THE LATEST FOX NEWS POWER RANKINGS IN THE MIDTERM RACES SHOW

Norman, who unsuccessfully campaigned earlier this year for the GOP gubernatorial nomination in the race to succeed McMaster, has been showcasing his support for the president in his Senate campaign and questioning Trump's backing of Darline Graham.

He was backed last week by Sanford, who briefly launched a long-shot and unsuccessful 2020 presidential challenge against Trump. Sanford, who is known as a fiscally conservative budget hawk, pointed to the nation's debt as a key motivator behind his decision to launch a Senate campaign, and later for backing Norman.

The Trump endorsement hasn't proven to be a sure bet this cycle in South Carolina.

Trump backed Lt. Gov. Pamela Evette for the GOP gubernatorial nomination — in the race to succeed the term-limited McMaster — ahead of the state's early June primary.

Evette was the top vote-getter in the primary but lost the ensuing runoff election against South Carolina Attorney General Alan Wilson in a landslide. And Trump, ever hungry for a victory, endorsed Wilson in addition to Evette days before the runoff.

"It’s becoming a referendum on Trump," a South Carolina-based Republican consultant told Fox News Digital.

The strategist, who asked for anonymity to speak more freely, argued Trump "came to South Carolina to solidify his endorsement because he has to show a win here."

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

Norman, as he runs for the Senate, is also backed by former South Carolina Gov. Nikki Haley, who served as ambassador to the United Nations during Trump's first term in the White House. Norman was the only member of South Carolina's congressional delegation, and the first member of the conservative House Freedom Caucus, to endorse Haley over Trump in the 2024 Republican presidential primaries.

"Trump still has a nasty taste in his mouth for Nikki Haley," the GOP strategist argued.

In Oklahoma, the Trump-backed Mazzei finished slightly behind state Attorney General Gentner Drummond in the initial June GOP primary, with a crowded field keeping either from winning the nomination outright. The winner of Tuesday's GOP runoff will be considered the clear general election favorite in the Republican-dominated state.

HEAD HERE FOR THE LATEST FOX NEWS POLLS IN THE MIDTERM ELECTIONS

Trump has boasted a powerful endorsement scorecard in GOP primaries so far this election cycle.

"My Endorsements are stronger than ever," the president touted this past weekend in a social media post.

But five of his gubernatorial picks in Republican primaries have fallen short. Besides South Carolina's Evette, that list includes Georgia Lt. Gov. Burt Jones and Rep. Randy Feenstra of Iowa, who lost nominating contests this spring. And two weeks ago, Wyoming Superintendent of Public Instruction Megan Degenfelder and Minnesota businessman and "My Pillow" founder and former CEO Mike Lindell fell short.

"There’s no question that an endorsement from President Trump provides a tremendous boost in a Republican primary. But it doesn’t necessarily mean the candidate’s going to win," veteran GOP strategist and communicator Ryan Williams told Fox News Digital.

Williams said that "the president still has a firm grip on the party, even in places where a candidate he backed loses a nomination." But he noted that "if there are underlying issues with a candidacy, those can pose problems that even an endorsement can’t overcome."

Meanwhile, in Georgia, two Democrats are vying to serve the remaining months through the end of the year of Scott's term in the House.

The finalists are former Gwinnett County School Board Chair Everton Blair and Marcye Scott, the late congressman's daughter.

World.title: LIZ PEEK: China is cheering as the Left blocks America’s AI infrastructure
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

The progressive Left is working hard to derail America’s AI dominance by blocking data center construction. So is China.

The AI push is critical to U.S. national security, to win what retired Lt. Col. Robert Maginnis calls the "new AI Cold War with China." But, it is also essential to U.S. economic growth. The U.S. needs to buttress its shrinking workforce, and AI agents are standing by to take over from retiring Boomers, self-deporting immigrants, and a declining number of college graduates.

AI is coming of age at the perfect time and yet anti-growth activists, amplified by foreign adversaries and media alarmism, want to shut it all down.

LAWMAKERS RAISE ALARM OVER NEVILLE ROY SINGHAM'S $278M NETWORK SPREADING CCP PROPAGANDA IN THE U.S.

China is helping them do that. While concerns about the build-out of energy-hungry data centers across the country are spurring authentic local opposition, there is also little doubt that America’s enemies are encouraging the resistance.

In 2023, the New York Times published a report detailing their investigation into Neville Roy Singham, an American Marxist based in Shanghai who, according to the Times, "works closely with the Chinese government media machine and is financing its propaganda worldwide."

At the time, Singham had funneled "at least" $275 million into leftist US nonprofits like Code Pink, The People's Forum, BreakThrough News, the Justice and Education Fund, and Tricontinental: Institute for Social Research. The Times documented that these groups are interconnected, sharing staff and content; the Times writes that Singham also "shares office space — and his groups share staff members — with a company whose mission is educating foreigners about "the miracles that China has created on the world stage."

Though he denies it, investigative reports and congressional leaders argue Singham's network advances China's strategic goals. Beijing’s main objective today is to race ahead of the U.S. in AI. President Xi cannot count on Chinese tech innovators, so is feverishly trying to hobble America’s data center build-out, the infrastructure essential to continued American dominance. Singham’s non-profit network is helping by amplifying the anti-data center campaign.

The Bitcoin Policy Institute reported recently that the "Party for Socialism and Liberation (PSL), a Marxist-Leninist group…whose stated mission is to dismantle American capitalism," is "deeply enmeshed" in local groups fighting against data center construction. The group’s leaders come from Singham’s non-profit network and the PSL has been effective in delaying or blocking about $24 billion in proposed AI-infrastructure investment.

REPORT: CHINESE PROPAGANDA, SINGHAM NETWORK, FOREIGN DARK MONEY LINKED TO CAMPAIGNS AGAINST DATA CENTERS

BPI writes, "The Singham network’s campaign against American AI has been years in the making"; it catalogs the "seeding [of] anti-data-center talking points well before the local fights began." For instance, the PSL's Communist paper, "Liberation News", published a piece in 2025 blaming rising electricity bills in Illinois to the data center boom, declaring the facilities "are generating massive profits for some, but leave workers with more bills and devastate the environment."

JIM BANKS, GOP LAWMAKERS RALLY BEHIND DOJ PROBE INTO ALLEGED CCP-LINKED FUNDING NETWORK

In June, in response to the BPI reporting, the House Energy and Commerce Committee demanded the White House and the FBI investigate foreign efforts to block the American data center buildout. The attack on AI progress is complex; the Manhattan Institute's Stu Smith wrote that the PSL and other Singham network groups are "not just one group or one campaign. It is an ecosystem of overlapping organizations, causes, and front-facing projects that all reinforce each other locally."

According to BPI findings, campaigns tied to the Singham network have contributed to delaying or restricting projects in East Charlotte, North Carolina, Prince George's County, Maryland and elsewhere.

The AI industry’s brilliant CEOs have been astonishingly slow to counter the anti-data center propaganda. Only recently have the firms begun a counter-narrative highlighting the increased tax dollars and other benefits generated by their companies. For example, in Richland Parish, Louisiana, a giant Meta data center produced a spike in sales tax revenue which, in turn, led to teachers receiving a bonus of nearly $51,000, more than many of them make in an entire year.

In Loudon County, Virginia, some 250 data centers are expected to provide $1.3 billion in taxes, or roughly 40% of the county’s total 2027 tax revenue. For local residents, that’s some payoff.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

Americans concerned about their energy bills or worried that data centers are consuming too much water are demanding legislators protect their interests, and rightly so. The fix is not difficult, and some states are already passing bills that will require hyperscalers to provide their own electricity and limit the water used in cooling the vast computers enabling the AI boom.

Americans are also worried that AI will steal their jobs. But the truth is, with millions of Boomers (finally) retiring, a declining birth rate and an exodus of immigrants further shrinking our workforce, the U.S. needs AI to provide the labor to drive our economy forward. Young people may have to reassess which fields will be most promising, but their future will without a doubt be enhanced, and not crushed, by the most powerful technological development ever created. Those who learn how to use AI will be rewarded; those who fight it will be run over.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Overlaying the opposition to AI is a mindless hatred of President Donald Trump, who won the support of our technology leaders because he offered an economy driven by cheap energy and unhampered by the suffocating regulations and green policies of Joe Biden and his Democrat colleagues. The Left’s attack on AI-fueled growth and the billionaires creating the investment surge scratches more than one itch.

AI backlash has become a hot political weapon in the upcoming midterms, with both Republican and Democrat candidates opposing the data center build-out. The stakes are high; only China will benefit from that opposition. Senator John Fetterman gets it, writing on X, "AI supremacy and energy dominance underpins our national security." He is correct.

World.title: America Needs AI to Survive. Working families also need to survive it
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Every few weeks, another multibillion-dollar AI data center is announced. The numbers keep getting bigger. So do the grid demands, the water consumption, and the land footprints.

A tech giant celebrates a new milestone. A small town wonders what it just signed away.

That disconnect deserves far more urgency than the latest LLM benchmark or model release.

KEVIN O'LEARY WARNS CHINA IS WINNING THE AI RACE BECAUSE U.S. STATES ARE SLOWING DATA CENTER PRODUCTION

The United States has no choice but to lead in artificial intelligence. China is investing aggressively, treating the technology as a geopolitical imperative. AI will dictate military capability, scientific breakthroughs, and economic hegemony for the next half-century. Falling behind is a luxury we cannot afford.

Winning, however, requires more than chips and capital. It requires a domestic social contract.

The American public has accepted massive technological disruption before because progress eventually minted a ticket to the middle class. Railroads built towns. Automobile factories created generational wealth. The internet launched millions of micro-economies and entirely new career paths. Workers lost jobs along the way, but they could always see new doors opening.

AI feels different. Because it is different.

SEN BERNIE SANDERS: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IS COMING FOR THE WORKING CLASS. WE MUST FIGHT BACK

The empires building it are scaling to multi-trillion-dollar valuations while requiring a fraction of the headcount of the industrial giants that came before them. Compounding that anxiety, the jobs AI threatens sit squarely in the middle-class professional tier. Software developers. Designers. Accountants. Corporate marketers. Legal analysts. These are people who spent decades believing that a specialized college degree was an absolute shield against automation.

That reality carries explosive political and social consequences.

I spend a significant amount of time in boardrooms advising directors on AI strategy. The conversation almost always centers on velocity. How fast can we deploy? How much productivity can we unlock? What market share can we capture?

Almost no one asks the foundational question:

How long will the public support this pace of change if they believe they are bearing the infrastructure costs while a handful of zip codes collect the rewards?

That question belongs on every board agenda today.

DEMOCRATS SOUND ALARM OVER AI JOB APOCALYPSE — BUT LABOR MARKET ISN'T FOLLOWING SCRIPT

The surrounding debate usually retreats to predictable ideological corners. One side argues the government should simply tax and redistribute the wealth AI creates. The other promises that breakthroughs in medicine and science will eventually lift all boats.

Neither answer addresses the psychological reality of the American worker. People rarely oppose technology because they dislike progress; they oppose it when they realize progress no longer includes them.

SILICON VALLEY IS LOSING THE DATA CENTER FIGHT, RISKING A REPEAT OF A CLASSIC FAILURE

Every extractive industry in history eventually had to learn this lesson. Oil companies learned it. Mining conglomerates learned it. Wind and solar developers are learning it now. Communities supplying the land, the electricity, the water, and the political baseline expect more than a corporate ribbon-cutting and a dozen permanent jobs.

AI infrastructure providers must anticipate the same reckoning.

When a tech company builds a data center designed to operate for decades, the host community should be able to point to an asset that will actually endure for generations.

We need to see permanently upgraded municipal electric grids. Dedicated AI institutes at local community colleges. Standardized apprenticeship programs that route local residents into high-paying technical careers. Sovereign compute resources reserved for regional universities and homegrown startups. Local venture funds backed by tech capital to help residents build businesses using the very systems their town is hosting.

In short: Leave something meaningful behind.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

None of this is philanthropy. It is an active investment in the social license to operate — the intangible asset upon which every transformational technology ultimately depends. Lose that public trust, and projects stall, local regulations multiply, zoning boards revolt, and expansion grinds to a halt. The AI industry is not immune to public backlash simply because its technology is extraordinary.

America will build astonishing AI systems over the next decade. I have zero doubt about our engineering capacity. The far more critical question is whether we will build a country that still believes those systems are working in its favor.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

History has a stubborn habit of answering that question long before the engineers finish training the next model.

World.title: Surging Dem with DSA ties is 'either a bona-fide socialist, or she's not very smart': GOP rep
World.content:

Florida Democratic Senate nominee Angie Nixon's denial that she is a socialist despite her membership in the Democratic Socialists of America should alarm voters as much as her surprise primary victory did, a lawmaker who fled Fidel Castro's Cuba told Fox News Digital.

Nixon, who upset Trump impeachment witness Alexander Vindman in last week's Democratic primary, told NBC News on Sunday that she is "not a socialist," despite acknowledging her DSA membership. She said she joined the far-left group because of its platform on public housing, healthcare, veterans and removing big money from politics.

"She's either a bona-fide socialist, or she's not very smart, because she ended up being a member of the Democratic Socialists of America," Rep. Carlos Gimenez, R-Fla., told Fox News Digital.

"I don't know what the heck she thought she was joining… Socialists [and] communists, deny what they are until they get into power," Gimenez said. He fled Castro’s Cuba as a child.

FLORIDA DEMOCRAT SENATE NOMINEE ANGIE NIXON INSISTS ‘I’M NOT A SOCIALIST’ AFTER JOINING DSA

Gimenez said he experienced that type of political pivot firsthand after Castro overthrew Fulgencio Batista in 1959.

Castro denied he was a Marxist and a communist early in the revolution but publicly acknowledged on Dec. 2, 1961 that he embraced Leninism and would do so forever, Gimenez recounted.

SOCIALISM WILL 'CONTROL PEOPLE' AND 'TAKE EVERYTHING AWAY' FROM AMERICA, ACCORDING TO THESE EXPATS

Gimenez argued that Nixon’s position, along with those of her DSA allies, "doesn’t sell" to the broader electorate.

"These socialists … are actually using democracy to destroy democracy," Gimenez said, pointing to Venezuela and Nicaragua as examples of movements that initially gained power through elections.

Gimenez said an early act of Venezuela’s Hugo Chavez was to pack the Supreme Court. He argued that socialist and communist regimes typically restructure government so the presidency answers to a single legislative chamber packed with apparatchiks.

"Sound familiar?" he said, drawing a comparison between that history and DSA proposals to abolish the Senate and restructure the Supreme Court.

NICARAGUA'S ORTEGA SAYS COUNTRY WILL 'NEVER AGAIN' HOLD ELECTIONS, SHUTTING OUT OPPOSITION

Gimenez pointed to Nicaraguan President Daniel Ortega's July announcement banning future elections after Ortega was democratically elected twice.

Ortega then "eliminated all pretexts of democracy" and plans to jail political opponents, Gimenez said, arguing that the development shows socialism as presented is "a pack of lies."

PROGRESSIVE FLORIDA LAWMAKER ANGIE NIXON TOPPLES TRUMP IMPEACHMENT WITNESS IN DEM SENATE PRIMARY UPSET

Gimenez predicted incumbent Sen. Ashley Moody, R-Fla., will "smoke" Nixon in November. He added that his district, which stretches from Miami to Key West and has a 70% Hispanic population that includes immigrants from Cuba and Venezuela, has "seen this movie before."

"We kind of look at each other and go ‘OK’. Unfortunately, across the nation, it is not the same," Gimenez said, pointing to New York City and Detroit and referencing the rise of Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Abdul El-Sayed.

Before Nixon’s comments, the DSA publicly celebrated what would have been Castro’s 100th birthday while attacking Secretary of State Marco Rubio for upholding the longstanding embargo and accusing him of hurting the Cuban people.

"They blame the embargo for everything," Gimenez said, adding that Rubio — the son of Cuban immigrants — is doing the right things. Gimenez said the embargo has never covered basic necessities such as food or medicine and argued that the only reason Cuba is broke is its leadership.

He noted Cuba used to be a global leader in sugar production but now imports cane.

"Why are they broke? Because they're incompetent. Why are incompetent? Because they are communists," Gimenez said, adding that the DSA is honoring a man who "incarcerated [his] entire island" so that no one can flee.

When socialists defend the Cuban healthcare system, Gimenez said his response is "the Cuban healthcare system... sucks," pointing to hospitals without supplies or medicines and a lack of public access to pharmaceuticals.

"It's okay to deny you all your basic rights as long as they give you healthcare? That's how screwy they are."

"I have seen socialism. I want no part of it. And hopefully the American people once they understand exactly what that brings and the price that you're going to pay because they lose your freedom, that they'll say we want no part of this."

World.title: Arizona grandpa to undergo amputation after collapsing on scorching sidewalk
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

An Arizona grandfather is preparing to undergo an above-knee amputation of his right leg after he tripped and fell while walking outside in Bullhead City during 120-degree heat earlier this month, according to his family.

Grant Siler, 72, fell during a walk on Aug. 3 in Bullhead City, causing his body temperature to rise to more than 105 degrees.

The family’s GoFundMe said Siler was on the ground for an estimated at least an hour before a passerby found him. The fundraiser said he suffered second and third-degree burns in multiple areas of his body, heat stroke and multiple organ shock.

HIKERS FACE URGENT GRAND CANYON HEAT WARNING AFTER TEEN’S DEATH ON POPULAR TRAIL

He was then taken to a burn ICU in Las Vegas, where he has been cared for since the incident. When he arrived at the facility, doctors discovered he was suffering from heat stroke and organ shock.

"He is in constant pain, can barely move, and has undergone two debridements. Also, he will soon need to undergo surgery for amputation, the extent is not yet known," the GoFundMe reads.

During surgery, a surgeon found that tissue in Siler’s right leg was so severely damaged it was unlikely to fully heal, according to an update posted to the fundraiser.

Siler is scheduled to have his right leg amputated above the knee on Aug. 31, according to FOX 10 Phoenix.

ESPN ANALYST MATT MILLER SAYS HE UNDERWENT LIFE-SAVING AMPUTATION OF LEFT ARM AFTER CAR ACCIDENT

"The plan now is to have an above-knee amputation. The Dr's feel he will overall heal faster and have better pain control this way," the fundraiser reads.

"We can all imagine that after any amputation, the road to recovery is long and hard...physically, mentally and emotionally," it continued.

His wife, Vicki, has been traveling one-and-a-half-hours each way to be with her husband as she continuing to work to support the family’s financial obligations. The family said the couple will also soon have to face medical bills to help with Siler’s recovery.

The family is accepting donations to help with home renovations, home medical supplies, prosthetics and other added costs.

Siler's daughter, Heather Crook, recalled an incident in which he dropped an 80-pound cinderblock on his foot but did not even take a Tylenol.

"He's hurting really bad," Crook told FOX 10. "He's the 'get up and walk it off' type."

"So for him to holler out in pain … it’s really hard to hear. That’s not the kind of person that he is," she added.

World.title: Lindsay Clancy trial: Postpartum is real, but child killing demands accountability, veteran prosecutor says

If you or someone you know is having thoughts of suicide, please contact the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline at 1-800-273-TALK (8255).

While failures by people, medical professionals and systems around Lindsay Clancy deserve scrutiny, nothing should erase a parent’s responsibility for killing a child, according to a veteran prosecutor who said he's concerned that public support for the Massachusetts mom is overshadowing the killing of her three young children.

Clancy is accused of killing her three young children — Cora, 5, Dawson, 3, and Callan, 8 months — and trying to end her own life by dropping from a second-floor window after sending her husband to pick up takeout and something from a pharmacy, according to the Plymouth County District Attorney's Office.

But as the case has drawn national attention, Clancy has also attracted supporters both online and in-person at the courthouse, and experts have warned that that support has taken attention away from the victims.

LINDSAY CLANCY'S THREE CHILD VICTIMS FORGOTTEN AMID CROWDS OF SUPPORT: MOTHER OF SIX

"Nobody who murders children is a victim no matter what they’re suffering through," said Jonathan Hatami, a veteran child abuse prosecutor. "You're never a victim if you murder people because victims don't do something. Something happens to them."

GOT A TIP?

The defense does not dispute that Clancy caused the deaths — but she has pleaded not guilty and is contesting criminal responsibility.

Hatami has spearheaded a number of high-profile cases against child abusers in Los Angeles, California, including the murder of 8-year-old Gabriel Fernandez, who was tortured and killed by his mother and her boyfriend. Gabriel's killing exposed a series of missed red flags by the county's Department of Children and Family Services and inspired a Netflix docuseries.

LINDSAY CLANCY DEFENSE SCORES ‘EXTREMELY HELPFUL’ PSYCHOSIS CONCESSION AS EXPERT FLAGS NEXT HURDLE

"Gabriel Fernandez was tortured and murdered by his mom and her boyfriend — however, there were a lot of other people...that were responsible," Hatami told Fox News Digital. There were a lot of people in government, in law enforcement, social workers, who missed all these different signs that really could have saved Gabriel — and they didn't do it. However, Pearl Fernandez and Isauro Aguirre were ultimately responsible for the torture and murder of Gabriel and were prosecuted for that and they were convicted of that."

LINDSAY CLANCY MURDER TRIAL BECOMES SOCIAL MEDIA OBSESSION AS TIKTOKERS, SLEUTHS DEBATE CONTROVERSIAL CASE

In Clancy’s case, he argued, many of the people and systems around her deserve scrutiny — but that should not turn her into the central victim of the story. In his view, she's been too much of the focus.

"Instead of about the three victims who were innocent kids," he said.

FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X

While failures of government and the child welfare system were investigated after Gabriel's murder, that didn't take responsibility away from the killers, he said. And in the Clancy case, he said he sees a risk that the focus on her mental health could eclipse the three children who were killed in their own home.

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS

"I didn't see people out in the streets cheering on Pearl Fernandez because there were other people that were somewhat responsible for what happened to Gabriel," he said. "And the same thing plays in this case. Lindsay admitted to strangling her three children to death. She admitted to strangling them to death with exercise cords."

LINDSAY CLANCY DESCRIBED A MALE VOICE ORDERING HER TO ‘KILL HER CHILDREN AND KILL HERSELF’: TESTIMONY

Clancy's defense has said she sought help repeatedly as she struggled with depression, sleeplessness, suicidal thoughts and voices urging her to harm herself and the children.

Defense attorney Kevin Reddington has argued that Clancy was under the effects of postpartum psychosis, while prosecutors allege she acted deliberately and understood what she was doing was wrong.

"If you murder your children, you need to be held accountable and responsible for that," Hatami said. "No matter what the whys are, no matter what reasons are."

SUSAN SMITH ELIGIBLE FOR PAROLE AGAIN AFTER BEING DENIED RELEASE FOR DROWNING HER 2 SONS IN 1994

If convicted of any of the three counts of first-degree murder she faces, Clancy would see a sentence of life in prison without the possibility of parole.
