World.title: Drniš Bypass Construction to Benefit Šibenik Port
World.content:
August the 24th, 2026 – The future Drniš bypass will greatly benefit the local economy, as well as Šibenik Port directly.

The construction of the second and third phases of the complex Drniš bypass project has begun, with the client being Hrvatske ceste (Croatian roads), and the contractor being the consortium of Texo Molior from Cavtat and CGP Slovenia.

Transport Minister Butković pointed out that after securing the financial structure and signing the contract, work on the project is now starting. Sinisa Malus reports for Poslovni that he also noted that it is a technically complex intervention with a route that includes two overpasses, two viaducts and a bridge over the Čikola River. Speaking about the continuation of activities on the future Šibenik–Drniš–Knin expressway, Minister Butković highlighted that the preparation of project documentation for the section from Drniš towards the Oklaj interchange is in an advanced stage.

a 34 million euro investment

After the design of that phase is completed, a tender is planned to be issued, so the project is being gradually prepared for phased implementation. He also referred to the reconstruction of state roads DC56 and DC33, which connect the Drniš area with Split and Knin respectively, and whose total reconstruction value is around 34 million euros. After the design of that phase is completed, a tender is planned to be issued, gradually preparing the project for implementation.

“A tender has already been issued for one, the other is in preparation, so there will be a great deal of investment in road infrastructure here in the area of the town of Drniš and Šibenik-Knin County,” added Minister Butković. Šibenik-Knin County Prefect Paško Rakić stressed that the Drniš bypass is of great importance for the entire county, especially for the traffic connection of its hinterland, and that residents of the wider Drniš and Knin areas will use it.

“The Šibenik–Drniš–Knin expressway, as well as this bypass, is the backbone of Šibenik-Knin County in terms of traffic, and it is as important to us as the Pelješac Bridge,” emphasised Prefect Rakić. “This is historic for us,” emphasised Drniš Mayor Tomislav Dželalija, noting that generations of Drniš residents have waited decades for this project.

a massive development boost for the area

Expressing satisfaction that the works were ceremonially started today, he pointed out that the removal of transit traffic, along with increased traffic safety, will create additional preconditions for the expansion of the economic zone and the further development of the town. He added that the Government of the Republic of Croatia, through strong investments including road and railway infrastructure, is giving impetus to the town’s development, and thanked them for the projects being implemented in the Drniš area.

President of the Management Board of Hrvatske ceste Ivica Budimir emphasised that the project has a broader economic significance for Drniš, especially because of the direct connection of the industrial zone with the Šibenik port.

“After this road is constructed, the industrial zone in the entire Drniš area will develop significantly faster, better and to a higher quality, and become much more competitive,” emphasised Budimir. Speaking about the technical demands of the project, he added that almost ten percent of the route consists of viaducts, while the most significant structure is the large bridge over the Čikola River canyon, with a span of 220 metres, along with a series of other structures along the route.

World.title: Baćina Lakes – Meet Croatia’s Freshwater Phenomenon
World.content:
August the 24th, 2026 – Baćina Lakes are Croatia’s freshwater phenomenon, with water warmer than that in the sea and the ability to swim year-round.

If you’ve ever driven from Makarska down toward Dubrovnik, you’ll have passed by them. You probably glanced left for a second, spotted a blue patch amid the greenery, and continued on toward the sea. Yet there, just a few kilometres from Ploče, lies something no other Croatian town has: seven lakes within the boundaries of a single town. They are called the Baćina Lakes and bear names that sound like a list from an old book: Oćuša, Crniševo, Podgora, Sladinac, Šipak, Plitko Lake, and Vrbnik.

Putni kofer writes that six of them are interconnected by narrow passages, so you can paddle or boat from one into another, while Vrbnik, which is also the smallest, is completely separate from the rest. Together they cover about 138 hectares.

they’re warmer than the sea

The Baćina Lakes form a cryptodepression, meaning their surface is only slightly above sea level, while their bottoms lie deep below it. Although they are just a step from the sea and surrounded by permeable limestone, the lakes are freshwater. Some springs are nevertheless directly connected to the sea, so salt water appears in the deeper layers. In the Klokun area near Plitko Lake there is a spring that supplies drinking water to the town of Ploče and the surrounding area.

During the scorching summer, the water in the lakes is noticeably warmer than the sea, with tourist sources citing a difference of roughly three degrees. Because of this, the swimming season here starts earlier and ends later than on the coast. The best-known bathing spots are those near the Mindel spring, and the hidden coves and small beaches are reached by kayak, paddleboard, or traditional Neretva boat.

links with queen teuta

Legend has it that the Illyrian Queen Teuta adored this area, and the lakes are still called Teuta’s pearls. Historians, however, have their own evidence and explanations. Near Sladinac Lake the remains of the Roman settlement of Praetoria have been found, along with the remains of an early Christian basilica from the 6th century and a necropolis of stećci tombstones.

Around the lakes a walking and cycling path about 15 kilometres long has been arranged, with benches, springs, and information boards. In 2020 the Public Institution for Protected Natural Areas of Dubrovnik-Neretva County installed 19 educational boards about dragonflies, amphibians, reptiles, and birds. Near the Oćuša spring there is a bird-watching hide, and the lakes also contain three small islets, one of which is named the Island of Love. The entire area forms part of the Natura 2000 ecological network, within two zones of the Neretva Delta, as a habitat for strictly protected and endemic species.

a worthwhile stop off on a long drive south…

A visit to the Baćina Lakes is truly an experience you will remember for a lifetime. Walking the paths that wind right beside the lakes will reveal scenes covered in water lilies, the reflection of clouds mirrored on the still water, and the song of rare birds that creates an almost meditative atmosphere.

Here you can also swim in crystal-clear water that provides refreshment during the great heat, and a special experience comes when the sun sets and the whole landscape is immersed in golden and pink tones. Then the lakes take on an almost fairy-tale appearance. It is a perfect moment for a photograph, but also for simply enjoying the silence of nature.

In the heart of the summer season, a parking space at the viewpoint along the main road is almost impossible to find. Down by the lakes themselves, however, there are usually no crowds. Most travellers photograph the view and drive on, while those who go down to the water, sit in a boat, or cycle a loop are completely enchanted and, like us, probably think: “How is this place not far better known?”

World.title: German GDP growth revised upwards, defying Iran war turmoil
World.content:
Frankfurt – German growth rose faster than previously estimated in the second quarter thanks to strong exports, official data showed Tuesday, as Europe’s biggest economy defied the turmoil unleashed by the Iran war.

Gross domestic product grew 0.3 percent from April to June compared with the first three months of the year, according to revised data from the statistics office Destatis.

A first estimate in July had put growth at 0.2 percent.

“The German economy is maintaining the growth momentum seen at the start of the year”, said Destatis’s chief Ruth Brand, adding that “growth was primarily driven by the positive development of exports”.

The economy expanded 0.4 percent in the first quarter.

The revision to second-quarter growth is another sign that the eurozone’s manufacturing powerhouse may be weathering the energy shock unleashed by the United States and Israel’s war against Iran better than feared.

Factory output and exports have also been ticking up in recent months despite the fallout from the conflict.

The revised GDP data showed that exports rose two percent in the second quarter from the first, while imports were also up substantially.

Investment fell slightly, dragged down by a hefty fall in the field of machinery and equipment. Spending by both households and governments registered a small increase.

The German economy has stagnated for several years due to high energy costs, growing competition from China and US President Donald Trump’s tariffs.

Hopes had been high at the start of the year that it would stage a strong rebound thanks to Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s spending blitz on defence and infrastructure.

The outbreak of the Middle East war has dimmed those expectations after the hit to energy-intensive manufacturers, with the government now expecting growth of just 0.5 for 2026 as a whole.

World.title: Hyundai reaches tentative deal with workers after strike
World.content:
Seoul – South Korean automaker Hyundai Motor and the union representing its workers have reached a tentative deal on wages and bonuses, both sides said on Tuesday after a rare full-day strike.

Around 40,000 employees of a roughly 73,000-strong domestic workforce at the country’s largest carmaker walked off the job on Friday, according to union figures, in the first such action for a decade.

The union said on Monday that it had returned to talks with the company and had postponed shorter strikes planned for this week.

Hyundai said on Tuesday that the two sides had struck a “tentative agreement”, while the union indicated that the firm had agreed to partly meet its demands.

“We agreed to increase the basic monthly salary by 100,000 won ($72) and pay a bonus equivalent to four months’ salary,” the union told AFP in a statement.

The company would also meet another demand to raise the retirement age once the government passes legislation on a nationwide hike from 60 years to 65.

Hyundai will not apply the wage peak system, which gradually reduces the salaries of older workers in their final years, after the retirement age is extended, the union said.

Union members will vote on the proposals on August 31.

“We acknowledge the commitment of our employees and appreciate the efforts of our negotiating teams in reaching this tentative agreement,” a Hyundai spokesman told AFP.

He also said both parties recognised that advanced technologies such as “physical AI and robotics are essential part” of the future of mobility.

The company’s workers have staged a total of 60 hours of strikes this year, causing estimated losses of around $1.6 billion, according to calculations by local news agency Newsis.

Hyundai posted record second-quarter revenue of 49.2 trillion won, although operating profit fell 20.8 percent year-on-year amid weaker sales.

World.title: Six months into Iran war, Hormuz traffic way down, sailors stranded
World.content:
Paris – Six months since the start of the Middle East war, the strategic Strait of Hormuz remains largely paralysed, with thousands of sailors still stranded in the Gulf and commodity carrier traffic way below its normal level.

– Only a few transits per day –

Before Iran blocked the strait in response to joint US-Israeli strikes in February, around one fifth of the world’s oil and liquefied natural gas exports passed through the waterway.

Iran’s Guards have also warned of a “danger zone” covering 1,400 square kilometres where mines may be present.

After Iran closed the strait on March 1, commodity carrier traffic plummeted to an average of 10 transits per day, compared with a daily average of 95 in February, according to an AFP analysis of data from maritime tracker Kpler.

An agreement signed by the United States and Iran in June led to a temporary rebound to 36 transits per day, before they dropped back to an average of 15 between the resumption of hostilities on July 8 and August 22.

– New routes, ‘dark’ transits –

Before the war, vessels crossed the strait freely via a route through the centre of the waterway adopted by the International Maritime Organization (IMO).

There are now two distinct routes: one to the north, near the Iranian coast — the only one approved by Tehran — and another to the south, between the Omani coast and potentially mined areas.

During the relatively calm period between June 17 and July 7, an average of nine ships per day used the Iranian route and eight the Omani one. The rest transited via unidentified routes or the traditional IMO corridor.

Ever since the ceasefire collapsed on July 8, two-thirds of transits have become “dark”, or unknown, compared with less than one percent before the war, according to Kpler.

These transits involve vessels whose exact route cannot be confirmed due to insufficient data stemming from disabled transponders, jammed signals or missing satellite imagery.

– Thousands of sailors stranded –

Some 6,000 sailors and 500 ships have remained stuck in the Gulf since the beginning of the conflict, the IMO told AFP.

The organisation said there were “ongoing discussions” to ensure a secure maritime route, adding that their outcome “depends on de-escalation in the region”.

The IMO had begun an initiative in June to evacuate more than 11,000 seafarers stuck in the Gulf, but the effort was soon suspended following an attack on a vessel.

Over the past six months, at least 20 sailors and dockworkers have been killed in incidents or attacks in the region, according to the IMO.

World.title: Stocks stagger and oil rises as traders eye Iran threat, Nvidia results
World.content:
Hong Kong – Asian stocks fluctuated Tuesday while oil edged up as investors assess a US plan for the “economic asphyxiation” of Iran, while tech firms struggled following another down day on Wall Street and ahead of earnings from chip titan Nvidia.

With the war against Tehran now in its sixth month, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the White House was declaring an “economic D-Day” on the Islamic republic and threatened to hit countries that trade with it.

The threat comes with talks to reopen the Strait of Hormuz stalled and neither side showing any sign of backing down — pushing oil prices up for most of August, which has in turn fanned long-term inflation fears and put pressure on bond markets.

“Around the globe, our objective is to sever every economic lifeline that sustains this tyrannical regime until Tehran stands alone,” Bessent told journalists Monday.

“We are going to hold everyone accountable, and this is economic asphyxiation of this regime,” he said, adding that countries not joining US sanctions would “share” in Iran’s isolation.

President Donald Trump was making phone calls to world leaders with requests to stop interactions with Tehran, Bessent said.

The Treasury Department said Iran’s digital assets, technology, gold, aviation and shipping sectors would be targeted for sanctions.

Both main contracts fell more than two percent Monday as Bessent’s comments appeared to suggest the US will hold off military action, but they ticked higher in early Asian trade.

His “increasingly aggressive economic campaign against Iran is designed to squeeze Tehran’s access to the global financial system while keeping the pressure economic rather than allowing the market to immediately price another military escalation”, wrote Stephen Innes, global strategist at Quintex Intel.

“For now, oil appears to have heard the message that way, which is doing Washington the considerable favour of taking some inflation pressure out of the system.”

Still, equities struggled as tech firms once again bore the brunt of selling, tracking a retreat in their counterparts on Wall Street.

Tech-rich Seoul sank more than two percent at one point as chipmakers SK hynix and Samsung retreated, while Hong Kong, Shanghai, Taipei and Manila were also off.

There were gains in Tokyo, Sydney, Singapore and Wellington.

The tepid performance comes ahead of much-anticipated earnings from Nvidia, which has become something of a bellwether for the AI boom.

With vast sums lavished on artificial intelligence investment over the past two years, markets are growing increasingly nervous about whether firms can deliver results to match.

And analysts have warned that even forecast-beating figures can sometimes not be enough.

Charu Chanana at Saxo Markets said: “Investors are not simply asking whether Nvidia can deliver another strong quarter. They are asking whether it can deliver enough upside to justify already-high expectations, especially with bond yields elevated.”

Eyes will also be on other tech names’ releases, including Salesforce and Marvell.

Also in focus is this week’s annual gathering of central bankers, economists and finance chiefs in Jackson Hole, Wyoming, where the Federal Reserve’s boss Kevin Warsh is due to speak.

His comments will be parsed for clues about monetary policy with inflation still stubbornly high and after Bessent said the Treasury would buy back more of its own bonds to push down borrowing costs after the 30-year yield surged to a 19-year high.

The Canadian dollar edged slightly higher after retreating against the US dollar Monday as Trump vowed to double tariffs on vehicles from its neighbour, fanning a trade war.

The US president’s threat comes after the two failed Friday to reach a deal to avert new 50-percent US tariffs on select Canadian goods. The duties took effect Saturday, and Ottawa laid out plans for retaliation.

World.title: Netanyahu got his Iran war, but maybe not his desired result
World.content:
Jerusalem – After decades of urging the United States to attack Iran, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu finally got his wish. But after six months of inconclusive hostilities, Israel may ultimately find itself in a worse position than it was before the war.

The Islamic republic, which Netanyahu has long cast as an existential threat, has not only survived but appears emboldened.

Underlying Netanyahu’s dilemma have been the wild swings in the approach of US President Donald Trump, who joined Israel in launching the conflict in late February, but by April abruptly called a ceasefire and sought a negotiated settlement in the face of souring public opinion and soaring oil prices.

“It’s a colossal failure of Israeli strategy regarding Iran,” said Danny Citrinowicz, a former top Israeli intelligence analyst on Iran who is now at the Tel Aviv-based Institute for National Security Studies.

“Yes, we had operational achievements, but strategically we’ve failed.”

Israel on the very first day killed Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, the supreme leader who ruthlessly suppressed dissent in Iran, including mass protests earlier this year, and backed virulently anti-Israeli groups like Hamas, which led the October 7, 2023 attacks.

But Khamenei was also seen as holding back on full-blown pursuit of nuclear weapons, a reluctance that could now end if the Islamic republic feels it has lost its conventional deterrents.

While Trump has recently declared economic warfare on Iran and periodically ordered new strikes, he has voiced support for a deal that would see sanctions relief.

Netanyahu had adamantly rejected a 2015 nuclear deal negotiated by then-president Barack Obama.

Citrinowicz said Israel now had a choice between accepting a new nuclear deal that would strengthen Iran, or trying to weaken it further and increasing the risk that it will seek a nuclear weapon.

“Israel is trying to do both but it’s not going to work,” he said.

– Degrading vs toppling –

An extraordinary 92 percent of Israelis believe Iran won or gained more from the conflict, according to a June survey by the Hebrew University of Jerusalem in collaboration with the Agam Institute — a warning sign for Netanyahu ahead of October 27 elections.

Netanyahu had said he was hoping to “create conditions for regime change” but did not explicitly make toppling the Islamic republic his goal.

Instead, some see Netanyahu following an Israeli playbook witnessed in Gaza, Lebanon and Syria — inflict overwhelming damage that will allow Israel to return and attack later as it sees fit, a strategy the country euphemistically calls “mowing the grass”.

“Netanyahu doesn’t see this as a loss. He has the United States directly at war with Iran, with Israel for now on the sidelines,” one foreign diplomat based in Israel told AFP on condition of anonymity.

Iranian counter-strikes killed 25 people in Israel and four in the occupied West Bank, but Iran has focused its fire more recently on Gulf Arab states that provide bases for US troops.

Alex Grinberg, a senior fellow focused on Iran at the Turan Research Center, said the war set back Iran significantly by eliminating infrastructure and people in the nuclear programme and imposing massive economic damage.

“I think Israel did achieve its strategic goals, meaning denying the Iranian regime the strategic capacity to threaten Israel,” he said, while casting doubt on the prospects for a favourable US-Iran deal.

– Risking public opinion –

The war has already complicated Israel’s relationship with its most crucial ally, and may preclude any possibility of a future reconciliation with the Iranian people.

The increasingly unpopular conflict triggered a surge of criticism of Israel in the United States, where its war against Hamas in Gaza had already dealt a heavy blow to its standing in the public eye.

Public perceptions of Israel inside Iran are difficult to gauge, as polling is difficult, but the two countries were allies before the Islamic revolution, and protests before the war indicated noticeable public opposition to the clerical government.

And while Netanyahu and Trump have both publicly professed to support the Iranian people, the US and Israel have issued apocalyptic threats over the course of the war that appeared to make little distinction between the Islamic republic and its citizens, and their strikes have destroyed infrastructure including top universities.

There is “a real possibility of lasting hostility towards Israel and the United States, particularly if the war is remembered through civilian casualties and damage to the country rather than solely through the removal of senior regime figures”, said Liora Hendelman-Baavur, a senior research fellow at the Alliance Center for Iranian Studies at Tel Aviv University.

“That hostility would not necessarily restore the Islamic republic’s legitimacy, but it could complicate future relations long after the present leadership has changed.”

World.title: Iraq, Qatar provide oil for loading inside Hormuz via bids
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Trade sources reported on Monday that Iraq’s national oil marketer, SOMO, and QatarEnergy are presenting crude oil through unusual bids that mandate purchasers to load cargoes within the Strait of Hormuz.

SOMO announced that it is offering Basrah Medium and Basrah Heavy crude for loading in September from either the Basrah oil port or a single point mooring, along with the necessary supporting facilities, as reported by Reuters.

QatarEnergy provided free-on-board oil loading at al-Shaheen, Qatar Marine, and Qatar Land ports in September and October.

Earlier, SOMO provided substantial discounts on Basrah crude in August to entice customers to load shipments from the Strait of Hormuz.

SOMO asked potential term purchasers to designate contractual volumes of Basrah Medium or Basrah Heavy crude for complimentary onboard delivery from the Basrah Oil Terminal or other port-related infrastructure.

Iraq’s oil marketer provided discounts ranging between $25 and $27 per barrel on Basrah Medium, according to the loading period. It provided discounts of $27.80 to $29.80 a barrel for Basrah Heavy.

Maritime traffic in the Strait of Hormuz decreased due to ongoing military operations in the region and heightened shipping security risks.

The significant price reduction aims to compensate for rising maritime insurance costs and freight expenses by transferring transit risk to purchasers.

World.title: Iraq to introduce new banknotes with three zeros removed
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq intends to remove three zeros from its currency to modernize financial transactions, reduce physical cash circulation, and return stockpiled funds to the official banking system.

Under the suggestion, a 25,000-Iraqi dinar note would become 25 Iraqi dinars, but the currency’s purchasing power and true financial value would stay unaffected.

According to Jamal Kocher, a Kurdish member of the Iraqi parliament’s finance committee, Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi has asked for the removal of zeros from invoices.

Kocher told The New Region that if the plan is implemented, 1,000 Iraqi dinars would be converted to one dinar, while 25,000 dinars would be equivalent to 25 dinars.

Earlier in August, Communications Minister Mustafa Sanad acknowledged the plan to eliminate the zeros and modify the currency.

The redenomination strategy aims to bring undeclared cash, estimated to be between 8 and 10 trillion Iraqi dinars that are currently held outside banks, back into official channels. This initiative seeks to combat crime, corruption, and money laundering.

According to the idea, everyday prices, incomes, and savings will alter correspondingly, resulting in a direct mathematical shift rather than a change in actual wealth.

Iraq has sought printing partners in the United Kingdom and Australia, as well as its traditional suppliers in France and Germany, to create an estimated 7.5 billion new banknotes.

While government officials such as the Communications Minister and Finance Committee members have emphasized the importance of an official implementation date, the Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) has yet to present a formal draft bill to parliament.

World.title: Iraq to raise oil exports via Turkey’s Ceyhan to 750,000 bpd
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Oil announced on Sunday a proposal to increase oil exports through the Turkish port of Ceyhan to 750,000 barrels per day by using tanker trucks to transport crude oil from southern oilfields.

The spokesperson for the Iraqi Oil Ministry, Salim al-Rikabi, told the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA) that the plan includes increasing exports through southern ports.

Iraq and Turkey recently inked a one-year short-term deal to continue operations through the critical Iraq-Turkey oil pipeline.

The agreement, reached in Ankara following discussions between Turkish Energy Minister Alparslan Bayraktar and Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair, guarantees the ongoing transportation of at least 750,000 barrels of Iraqi crude oil per day to the Turkish port of Ceyhan.

Turkey’s state-owned crude oil and natural gas pipeline corporation (BOTAS) signed an agreement with Iraq’s State Organization for Marketing of Oil (SOMO) and the North Oil Company (NOC).

The new deal is now valid for 12 months until both countries develop a new, long-term legislative framework.

The previous agreement, which was reached in 1973, officially expired on July 27.

The short extension of the deal is crucial for Iraq’s revenue from oil exports, as Baghdad seeks alternative export routes to mitigate risks linked to the Strait of Hormuz.

World.title: Sadhguru, Graphic India team up for animated film 'Shiva -The Adiyogi'

Sadhguru has announced a collaboration with Graphic India this Shravan to produce an animated feature film on Shiva as Adiyogi, described in the yogic tradition as the first yogi and the source of Yoga.

The film will draw on yogic lore narrated by Sadhguru and explore the origins of Yoga and the story of Shiva as Adiyogi through animation and cinematic storytelling. Graphic India co-founder Sharad Devarajan will serve as the filmâs producer, co-creator and writer.

World.title: Beyond Empowerment: Helping women to stay in work
World.content:
Women cannot participate fully in the economy if they carry a disproportionate share of unpaid care work.

Women continue to shoulder a far greater share of unpaid domestic and caregiving work than men, a gap that affects labour-force participation and is increasingly being addressed through childcare, livelihood and inclusion-focused CSR initiatives.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

For years, CSR programmes aimed at women have focused on familiar themes such as scholarships, skill training, self-help groups and entrepreneurship. But a more fundamental barrier is increasingly coming into focus: women cannot participate fully in the economy if they carry a disproportionate share of unpaid care work.Indiaâs 2024 Time Use Survey found that 81.5% of women aged six and above participated in unpaid domestic services on a given day, compared with 27.1% of men. Women who participated spent an average of 289 minutes a day on such work, against 88 minutes for men. The gap is also visible in unpaid caregiving, where 34% of women participated compared with 17.9% of men.The economic consequences are clear. Indiaâs female labour force participation rate was 40% in 2025, compared with 79.1% for men. Among women outside the labour force, 44.4% cited childcare or commitments in homemaking as their main reason.This is changing how the private sector can think about inclusion. Instead of asking only how to train or employ more women, CSR programmes can address issues that prevent them from entering and staying in paid work.Childcare is an obvious starting point. The govtâs Palna scheme provides day-care facilities for children aged six months to six years, including early stimulation, pre-school education, nutrition and health services.By March 2025, 11,395 Anganwadi-cumcreches were approved across states and UTs, although only 1,761 were operational.This gap creates space for corporate and civil society partnerships. Vedantaâs Nand Ghar initiative is one example. Mobile Creches offers another model, combining childcare with support for children from marginalised communities.The significance of such programmes is that childcare need not be viewed simply as a welfare service. It can be economic infrastructure. If reliable childcare frees up womenâs time, the next question is whether that time translates into income, assets and greater economic agency.This is where CSR-backed livelihood programmes can connect with care interventions. Mann Deshi Foundation, for example, reports having supported more than 1 million women, with 9 lakh reached through its womenâs business schools since 2012.Its 2024-25 data shows that 94% of trained women reported an increase in monthly average income, with the average rise at 56%, while 76% gained ownership of assets. Its Rural Chamber of Commerce for Women reports reaching 1.3 lakh women for financial linkages, with average monthly income rising from Rs 4,300 to Rs 15,296 afterwards.The lesson for CSR is important. Training women without looking at constraints on their time, access to finance and ability to reach markets can produce limited gains. A more complete intervention connects childcare and care services with skilling, credit, entrepreneurship, market access and asset ownership.The same principle applies to disability inclusion. CSR-led organisations are increasingly helping move disability programmes from charity towards employment and economic participation. Other CSR and civil society partnerships address livelihood barriers among vulnerable groups.What emerges is a broader understanding of inclusion. Women cannot be empowered simply by giving them a training certificate. A person with a disability cannot be included simply by providing an assistive device. A migrant worker cannot be protected merely by registration on a government portal. Effective social investment must address the barriers between a person and economic participation: care, mobility, documentation, accessibility, skills, credit and employment. For CSR, that represents a shift from funding individual interventions to building pathways. The opportunity is significant.

World.title: From 10% to 100%: Aviation ministry weighs annual dope tests for all pilots
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The aviation ministry is considering mandating dope tests for all pilots at least once a year, civil aviation minister Ram Mohan Naidu Kinjarapu said on Tuesday.

The current rules require dope testing of 10 per cent of the overall pilot network, but the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) is examining whether testing can be expanded to cover every pilot at a random time during the year.

âThere are multiple ways of approaching this dope test. Right now, the rule says 10% across the overall pilot network. DGCA is engaging, and one of the opinions from our side is that everyone has to go through it in the year at a random time,â Naidu told reporters.

The minister added the government would need to balance aviation safety with the operational impact of implementing 100 per cent testing.

âWe have to see how all the stakeholders are going to respond to this because one is the safety aspect of it, and the second thing is the operational impact, which also has to be taken into consideration,â he said.

Meanwhile, addressing the recent Delhi-Phuket flight incident, Naidu said the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) is investigating the incident and a preliminary report is expected soon.

The minister said the flight data recorder and the aircraft are intact and in the possession of the investigating agency, which would help in the probe.

âAAIB is presently taking up the investigation. Because everything is intact, the flight data recorder and everything is intact, and the plane is also in their possession, I believe that we can expect a preliminary report very early from now,â he said.





Naidu also said the DGCA is holding consultations with stakeholders on existing regulations concerning substance use and ways to strengthen the policy.

âMore importantly, in terms of substance use and everything, DGCA is also having stakeholder consultations right now on what the regulation says today and how we ensure there is a strict policy around this in the future as well. So, this consultation is going on right now,â he said.

The AAIB is examining the circumstances surrounding the incident, while the DGCA consultations are focused on reviewing existing regulations and strengthening safeguards related to substance use in aviation.

The development comes after Air India flight AI2379, operating from Phuket to Delhi on August 4, experienced a sudden 300-foot altitude drop over Odisha, leaving 20 passengers and four cabin crew members injured.

World.title: SEBI’s ITRI — a global test for India’s future-ready financial architecture | Explained
World.content:
The story so far: Market regulator Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has introduced a technology health scorecard for market infrastructure institutions (MIIs) to measure the robustness of their critical IT systems rather than merely checking routine compliance.

SEBI’s IT Resilience Index (ITRI) appears to be among the first attempts globally by a regulator to design a quantitative resilience barometer, as measurable as capital adequacy for banks, for MIIs such as stock exchanges, clearing corporations and depositories.

Why SEBI is introducing the IT Risk Index (ITRI) for capital markets?

The move to assess MII vulnerabilities comes in view of the rising technological dependence of Indian capital markets, where even a few minutes of disruption can affect millions of investors and billions of rupees in trades.

The ITRI will gauge whether the IT systems supporting trading, clearing, settlement and securities holding are capable of handling operational shocks, cyber threats, technical failures and sudden spikes in market activity.

The foundation for the proposed index was laid in 2015, when SEBI, through a circular, termed MIIs as “systemically important”, thus calling for a “robust” cybersecurity framework to perform systemically critical functions.

How will the ITRI work and measure market technology risk?

The need for ITRI comes at a time when India’s securities market is experiencing sea changes in digital transformation, as seen from increased participation of retail investors through online platforms, higher algorithmic trading volumes and faster settlement cycles. Market efficiency has now become inseparable from technology reliability, making it a boardroom issue.

The proposed index, which seeks to shift from a pure compliance-based mode to a quantitative risk-monitoring framework, will be based on nine parameters, each weighted on the basis of a systemic-risk hierarchy, even as questions remain on the statistical estimation of the proposed weights, which have been assigned after discussions with its Technical Advisory Committee. The Industry Standards Forum of MIIs would further define the detailed sub-parameters and measurement criteria.

The weighting exercise implies a risk-prioritisation approach, giving greater importance to parameters whose failure can immediately disrupt the functioning of MIIs.

Availability and security have been accorded the highest weight, at 20% each, as they represent the first line of defence for a financial market’s functioning.

The 10% weightage on Business Continuity and Reliability reflects a change in regulatory perspective. The focus was earlier on preventing failures, but over time, resilience frameworks have focused on absorbing shocks and recovering quickly.

Scalability has been assigned a 5% weight amid SEBI’s view that Indian markets are growing rapidly but do not pose an immediate stability risk.

The present weights should, at best, be seen as a starting framework because the market regulator may have to refine them using actual outage data, cyber incidents and stress tests.

MIIs would also develop an Early Warning System (EWS) to detect any deterioration in ITRI parameters that could potentially lead to performance issues, system slowness or other disruptions, and take remedial measures.

How does SEBI’s ITRI compare to global regulatory standards?

Several markets have created similar operational resilience frameworks, though not always in the form of a single ITRI.

The U.K.’s Financial Conduct Authority and Prudential Regulation Authority have put in place operational resilience rules requiring financial institutions to identify important business services, set disruption tolerances and demonstrate their ability to recover from severe operational shocks.

Unlike SEBI’s proposed index, the European Union’s most comprehensive Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) is a regulatory rulebook rather than a numerical scorecard.

The U.S. does not have a single ITRI for bourses. Instead, technology resilience is embedded into regulatory oversight.

Singapore’s Monetary Authority of Singapore has one of Asia’s strongest technology risk guidelines, which could be particularly relevant for India since both countries have highly digital financial ecosystems and a large retail presence.

Hong Kong’s regulators have developed cyber resilience assessment frameworks for financial institutions and market intermediaries, closer to SEBI’s strategy as it uses measurable maturity levels, and regulators rely on comprehensive operational resilience frameworks and cross-sectoral exercises rather than a numeric scoring index.

Australia follows a resilience-based approach through regulators such as the Australian Securities and Investments Commission and the Australian Prudential Regulation Authority, but its focus areas are critical operations mapping, technology dependencies, outsourcing risks and cyber recovery.

How is ITRI different?

Most regulators worldwide follow a principle-based operational resilience model, but SEBI’s distinctive model attempts to convert resilience into a measurable index.

With India’s capital markets becoming among the most technology-intensive globally, a failure at an exchange or clearing corporation level is not just an IT problem but a financial stability risk. The EWS identifies weaknesses before they become failures.

With increasing dependence on AI (artificial intelligence), cloud infrastructure, high-frequency trading and digital settlement, technology risks would become more complex. SEBI has already initiated discussions on a long-term technology roadmap for MIIs covering areas such as AI, cloud computing, distributed ledger technology and quantum-safe systems.

SEBI has already constituted a working group to formulate a short-term and long-term technology roadmap for MIIs, taking a holistic view on the adoption of emerging technologies including AI/machine learning, Suptech, RegTech and tokenisation.

What are the key implementation challenges facing the ITRI?

The biggest challenge before SEBI is the pace of technological change because technology risks evolve faster than regulatory frameworks.

Questions may arise on a common index when stock exchanges, clearing corporations and depositories have different technology architectures and functions.

Cybersecurity remains unpredictable because institutions with sophisticated systems have suffered global cyber incidents.

Moreover, substantial investments are needed to build automated monitoring systems, conduct continuous testing and maintain redundant infrastructure.

Can the ITRI secure the future of India’s capital markets?

SEBI’s ITRI is a global assessment of India’s ability to build a future-ready financial market architecture. The real test will be whether a high score translates into faster recovery in the event of an actual cyberattack, system outage or technology shock.

If implemented effectively, it could become a global template to safeguard the digital foundations of finance.

World.title: Integrating Mangaluru with SWR: Capt. Chowta urges Karnataka CM to throw his weight behind Railway’s decision
World.content:
As the Karnataka government remains mute over the Railway Ministry’s decision to bring Mangaluru Railway Region under South Western Railway (SWR) and the Keralam government led by Congress’ V.D. Satheesan vehemently opposes the move, Dakshina Kannada MP Captain Brijesh Chowta has urged Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar to throw his weight behind the decision favouring the State.

“This is not about taking a position against a neighbouring State. It is about placing Karnataka’s considered position on the railway administration and developmental requirements of Mangaluru formally before the Union Government. I believe the people of Karnataka can reasonably expect our State Government to stand behind this long-pending demand and support its implementation,” he said in an August 24 letter to Mr. Shivakumar.

Capt. Chowta said the August 21 notification of the Railway Ministry bringing Mangaluru under SWR’s Mysuru Division from Southern Railway’s Palakkad Division was the culmination of people’s aspirations from the region ever since SWR was formed in 2023. The changes are made keeping in view the operational requirements of the railway network.

Important for Karnataka

The MP said the revised arrangement is important for Karnataka as a whole. Mysuru Division already administers the Hassan-Mangaluru section, which provides the principal rail connection between the coast and the interior of the State. Bringing Mangaluru within the same divisional framework will allow the coastal terminal, the ghat section and the inland corridor towards Hassan and Mysuru to be planned and administered in a more integrated manner.

Maritime gateway

Mangaluru is also Karnataka’s principal maritime gateway. The New Mangalore Port serves the industrial and commercial hinterland of the State and depends substantially on rail connectivity for movement of cargo. The revised arrangement, therefore, gives Karnataka an opportunity to approach the Mangaluru-Hassan-Mysuru axis as an integrated passenger and freight corridor connecting the coast and the port with the interior of the State.

Capt. Chowta recalled his efforts in pursuing the integration issue with the Centre after getting elected to the Lok Sabha.

While Mr. Satheesan is learnt to have approached the Prime Minister against the bifurcation, Keralam MPs cutting across party lines too have opposed the decision.

Recalling Mr. Shivakumar’s first meeting with Karnataka MPs after assuming the office, that one must rise above party differences on matters concerning Karnataka, Capt. Chowta urged the former to apply the same principle to the Mangaluru Railway issue too.

While leaders and MPs from Keralam belonging to Congress have taken a clear public stand seeking reversal of the decision, it would be difficult for Karnataka people to understand why their government is keeping silent on a formally notified decision directly concerning Karnataka.

He urged Mr. Shivakumar to convey to the Union government Karnataka’s support for implementing the August 21 decision.

World.title: 14 years and counting: Arippa in Keralam awaits electricity
World.content:
As Keralam stares at a potential crisis in the power sector stemming from inadequate power generation caused by a deficient monsoon, the newly formed UDF government is under fire for undeclared power outages during peak consumption hours.

But there is a group of people in the State forced to live in perpetual darkness.

Shrouded beneath the damp, emerald canopy of the Kulathupuzha forest range in Kollam district, Arippa unfolds as a landscape of quiet defiance. This is where the pristine wilderness of the Western Ghats gives way to a fragile tapestry of weathered blue-tarpaulin hutments built on contested land.

In Arippa, the struggle continues for over 250 families who have been living without an electricity connection for the past 14 years. The occupants received land title deeds right before the State elections in April-May this year, but have been caught in administrative limbo between the Forest and Revenue departments.

Though the title deeds were handed over, the landowners are unable to obtain possession certificates from the village office, with authorities citing a previous objection from the Forest Department. The ongoing dispute between the Forest and Revenue departments has prevented residents from applying for any utility services, including power and water connections.

The entire process of handing over the land was conducted by the Revenue Department in a hasty manner without completing the necessary formalities, alleges Rameshan, one of the leaders of the Adivasi Dalit Munnetta Samithi (ADMS), which has led the land struggle since 2012. In effect, the hardships of the residents of Arippa have persisted even after the formal land struggle ended.

This has forced the families to rely entirely on diesel-powered lanterns for their power requirements.

Nisha, a resident of Arippa who used to travel 60 km every day to work as security staff at a private firm in Thiruvananthapuram Technopark, has remained at the settlement for the past four months, fearing her title deed would be cancelled if she was found absent during a possible inspection by officials. Like Nisha, other young residents depend on a grocery store in a nearby village to charge their mobile phones, paying ₹5 to10 daily.

Minister for Forests and Wildlife Shibu Baby John recently said the Forest Department would not stake any further claim on the assigned land.

“An in-principle agreement has been reached within the government to protect the interests of the landless families,” the minister said. He attributed the ongoing dispute to procedural lapses during the land distribution drive undertaken by the previous administration in the run-up to the Assembly elections. “The crisis stems from allotment procedures carried out without completing the requisite statutory formalities. The present government is committed to resolving the issue amicably,” he added.

Outlining a concrete timeline for redressal, the minister assured that the entire issue would be resolved within six months. He said he would visit Arippa in the coming days to interact with residents, assess the ground situation, and hear their grievances directly before taking final corrective measures.

Residents and leading activists, including Sreeraman Koyyon, State president of the Adivasi Dalit Munnetta Samithi (ADMS), expressed hope over the outcome of the recent ministerial meeting between the Forest and Revenue departments. Even as the Edamon-Kochi high-tension electricity transmission line passes through the Kulathupuzha forest range, the shanties right below remain engulfed in darkness, presenting a stark picture of neglect and social exclusion.

World.title: The bygone movie theatres of Chennai: a compilation
World.content:
As Chennai city celebrates the 387th anniversary of its founding this year (as Madras Day), The Hindu looks back at the city’s iconic cinema halls that reveal a rich tapestry of cultural history and changing urban landscapes. Long before the era of modern multiplexes and malls, single screens and theatre complexes served as the vibrant heartbeat of movie buffs in the city.

From the legendary Udhayam Theatre Complex in Ashok Nagar—hailed as the ultimate “collection king” and a premier first-day-first-show destination—to the architectural marvels of Safire Theatre on Mount Road that once defined the city’s cosmopolitan pulse, these spaces shaped generations of memories.

Though many of these historic landmarks including the Pilot Theatre at Royapettah and National Theatre at Virugambakkam have since given way to commercial/residential real estate and high-rises, revisiting their legacy offers a nostalgic and poignant glimpse into the golden age of moviegoing in Madras, reminding residents of the enduring cultural roots underlying Chennai’s rapid metropolitan transformation.

Their stories also mirror the city’s own transformation: neighbourhoods grew, audiences changed, technology altered the business of exhibition, and old cinema spaces gradually disappeared or were repurposed.

World.title: Romance, longing, life, and cinema on Chennai’s beaches
World.content:
Filmmakers have always used certain symbols, motifs, and signifiers to represent ideas, concepts, and places. Over the many years, popular city landmarks, including the hotel Taj Mahal Palace in Mumbai and the Cubbon Park in Bengaluru, have been used as establishing shots to depict the city in which a film is set. For Chennai, it has always been a toss-up between Marina/Elliot’s Beach, Central Station, Anna Flyover, Spencer Plaza, and LIC Building.

While one could argue that the LIC Building established the “big city” vibe and that Spencer Plaza represented Chennai’s “modern and capitalist” aspects, the beach has always been used to represent love and life.

Remember the song, Enna Paarvai, Undhan Paarvai, from Kadhalikka Neramillai, a popular 1960s film that many, swear to be the unmatched “evergreen romantic” comedy. The song showcases a young couple — Muthuraman and Kanchana — shaking a leg to a melodious song at the beach, unrecognisable with manicured lawns and the absence of cars.

Similarly, in Mani Ratnam’s Alaipayuthey, staying true to the perception of the beach as a sanctuary for those in love, the lead-in to the song, Snehithane, shows the hero waiting for the heroine at the beach.

The iconic Ilaiyaraaja song Idhu Oru Pon Malai Pozhudhu from the film Nizhalgal showcases the beach as a place where college students go to smoke weed after bunking classes and build grandiose dreams about their future.

Beach and sport

Filmmaker Venkat Prabhu’s debut film, Chennai 600028, captured another aspect of the beach — its popularity as a space for playing sports, until the police began imposing restrictions. While the Gen Z crowd may not be aware, the black tar road on the beach used to be where hundreds of tennis ball cricket matches took place in the evenings, while the fiercely contested football and volleyball games happened on the beach sands. The final “match” with the school kids at the beach reflected its popularity as a space for playing sports, until the police began imposing restrictions.

Filmmaker Vetrimaaran’s Vada Chennai portrayed the lives of those who live near the coast and depend on the Kasimedu Fishing Harbour for their livelihood. While the film itself is about Chennai’s underworld, it focuses on the trials and tribulations of those living near the beach through various points in recent history. Not just the beach, but its people, their politics and economic conditions were the focus of the critically-acclaimed film.

In actor Sivakarthikeyan’s Marina, the beach becomes a place of refuge for those running away from home.

In a way, the Marina, the Elliots Beach, and the sandy beaches along the East Coast Road evoke different perceptions. While the Marina has maintained its position as the city’s major landmark for tourists, the Elliots’ Beach and those further down the East Coast Road have slowly transformed themselves to attract the hip and fashionable youngsters of Chennai.

With the city growing at a rapid pace, there may be more “landmarks” or cultural markers that the filmmakers will be interested in, but one thing is for sure, the beaches in Chennai will continue to fascinate the storytellers for many years to come.

World.title: Sanskrit varsity Syndicate revokes decision on unsigned exam tabulation registers, orders probe into lapses
World.content:
The Syndicate of the Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit (SSUS) in Keralam has cancelled its July 17, 2026 decision to permit officials in the examination wing, who were found not to have signed the tabulation registers of exams held long back, to complete the mandatory process.

A special Syndicate meeting convened by Vice-Chancellor Ciza Thomas on August 22, 2026 resolved to annul the earlier decision and entrusted the Syndicate sub-committee on Examinations to conduct a probe into the discrepancies.

The committee will check whether there were differences in the entries made in the tabulation register and the final mark list awarded to the students, according to senior varsity officials.

A preliminary assessment by the authorities found that the officials had not recorded their signatures in exams held since 2018. Those who had put their signatures on the tabulation register following the Syndicate decision on July 17 included those who had retired from service.

Only a detailed probe will ascertain whether such a lapse had occurred before 2018, they said.

The matter was included as item no. 31 in the minutes of the Syndicate meeting. It stated that the Syndicate resolved to entrust section officers of three sections in the examination wing to inform officials in the category of Assistant to Deputy Registrars, who have not signed in the tabulation registers, to record it.

The initial assessment found that the erring officials were asked to record their signatures on the tabulation registers even before an official order was issued, confirming the Syndicate decision taken on July 17. A former senior official of the exam wing confirmed that there had been instances in the past where signatures were not recorded in the tabulation registers and attributed it to the gaps in the system.

Petition before Governor

The Save University Campaign Committee (SUCC) has urged Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar to initiate a judicial probe into allegations of irregularities in the examination wing.

In a petition submitted to the Governor, who is also the Chancellor of State universities, the committee alleged that it is a serious lapse on the part of the officials concerned for not recording their signatures on the tabulation register. Permitting retired officials to record their signatures on official documents amounted to violation of the rules and regulations of the university, it said in a communication.

World.title: NSA Doval, Wang Yi hold border talks in Beijing
World.content:
National Security Advisor Ajit Doval on Tuesday (August 25, 2026) met with Wang Yi, Foreign Minister of China, for the 25th Round of the Special Representatives (SR) talks in Beijing.

Mr. Doval and Mr. Wang are the designated SRs for the boundary talks mechanism, which was established in 2003 to comprehensively address the dispute of the India-China border spanning 3,488 km.

Ahead of the talks, Mr. Doval called on Han Zheng, Vice-President of the People’s Republic of China, during which they discussed “ways to strengthen peace and tranquility in the border areas”.

Mr. Han was quoted by the Xinhua news agency as saying: “China and India should view and handle bilateral relations from a strategic and long-term perspective, and work together to implement the important consensus reached by their leaders.”

“The two sides should enhance strategic mutual trust, tap the potential for cooperation, maintain close multilateral coordination, properly manage differences, and promote the sustained and stable development of China-India relations,” he said.

Mr. Doval said that as the world’s two most populous and fastest-growing major economies, India and China have a “historic opportunity” for cooperation, adding that India stands ready to work with China to deepen mutually beneficial cooperation, properly address the boundary question and make new progress in bilateral relations.

In a post on X, the Indian Embassy in Beijing said that the “NSA and VP Han discussed ways to strengthen peace & tranquility in the border areas and further improve bilateral relations across economic, political and multilateral fora, in accordance with the consensus reached between the leaders of the two countries.”

Mr. Doval’s visit comes ahead of next month’s expected trip to India by Chinese President Xi Jinping for the September 12 BRICS Summit, and provides both sides the opportunity to take stock of the relationship.

Ties have gradually normalised following the October 2024 meeting between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Mr. Xi in Kazan, Russia.

(With inputs from PTI)

World.title: How to check your name in Telangana SIR Draft Electoral Rolls-2026? A step-by-step guide
World.content:
Telangana’s draft electoral rolls-2026 were published on August 17, 2026, after conducting enumeration phase as part of Special Intensive Revision (SIR) in the State. People can check online if their name is included in the draft electoral rolls.

Step-by-step guide

The link to access the draft rolls was made available on the website of Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) - Telangana (ceotelangana.nic.in).

Click on the tab ‘Special Intensive Revision (SIR) Draft Electoral Rolls-2026’, which leads to a page where people will be asked to select district, Assembly Constituency and language. Thereafter, the draft rolls according to part number and part name will be displayed. After selecting it and entering captcha, people can download the draft rolls.

The draft rolls will have details of the elector’s names, EPIC number, relative’s name, age and gender. Photos are not displayed in the online draft rolls. It also has images of polling stations, google map view.

How to know part number and part name?

Voters wondered how they could know the part number and part name to select the draft rolls to check for their name. Some people sent SMS to the phone number ‘1950’, with the message ‘ECI <EPIC number>’. In response, they received a message including the elector’s name, serial number, part number, Assembly constituency name and number, district and State.

ASDD list

A few days after publishing the draft rolls-2026, the list of electors categorized as Absent, Shifted, Dead and Duplicate (ASDD) too was made available on the CEO’s website. To check the list of people whose names were not included in the draft rolls of 2026, people have to select district, Assembly constituency and part number. Or, they can check by entering their EPIC number.

However, the online ASDD list is available only in Telugu. People have urged the CEO to make the list available in other languages as well. The details were mentioned in English when checked against EPIC number.

Number of electors in Telangana SIR draft rolls and ASDD list

There were 3,38,26,448 electors in the State as on August 10, 2026. As per the information from the CEO’s office, electors as on August 17, 2026, were 2,64,87,213 including 60,50,918 electors in ‘Anomalies’ category and 32,36,659 voters in ‘No Mapping’ category. And, 73,39,235 people were in ASDD list including 9,22,229 voters categorised as ‘Dead’; 11,25,546 as untraceable or absent; 45,18,963 as permanently shifted and 1,02,294 as ‘others’.

Key dates

The CEO on August 24, 2026, directed District Election Officers (DEO), Electoral Registration Officers (ERO) and AEROs to hold grama/ward-level meetings and read out names of voters in ASDD list and draft voters list.

They were also directed to expedite the process of issuing notices to voters in Anomalies and No Mapping categories. Hearing venue, date and time have to be clearly mentioned in the notices.

World.title: Imran's hospital transfer: PTI resubmits contempt plea after SC raises objections
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The PTI on Tuesday resubmitted a contempt of court petition by PTI founder Imran Khan’s sister to the Supreme Court (SC) against the alleged violation of its August 18 order for the ex-premier’s transfer to a private hospital.

The development came shortly after the SC had returned the plea after raising certain objections.

PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan said that the SC registrar had informed him that the petition was being returned, with one of the objections being that the list of charges levelled against the respondents had not been dispatched. He had also said that the PTI was going to resubmit the petition after removing the objections raised.

Last week, Imran’s sister Uzma Khan had filed a petition before the SC against authorities for violating the court’s Aug 18 order. In its order, the court had ordered the government to shift Imran to Shifa International Hospital, a private facility, within two days for examination and treatment by a multidisciplinary medical board.

However, the government instead took the PTI founder to Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims), a government hospital, for a check-up and then subsequently transported back to prison. At the time, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar had blamed “the security situation created by PTI workers on the way to and outside” the hospital for the diversion.

In her petition, Uzma — who was present for the check-up — had named Islamabad Chief Commissioner (retired) Lieutenant Sohail Ashraf, Interior Secretary Ahmed Raza Sarwar, Punjab Inspector General Prisons Mian Salik Jalal, Adiala Jail Superintendent Sajid Baig, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar and Information Minister Attaullah Tarar as respondents.

She had alleged that the respondents had committed wilful, deliberate and contumacious disobedience and violation of the order. She had also requested the apex court to depute an officer or appoint a local commission to ensure that Imran was immediately shifted to the private hospital in accordance with its earlier directions.

At the same time, the Islamabad chief commissioner had also approached the SC, seeking an early hearing of his review petition, in which the legality of the Aug 18 order was questioned.

On Monday, Gohar had met the SC registrar and was assured that a bench would be constituted soon to proceed with the contempt of court petition.

Responding to a question, he had also brushed aside the impression of any deal with the government, saying that the PTI founder did not make deals, otherwise he would not have spent three years in prison.

World.title: 'The matter is being viewed positively': Official says Bangladesh interested in joining Makkah defence pact
World.content:
Bangladesh has expressed interest in participating in the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye, a top diplomat said Monday.

“We have expressed our interest in the Makkah Defence pact […] Bangladesh is now a country of recognition. The partners in West Asia (Middle East), the partners in the Muslim world around the globe are now inviting the leadership of Bangladesh, especially the leadership of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, to be with them in many places,” said Humayun Kabir, who was appointed as state minister for foreign affairs last week.

“If there is one [agreement] in West Asia, if there is a security agreement between Islamic countries, then it is not unusual to go there. Let’s see. The matter is being viewed positively,” said Kabir, who previously served as an adviser to Rahman.

Pakistan, Turkiye and Saudi Arabia signed the joint defence agreement at a trilateral summit in Makkah on August 7, pledging to strengthen collective security, deepen defence cooperation and promote peace and stability in the region and beyond.

The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement was signed by Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif during the summit held at Al-Safa Palace.

World.title: Amid distrust, Tehran wants US to initiate de-escalation
World.content:
Pakistan’s Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Asim Munir exchanges views with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian during their meeting in Tehran.—Reuters

• CDF Munir holds meetings with Pezeshkian, Ghalibaf and Rezaei

• Iranian leaders stress commitment to Islamabad MoU; say Washington’s approach hindering regional stability, eroding trust in US

• Discussions focused on preventing further escalation, reopening of Hormuz, swift end to conflict, ISPR says

• Oman FM due in Tehran today for next round of talks on Hormuz

ISLAMABAD: The United States must take the first steps towards de-escalation by fulfilling its commitments under the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding (MoU), Iran conveyed to Pakistan on Monday, as the latter sought to revive the diplomatic process for ending the US-Iran conflict.

The message was conveyed during Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir’s meetings in Tehran; with Iranian President Dr Masoud Pezeshkian, chief negotiator and Parliament Speaker Bagher Ghalibaf, and Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council Gen Mohsen Rezaei, as he sounded out Tehran on the possibility of reviving the June understanding.

“We are committed to implementing the terms of the Memorandum of Understanding. It is the United States that must adhere to its commitments based on the agreement,” Ghalibaf told Field Marshal Munir, according to an Iranian account of their meeting.

This sentiment was echoed by Gen Rezaei in his meeting with Field Marshal Munir, who was quoted by IRNA as saying: “We distrust America and it must change its behaviour”.

Field Marshal Munir said Pakistan would continue its efforts to help restore stability in the region, Press TV reported.

According to Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi accompanied the army chief during the one-day visit, which also included meetings with Iranian Interior Minister Eskandar Momeni and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi.

“Comprehensive discussions focused on measures to prevent further escalation, reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and expedited termination of the conflict. The two sides also exchanged views on regional peace and the ways to arrive at a negotiated settlement to the disputes,” ISPR said.

The Iranian leadership appreciated Pakistan’s constructive role and sincere efforts towards facilitating dialogue, de-escalation and a peaceful resolution of the conflict, the statement noted.

The field marshal’s visit comes as the two warring sides have returned to hostilities following the expiry of the 60-day armistice brokered under the Islamabad MoU.

Pakistan has, however, continued to regard the agreement as the available framework for a return to dialogue, while Iran has insisted that Washington must first address what Tehran considers breaches of the understanding.

The visit assumes added significance because Field Marshal Munir spoke by telephone with US President Donald Trump last week, before travelling to Tehran. The contents of that conversation have not been made public, but the contact provided Islamabad with a direct channel to carry the US position to Tehran, while seeking to assess whether Iran was prepared to re-engage.

The army chief’s trip began just before Washington announced a fresh economic pressure campaign against Iran, with sanctions and restrictions on Iranian oil exports likely to form a major part of the new measures.

Tehran has warned that further US pressure would deepen the confrontation rather than create conditions for negotiations.

Ghalibaf described Washington’s approach as “hinder[ing] regional stability and further erod[ing] trust in Washington”.

“Americans know that no one buys their bombast, the United States is not in an economic position to further restrict its relations with other countries,” he said in a post on X after meeting Field Marshal Munir.

The Strait of Hormuz remains central to the impasse. Iran has been insisting that US first fulfil its commitments relating to the waterway, before it considers a wider reopening and a return to the next phase of negotiations.

Field Marshal Munir’s meeting with Gen Rezaei was particularly significant because the Iranian general has recently taken over as secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, placing him at the centre of Tehran’s national security decision making at this critical stage in its confrontation with Washington.

During their conversation, Rezaei particularly emphasised Iran’s security interests in the Strait of Hormuz and the need for any settlement to address the military and economic pressures imposed on Tehran.

The issue of Strait of Hormuz is meanwhile being discussed in a separate diplomatic track in the shape of Iran-Oman talks on arrangements for navigation in the strait.

Omani Foreign Minister Badr Al Busaidi is due in Tehran on Tuesday, adding to the diplomatic activity surrounding the strait at a time when Pakistan is seeking to regain its role in the wider US-Iran process.

Published in Dawn, August 25th, 2026

World.title: Body of US climber who died in Broad Peak avalanche airlifted from base camp
World.content:
GILGIT: The body of US climber Sarah Mallory Geis was airlifted from the Broad Peak base camp on Tuesday after the recovery operation was paused due to continued bad weather.

Geis died in a deadly avalanche that[ killed](https://Body of US climber who died in Broad Peak avalanche airlifted from base camp) a 10-member expedition last month. Her body was recovered by three local porters voluntarily from Broad Peak (8,047m) on Friday, 22 days after she went missing in the avalanche. Local volunteers have moved the body to Broad Peak basecamp.

General Secretary Alpine Club of Pakistan Ayaz Shigri confirmed to Dawn that the body of the US climber was airlifted to Skardu through Pakistan Army helicopters. The body was received by ACP officials, district administration, police and medical officials at a helipad in Skardu.

Shigri said the body had been shifted to the Combined Military Hospital (CMH) Skardu and would be sent to Islamabad after completion of relevant legal procedures.

Earlier, Shigri had told Dawn that the search for the tenth deceased member, Nawang Thindu Sherpa, was underway.

The avalanche struck on July 30, cutting off contact with the international expedition led by world-renowned British-Nepali mountaineer Nirmal Purja on Broad Peak, one of the world’s highest mountains. Purja’s company later confirmed there were no survivors.

Broad Peak is the world’s 12th highest mountain, located in the Karakoram range, and is regarded as one of the toughest and most technical climbs of all the 8,000-metre-plus ascents.

Mission to retrieve Asma Mushtaq’s body from Spatnik resumes

Meanwhile, a rescue team resumed its trek at Spantik on Tuesday to recover the body of Pakistani mountaineer Dr Asma Mushtaq, who died while descending the 7,027m peak in Gilgit-Baltistan’s Shigar district.

The 34-year-old died on Aug 20 while descending from the mountain also known as Golden Peak, after suffering from high-altitude sickness. Her body remains at Camp 3, which is located at a height of approximately 6,250 metres.

Efforts to retrieve her body were earlier disrupted due to severe weather.

ACP’s Shigri told Dawn on Monday that weather conditions were expected to improve on Tuesday, after which the rescue team, comprising six high-altitude porters, would make another attempt to bring Mushtaq’s body down to the base camp.

Subsequently, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar posted on X that the rescue team had resumed its operation after weather conditions improved.

“The rescue team has once again departed from the base camp and is now heading towards Camp 2. The team is moving carefully and will continue the operation as conditions permit. We pray for their safety and success,” he said.

Shigri had told Dawn that Pakistan Army helicopters were expected to airlift Mushtaq’s body to Skardu after its arrival at the base camp.

During her ascent, Mushtaq had successfully reached the 7,027-metre summit of Spantik and was in good health at the time, ACP said in statements issued on Thursday.

However, she developed a serious high-altitude medical emergency at an elevation of about 6,400 metres during the descent.

High-altitude sickness encompasses a range of pulmonary and cerebral conditions caused by hypoxia, or oxygen deprivation, due to rapid ascent and inadequate acclimatisation to high altitudes.

Her mountain guide, Akbar Ali, and expedition guide, Muhammad Amin, immediately came to her assistance.

“Despite the immediate and dedicated efforts of her mountain guides, who provided every possible ass­i­s­tance under extre­mely challenging conditions, she could not survive,” Karrar Haidri, a senior vice president for ACP, said in a condolence statement.

Shigri had said Mushtaq was part of a five-member Pakistani women’s expedition team that summited Spantik, which included climbers Zoni Aslam, Zaba Shigri, Shama and Sohana.

Climate change-induced shifts in weather patterns have worsened conditions on the peaks of the Karakoram Range in GB, creating serious difficulties for mountaineers.

Additional input from Jamil Nagri

World.title: Bitcoin rises above $80,000 as soft dollar, debasement fears boost momentum
World.content:
Bitcoin rose above $80,000 to hit a more than three-month high on Tuesday as a soft US dollar, in the wake of the moves by Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent to calm the bond market, revived momentum in the crypto sector.

US President Donald Trump last week called on Congress to pass a bill that would bring clearer definitions to the growing cryptocurrency sector. Since then, bitcoin, the world’s largest cryptocurrency, has risen 16 per cent.

It was last at $80,323.24 in Asian hours, having earlier touched $81,237.94, its highest level since mid-May. Bitcoin is up 28pc so far in August, set for its biggest monthly gain since November 2024.

Cryptocurrencies also got a big boost after the US Treasury last week unveiled plans to buy back more long-dated bonds to help cap the gains in the long-end yields, a move that has led to the US dollar bearing the brunt of investor angst.

Tim Sun, senior researcher at HashKey Group, said Bessent’s messaging has reinforced the market’s view that, at least through the midterm elections, US policymakers may have a lower tolerance for a further rise in long-end yields.

“That would create a relatively supportive macro backdrop for assets such as bitcoin and gold,” Sun said.

Gold has been the other beneficiary of the dollar weakness, rising to a three-month high.

The Treasury announcement is “exactly the type of thing bitcoin loves”, Geoff Kendrick, global head of digital assets research at Standard Chartered, said in a note last week, adding that bitcoin was built to allow investors a way to avoid this type of intervention.

The action stoked increased chatter around the so-called debasement trade, where the moves to prevent long-end yields from reaching market-clearing levels via buybacks lead the pressure to shift from the bond market to the currency market.

“This (Treasury announcement) prompted buyers to scramble into physical and digital assets as debasement trade fears re-emerged,” said Tony Sycamore, market analyst at IG.

“A sustained break above here would open the door for a move towards $95,000 and $100,000.”

World.title: 3 more Adiala inmates seek private care
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: At least three inma­tes of Adiala jail have approached the Isla­mabad High Court seeking treatment at private hospitals and greater access to their families, following the Supreme Court’s recent order directing authorities to shift former prime minister Imran Khan to a private hospital for medical examination and treatment.

The petitions before the IHC vindicate the government’s concern that the SC order in Imran Khan’s case could set a precedent for other prisoners to seek similar relief.

The federal government, in its review petition before the Supreme Court, had argued that allowing a convict to receive treatment at a private hospital could disturb the existing prison system and trigger a “floodgate” of similar applications from other prisoners.

The issue is now before the IHC, where Justice Muhammad Asif sought comments from the jail superintendent on petitions filed by prisoners Ilyas Khan, Muhammad Ismail Khan and Owais Altaf. The court also issued noti­ces to prison authorities, and adjourned proceedings until Aug 27.

During the hearing, Barrister Akhtar Chheena, representing Ismail Khan, said his client was suffering from haemophilia and had developed internal bleeding. He submitted that the prisoner had been taken to hospital around 10 times in the last two months, but his condition had not improved.

According to the counsel, treatment for the particular condition was presently possible only at Shifa Interna­tio­nal Hospital. He relied upon the SC’s recent ruling and argued that where a disease could not be treated at a government hospital, a prisoner could be shifted to a private facility, with the family bearing the cost of treatment.

The counsel requested the court to constitute a medical board to determine whether the required treatment was available at a government hospital.
